 * The detail of a `warm` event line (spec 27 P2.3.8): the draws of a pipeline warm-up run.
 * Structural.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const warm: WarmDetail = { draws: 18 };
 * ```
 */
export type WarmDetail = { draws: number };

/**
 * The detail of the editor's own `devtools` event line (addendum 3B/4 item 1): the overlay window's
 * mode and tab. The recorder writes it; perf ignores it.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const devtools: DevtoolsDetail = { mode: "card", tab: "frames" };
 * ```
 */
export type DevtoolsDetail = { mode: "hidden" | "pill" | "card"; tab: string };

/**
 * Kept pictures of the last drawn frame (spec 23 P12.1): pictures drawn as one texture, the MB their
 * textures hold, and retakes in the last full second. Structural.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const kept: KeptStats = { pictures: 1, mb: 1.4, retakes: 0 };
 * ```
 */
export type KeptStats = { pictures: number; mb: number; retakes: number };

/**
 * The members of the engine's `RenderStats` perf reads (11 R12.2, addendum 3B/4 item 3):
 * `renderPasses` is the engine's; `renderPassesMax` and `kept` (spec 23) and `redraws` /
 * `rebuilds` (spec 26, dev or agent builds only) are not in the engine yet.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const stats: RenderStatsLike = { renderPasses: 3, renderPassesMax: 3, kept: { pictures: 1, mb: 1.4, retakes: 0 }, redraws: 0, rebuilds: 0 };
 * ```
 */
export type RenderStatsLike = Pick<Renderer.RenderStats, "renderPasses"> & {
  renderPassesMax: number;
  kept: KeptStats;
  redraws?: number;
  rebuilds?: number;
};

/**
 * The engine's performance monitor as the editor uses it: `app.renderer.monitor` of an agent build
 * (11-monitor R13.1, 11:1153-1158; the engine's `Renderer.PerfMonitorApi`). Structural, because
 * the editor's event names include `pool-trim` and `warm`; the engine's monitor is assignable to it
 * (`engine-contract.test.ts`). In a build without the agent flag every member exists and does
 * nothing: `frames()` answers a ring of capacity 0, `stream` never calls.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // perf finds it on the game it wraps.
 * const monitor: MonitorLike | undefined = monitorOf(registry.game());
 * monitor?.frames().capacity; // 1024 on a debug build of the phone
 * ```
 */
export type MonitorLike = {
  /**
   * 11:1291-1314. The header (and startup) at once, then samples, spikes, long frames, events,
   * marks, thermal; each line fresh and deeply frozen.
   *
   * @param listener - Called with each line.
   * @returns The unsubscribe.
   */
  stream(listener: (line: PerfLogLine) => void): () => void;
  /**
   * 11:1317-1334. The same ring object on every call.
   *
   * @returns The frame ring.
   */
  frames(): FrameRing;
  /**
   * 11:1337-1349. A mark line, `auto: false`.
   *
   * @param label - The mark's label.
   */
  mark(label: string): void;
  /**
   * 11:1352-1369. An event line at the frame it happens in.
   *
   * @param name - The event name.
   * @param detail - The event detail.
   */
  event(name: PerfEventName, detail?: Readonly<Record<string, Json>>): void;
  /**
   * 11:1372-1394. Opens a span of agent work (a nested begin is ignored).
   */
  beginAgent(): void;
  /**
   * 11:1372-1394. Closes the span (an end without a begin is ignored); the engine also hands it to
   * `time.chargeAgent`.
   */
  endAgent(): void;
  /**
   * 11:1399-1418. The A/B resolution switch; the editor does not call it.
   *
   * @param resolution - The resolution, or undefined for the default.
   * @returns The resolution now.
   */
  setResolution(resolution: number | undefined): number;
};
~~~

#### `causes.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * The engine's cause bits, in PerfCause order (11:816, 11:1009): index = bit.
 */
export const CAUSE_BITS: readonly PerfCause[] = [
  "gap",
  "js",
  "gpu",
  "compile",
  "upload",
  "longFrame",
  "gc?"
];

/**
 * Primary cause codes, by the editor's rank (R11 answer 11): 1 gpu, 2 upload, 3 compile, 4 longFrame,
 * 5 js, 6 gc?, 7 gap; 0 = not a spike. A lower code wins. A long frame names its scripts, so it
 * outranks plain JS; gc? is a hint, so only gap ranks below it.
 */
export const CAUSE_RANK: readonly PerfCause[] = [
  "gpu",
  "upload",
  "compile",
  "longFrame",
  "js",
  "gc?",
  "gap"
];

/**
 * The primary cause code of a frame's cause bits. Allocation-free: a loop over the bit masks in
 * rank order.
 *
 * @param bits - The `causes` column value.
 * @returns 1..7 by CAUSE_RANK, 0 when no bit is set.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * primaryCause(0b0010010); // 2: upload beats js
 * ```
 */
export function primaryCause(bits: number): number;

/**
 * The cause names of a frame, primary first, then by rank. Allocates: for records, not the read loop.
 *
 * @param bits - The `causes` column value.
 * @returns The names; [] for a frame that is not a spike.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * causesOf(0b0100010); // ["longFrame", "js"]
 * ```
 */
export function causesOf(bits: number): PerfCause[];

/**
 * The name of a primary cause code.
 *
 * @param code - 1..7.
 * @returns The PerfCause; undefined for 0 or out of range.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * causeName(6); // "gc?"
 * ```
 */
export function causeName(code: number): PerfCause | undefined;

/**
 * The change names of a frame's `changed` bits, in PerfChange order.
 *
 * @param bits - The `changed` column value.
 * @returns The names; [] when nothing changed.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * changesOf(0b01000); // ["bundle"]
 * ```
 */
export function changesOf(bits: number): PerfChange[];
~~~

#### `rate.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * Frames per second of one frame of a rate: `Math.round(1000 / rateMs)`.
 *
 * @param rateMs - One frame of the rate, ms (the ring's `rateMs` column).
 * @returns The fps; 0 for a value that is not a finite number above 0 (a ring before `rateMs`, NaN).
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * rateFps(8.33); // 120
 * ```
 */
export function rateFps(rateMs: number): number;
~~~

#### `text.ts`

~~~ts
/** The longest text `cleanText` keeps by default, in characters. */
export const CLEAN_TEXT_MAX = 128;

/**
 * A phone's text, safe to print: control characters (C0, DEL, C1) and bidi embeddings, overrides
 * and isolates dropped, then at most `max` characters (code points, so a character is never cut in
 * half).
 *
 * @param text - The text as the phone sent it.
 * @param max - The most characters kept (128 by default).
 * @returns The clean text.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * cleanText("garden\u001b[2J‮/boss"); // "garden[2J/boss"
 * ```
 */
export function cleanText(text: string, max: number = CLEAN_TEXT_MAX): string;
~~~

#### `values.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * Why perf has no monitor: a headless game (no renderer), or an engine before block 2b.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const reason: PerfOffReason = "no-renderer"; // a headless test game
 * ```
 */
export type PerfOffReason = "no-renderer" | "no-monitor";

/**
 * What perf can measure now. "waiting": the monitor exists but its ring is empty (capacity 0: the
 * agent flag is off, or the renderer has not attached yet).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.perf.status(); // { state: "on", lost: 0, gpuTimer: true } on the phone
 * ```
 */
export type PerfStatus =
  | { readonly state: "on"; readonly lost: number; readonly gpuTimer: boolean }
  | { readonly state: "waiting" }
  | { readonly state: "off"; readonly reason: PerfOffReason };

/**
 * The loop's frame rate as perf knows it: `fps` from the newest row's `rateMs`; `mode`, `reason`,
 * `displayHz` from the newest `rate` event (`RateChange`), else from the header's `rate`
 * (`FrameRate`, spec 21), else null (an engine before spec 21).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const rate: PerfRate = { fps: 120, mode: "auto", reason: "start", displayHz: 120, switches: 0 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfRate = {
  /** Frames per second of the newest row (`rateFps(rateMs)`); null while the window is empty. */
  readonly fps: number | null;
  readonly mode: RateMode | null;
  readonly reason: RateReason | null;
  readonly displayHz: number | null;
  /** Rate switches inside the window (rows whose `rateMs` differs from the row before). */
  readonly switches: number;
};

/**
 * What perf reads from `renderer.stats()` (11 R12.2, addendum 3B/4 item 3; 23 P12.1; 26 R2.3.3). A
 * key the engine does not answer is null (an engine before spec 23 has no `kept`; a production
 * build has no `redraws`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // The memory screen at rest on a debug build, its lamps kept.
 * const render: PerfRenderStats = { passesMax: 1, kept: { pictures: 4, mb: 1.6, retakes: 0 }, redraws: 0, rebuilds: 0 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfRenderStats = {
  /** `stats().renderPassesMax`. */
  readonly passesMax: number | null;
  /** `stats().kept`: pictures drawn as one texture, the MB they hold, retakes in the last second. */
  readonly kept: KeptStats | null;
  /** `stats().redraws`: the engine's Graphics redraws in the last second (dev and agent builds). */
  readonly redraws: number | null;
  /** `stats().rebuilds`: Pixi's instruction rebuilds in the last second (dev and agent builds). */
  readonly rebuilds: number | null;
};

/**
 * The pill, the header and the counters: the window's fps and spike count, and the newest sample
 * and screen facts as the engine sent them.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const second: PerfSecond = { state: "on", fps: { loop: 60, drawn: 54 }, spikes: 6, budgetMs: 16.67,
 *   rate: { fps: 60, mode: "auto", reason: "missed", displayHz: 120, switches: 1 },
 *   render: { passesMax: 3, kept: { pictures: 1, mb: 1.4, retakes: 0 }, redraws: 0, rebuilds: 0 },
 *   sample: null, display: null, device: null, gpu: null, build: "debug-20261014T160000Z", engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0" };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfSecond = {
  readonly state: PerfStatus["state"];
  /** Frames of the last 1000 ms of the window: run by the loop, drawn by the renderer. */
  readonly fps: { readonly loop: number; readonly drawn: number };
  /** Spikes in the window (the one-window rule, design §4). */
  readonly spikes: number;
  /** The newest frame's own budget (its `budgetMs` column); 16.7 while the window is empty. */
  readonly budgetMs: number;
  /** The loop's rate now and who decides it (counters, device row). */
  readonly rate: PerfRate;
  /** `renderer.stats()` read when this value was built; null when the renderer has no `stats` or it threw. */
  readonly render: PerfRenderStats | null;
  /** The newest `sample` line, as the engine sent it; null before the first. */
  readonly sample: PerfSampleLine | null;
  /** header.display, replaced by every `display` event. */
  readonly display: PerfDisplay | null;
  /** header.device. */
  readonly device: PerfHeaderLine["device"] | null;
  /** header.gpu. */
  readonly gpu: PerfHeaderLine["gpu"] | null;
  /** header.build: spec 10's build id. */
  readonly build: string | null;
  /** header.engine: spec 10's engine fingerprint. */
  readonly engine: string | null;
};

/**
 * A frame event of the game that a spike record lists under "what changed": a game overlay changing
 * (`label` + `what`), a pool trim (MB freed) or a warm-up run (draws).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const opened: PerfFrameEvent = { kind: "overlay", frame: 4812, label: "shopDimLayer", what: "open", mode: "freeze" };
 * const trim: PerfFrameEvent = { kind: "pool-trim", frame: 4811, reason: "rest", freedMb: 41.5 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfFrameEvent =
  | {
      readonly kind: "overlay";
      readonly frame: number;
      readonly label: string;
      readonly what: OverlayWhat;
      readonly mode: string;
    }
  | {
      readonly kind: "pool-trim";
      readonly frame: number;
      readonly reason: PoolTrimDetail["reason"];
      readonly freedMb: number;
    }
  | { readonly kind: "warm"; readonly frame: number; readonly draws: number };

/**
 * One spike of the window, for lists and MCP.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const spike: PerfSpikeSummary = { frame: 4812, agoMs: 980, ms: 41.3, budgetMs: 16.7, overMs: 24.6, cause: "upload",
 *   causes: ["upload", "gap"], jsMs: 8, gpuMs: 6.6, path: "garden/boss", why: "41.0 MB of textures uploaded this frame (bundle garden-boss)" };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfSpikeSummary = {
  readonly frame: number;
  /** ms before the newest frame of the window. */
  readonly agoMs: number;
  readonly ms: number;
  /** The frame's own budget: its `budgetMs` column, the budget the engine's spike rule used for it. */
  readonly budgetMs: number;
  /** ms − budgetMs. */
  readonly overMs: number;
  /** The primary cause by CAUSE_RANK. */
  readonly cause: PerfCause;
  /** Every cause, primary first. */
  readonly causes: readonly PerfCause[];
  readonly jsMs: number;
  readonly gpuMs: number | null;
  /** The flow path of the frame (ring.paths). */
  readonly path: string;
  /** One sentence: why this frame was late. */
  readonly why: string;
};

/**
 * The spike record (design §7): the summary plus the frame's numbers and, once the engine's spike
 * line arrived (about one flush later), its full detail.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.perf.spike(4812)?.rateSwitch; // { from: 120, to: 60, reason: "missed", mode: "auto" }
 * ```
 */
export type PerfSpikeRecord = PerfSpikeSummary & {
  /** Epoch ms of the frame's start (header.timeOrigin + t); null before a header. */
  readonly at: number | null;
  /** The frame's rate in fps (`rateFps(rateMs)`). */
  readonly fps: number;
  /** The rate switch at this frame; `reason` and `mode` from its `rate` event (null when only the rows show it). */
  readonly rateSwitch: {
    readonly from: number;
    readonly to: number;
    readonly reason: RateReason | null;
    readonly mode: RateMode | null;
  } | null;
  readonly gapMs: number | null;
  readonly drawn: boolean;
  /** The GPU time may still change. */
  readonly gpuPartial: boolean;
  /** Phase ms in PHASES order plus agent; null when the ring slot was overwritten and no spike line came. */
  readonly phases: {
    readonly input: number;
    readonly animate: number;
    readonly layout: number;
    readonly sync: number;
    readonly signals: number;
    readonly render: number;
    readonly agent: number;
  } | null;
  readonly passes: number | null;
  readonly draws: number | null;
  readonly filters: { readonly applies: number; readonly mpx: number } | null;
  readonly uploads: { readonly count: number; readonly mb: number } | null;
  readonly compiles: number | null;
  readonly changed: readonly PerfChange[];
  /** The game's frame events of this frame (and the `pool-trim` lines of the frame before), in arrival order. */
  readonly events: readonly PerfFrameEvent[];
  /** The engine's spike line; null until it arrives. */
  readonly detail: PerfSpikeLine | null;
};
~~~

#### `window.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * The last `windowMs` of frames as struct-of-arrays, oldest row first: what the frame graph draws.
 * perf owns one, rewrites it at every read and hands it out only for the length of a `readWindow`
 * call, as the read-only `PerfWindowView` (never keep the reference; copy what you keep); a tools
 * page fills its own from the wire with `readWireWindow`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.perf.readWindow(window => {
 *   window.count; // 358 at 60 fps
 *   window.budgetMs[window.count - 1]; // 16.67
 * });
 * ```
 */
export type PerfWindow = {
  /** Rows the arrays hold. */
  readonly capacity: number;
  /** Rows in use, oldest first. */
  count: number;
  /** Page-clock ms of the left edge of the time axis: endMs − windowMs. */
  startMs: number;
  /** Page-clock ms of the right edge: start of the newest frame plus its frame time. */
  endMs: number;
  /** False when the page has no GPU timer (header.gpu.timer null, WebKit): the graph stacks JS and idle only. */
  gpuTimer: boolean;
  /** Increments whenever any row or scalar changed, so a painter skips an unchanged window. */
  version: number;
  /** The frame number of each row. */
  readonly frame: Uint32Array;
  /** Page-clock ms of each frame's start. */
  readonly t: Float64Array;
  /** Frame time: max(gap, js + gpu). */
  readonly ms: Float32Array;
  /** The game's work: workMs − agentMs, at least 0. */
  readonly jsMs: Float32Array;
  /** GPU ms; NaN = not measured (yet). */
  readonly gpuMs: Float32Array;
  /** One frame of the frame's rate, ms (ring column `rateMs`); a change from one row to the next is a rate switch. */
  readonly rateMs: Float32Array;
  /** The frame's own spike budget, ms (ring column `budgetMs`): the budget the engine's spike rule used for it. */
  readonly budgetMs: Float32Array;
  /** 1 when the renderer drew the frame. */
  readonly drawn: Uint8Array;
  /** The engine's cause bits (CAUSE_BITS). */
  readonly causes: Uint8Array;
  /** The primary cause code (CAUSE_RANK), 0 = not a spike. */
  readonly cause: Uint8Array;
  /** Rows of the spikes, oldest first. */
  readonly spikes: Uint16Array;
  /** Spikes in `spikes`. */
  spikeCount: number;
};

/**
 * The window as a reader sees it: every scalar `readonly` and every column a read-only
 * `ArrayLike<number>` (a typed array is assignable to it), so a visitor cannot write a row or a
 * scalar without a cast. No copy is made; typed arrays cannot be frozen, so the guard is the type.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.perf.readWindow(window => {
 *   window.ms[window.count - 1]; // 41.3
 *   // window.ms[0] = 0; — a type error: the index signature only permits reading
 * });
 * ```
 */
export type PerfWindowView = {
  readonly capacity: number;
  readonly count: number;
  readonly startMs: number;
  readonly endMs: number;
  readonly gpuTimer: boolean;
  readonly version: number;
  readonly frame: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly t: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly ms: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly jsMs: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly gpuMs: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly rateMs: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly budgetMs: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly drawn: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly causes: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly cause: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly spikes: ArrayLike<number>;
  readonly spikeCount: number;
};

/**
 * The wire form of a window (source `editor.perf.window`). Columns are plain arrays, so the value
 * is Json.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const wire: PerfWindowWire = { v: 1, startMs: 40123.5, endMs: 46123.5, gpuTimer: true, frame: [4811, 4812],
 *   t: [5917.4, 5958.7], ms: [16.7, 41.3], jsMs: [3.4, 8], gpuMs: [5.2, 6.6], rateMs: [16.67, 16.67],
 *   budgetMs: [16.67, 16.67], drawn: [1, 1], causes: [0, 17] }; // 17 = gap + upload: primary upload
 * ```
 */
export type PerfWindowWire = {
  v: 1;
  startMs: number;
  endMs: number;
  gpuTimer: boolean;
  frame: number[];
  /** ms after startMs. */
  t: number[];
  ms: number[];
  jsMs: number[];
  gpuMs: (number | null)[];
  rateMs: number[];
  /** The frame's own spike budget (ring column `budgetMs`). */
  budgetMs: number[];
  drawn: (0 | 1)[];
  causes: number[];
};

/**
 * Allocates a window of `capacity` rows: every array once, `count` 0, `gpuTimer` true, `version` 0.
 *
 * @param capacity - Rows, a whole number from 1 to 65535.
 * @returns The empty window.
 * @throws {TypeError} For a capacity that is not a whole number from 1 to 65535.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createPerfWindow(1024).capacity; // 1024
 * ```
 */
export function createPerfWindow(capacity: number): PerfWindow;

/**
 * The row of a frame number (binary search: frames grow along the rows).
 *
 * @param window - The window.
 * @param frame - A frame number.
 * @returns The row; −1 when the frame is not in the window.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * rowOfFrame(window, 4812); // 357 when 4812 is the newest of 358 rows
 * ```
 */
export function rowOfFrame(window: PerfWindowView, frame: number): number;

/**
 * The next (1) or previous (−1) spike row after (before) `row`, wrapping around; from a row that is
 * not a spike, the first spike after / the last before it.
 *
 * @param window - The window.
 * @param row - The row to step from.
 * @param dir - 1 for next, −1 for previous.
 * @returns The spike row; −1 when the window has no spike.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * stepSpike(window, 300, 1); // 12: past the newest spike (row 290), wrapped to the oldest
 * ```
 */
export function stepSpike(window: PerfWindowView, row: number, dir: 1 | -1): number;

/**
 * The 1-based position of a row among the spikes: the "5/6" counter is `spikeOrdinal` / `spikeCount`.
 *
 * @param window - The window.
 * @param row - A row.
 * @returns The position; 0 when the row is not a spike.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * spikeOrdinal(window, 290); // 5 when row 290 is the fifth spike
 * ```
 */
export function spikeOrdinal(window: PerfWindowView, row: number): number;

/**
 * The mean of the measured `gpuMs` of the drawn rows: the "GPU avg" counter of the overlay and the
 * tools strip. An indexed loop, no allocation.
 *
 * @param window - The window.
 * @returns The mean; null when no drawn row has a measured GPU time (WebKit has no GPU timer).
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * meanGpu(window); // 6.1
 * ```
 */
export function meanGpu(window: PerfWindowView): number | null;

/**
 * The wire value of a window (source `editor.perf.window`). Allocates: `t` as ms after `startMs`
 * rounded to 0.1, ms values (`rateMs` and `budgetMs` included) to 0.01, a `NaN` GPU time as `null`.
 *
 * @param window - The window.
 * @returns The wire value.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * writeWireWindow(window).budgetMs; // [16.67, 16.67]
 * ```
 */
export function writeWireWindow(window: PerfWindowView): PerfWindowWire;

/**
 * Fills `into` from a wire value: false and `into` untouched for a value of another shape (see
 * `checkedWire`); keeps the newest `into.capacity` rows; drops the cause bits the editor does not
 * know; recomputes `cause` and `spikes` with `primaryCause`; `version += 1`.
 *
 * @param value - The value of `editor.perf.window`.
 * @param into - The window to fill.
 * @returns Whether the value was a window.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * readWireWindow({ v: 2 }, window); // false: window unchanged
 * ```
 */
export function readWireWindow(value: Json, into: PerfWindow): boolean;
~~~

#### `guards.ts`

~~~ts
/**
 * The engine's performance monitor of a game: `game.renderer.monitor` when it has `stream`,
 * `frames`, `mark`, `event`, `beginAgent` and `endAgent` as functions. Never throws.
 *
 * @param game - The game app (any value).
 * @returns The monitor, or undefined.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * monitorOf({ time: {}, flow: {} }); // undefined: a headless game has no renderer
 * ```
 */
export function monitorOf(game: unknown): MonitorLike | undefined;

/**
 * Why a game has no monitor perf can use.
 *
 * @param game - The game app (any value).
 * @returns "no-renderer" without a renderer object, "no-monitor" with one but no usable monitor,
 *   undefined when a monitor exists.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * offReasonOf({ renderer: {} }); // "no-monitor": an engine before block 2b
 * ```
 */
export function offReasonOf(game: unknown): PerfOffReason | undefined;

/**
 * Whether a value has the shape of a `PerfDisplay` (11:960-964).
 *
 * @param value - The detail of a `display` event.
 * @returns Whether it is a display.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isPerfDisplay({ dpr: 2 }); // false: canvas, css, safeArea, backend and orientation are missing
 * ```
 */
export function isPerfDisplay(value: unknown): value is PerfDisplay;

/**
 * What perf reads from `game.renderer.stats()`: calls it once and copies `renderPassesMax`, `kept`,
 * `redraws`, `rebuilds`, each null where the engine does not answer it. Never throws.
 *
 * @param game - The game app (any value).
 * @returns The copy; undefined when there is no `stats` function or the call throws.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * statsOf({ renderer: { stats: () => ({ renderPasses: 1 }) } });
 * // { passesMax: null, kept: null, redraws: null, rebuilds: null }: an engine before spec 23
 * ```
 */
export function statsOf(game: unknown): PerfRenderStats | undefined;

/**
 * A game frame event of an event line (engine fact 11): `overlay` with a numeric `entity`, a string
 * `label`, `what` among `OverlayWhat` and a string `mode`; `pool-trim` with its reason and a finite
 * `freedMb`; `warm` with finite `draws`. The editor's own `devtools`, `command`, `recorder` lines
 * and malformed details are not frame events.
 *
 * @param line - An event line.
 * @returns The frame event, or undefined.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * frameEventOf({ v: 1, kind: "event", t: 0, build: null, frame: 4812, name: "warm", detail: { draws: 18 } });
 * // { kind: "warm", frame: 4812, draws: 18 }
 * ```
 */
export function frameEventOf(line: PerfEventLine): PerfFrameEvent | undefined;

/**
 * Whether a value has the shape of a `RateChange` (21:117-129): numbers `from`, `to`, `dwellMs`;
 * `reason` and `mode` among their unions; `displayHz` a number or null; `window` with three numbers;
 * `thermal` a status or null.
 *
 * @param value - The detail of a `rate` event line.
 * @returns Whether it is a rate change.
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * isRateChange({ from: 120, to: 60 }); // false: reason, mode, window and dwellMs are missing
 * ```
 */
export function isRateChange(value: unknown): value is RateChange;
~~~

---

## 4. Error codes

All errors are JSON-RPC error objects (`WireError`). Messages start with `[moku-editor] ` (`ERROR_PREFIX`). No stack crosses the wire. `bareMessage(message)` strips the prefix for UI text.

| Code | `errorCode` key | `data.reason` | Retryable | Raised by | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -32600 | `invalidRequest` | — | no | hub | duplicate `sub` on one connection; more than 256 pending calls per tools connection |
| -32601 | `unknownMethod` | `unknown_id` (with `data.id`) or none | no | channel, bridge, hub, files, capture | unknown source or command id; unknown channel or method; missing file or folder (`files`) |
| -32602 | `invalidInput` | `invalid_input` (`data.field`) | no | registry, capture, hub, files | input fails `checkInput`; bad `sub`; text over 2 MiB or binary over 16 MiB on write; bad data URL |
| -32000 | `commandFailed` | `command_failed` | no | registry, capture, hub, files | a door threw; `game.capture` gave no picture; a series is already recording; IO error; file too large on read |
| -32001 | `gameReloaded` | `game_reloaded` | yes | hub | the agent closed while a call was pending |
| -32001 | `pageClosed` | `page_closed` | yes | hub | the editor page closed before it answered a relayed `editor.select` |
| -32002 | `timeout` | `timeout` | yes | bridge, hub, link | the call passed its deadline (the command is not cancelled) |
| -32002 | `timeout` | `link_closed` | yes | link | socket not open, socket closed, or `app.stop()` |
| -32003 | `noSession` | `no_session` | no | hub, link | no game connected, or the named session is not open |
| -32003 | `noSession` | `choose_session` | no | hub, link | several sessions and not exactly one embedded; `link.choose` with an id that is not open |
| -32003 | `noEditorPage` | `no_editor_page` | no | hub | `editor.select` and no tools connection with `role=page` is open ("Open the editor page: <url>") |
| -32004 | `forbiddenPath` | `forbidden_path` | no | files | a path fails a sandbox rule |
| -32005 | `versionConflict` | `version_conflict` | no | files | stale `version`, or a `version` for a missing file |
| -32006 | `notJson` | `not_json` | no | registry (`toWireValue`) | a value is not JSON (function, symbol, bigint, cycle, depth over 64) |
| -32007 | `unauthorized` | `unauthorized` | no | hub | a request from an agent connection |
| -32008 | `notInstalled` | `not_installed` (with `data.id`) | no | registry | a read or watch of a source the game does not have: its door threw on the probe (manifest `available: false`). Message `[moku-editor] source <id> is not available in this game: <reason>`. The link does not log or retry it. |
| -32009 | `readOnly` | `read_only` (with `data.id`) | no | registry | the page's build refuses the command: a `--debug` page runs `read` and `cosmetic` commands only (the engine's `controlReadOnly`). `[moku-editor] <id>: refused by this debug build, which runs read and cosmetic commands only.` / `  Build the game with --debug=full to run it.` |
| -32009 | `devOnly` | `dev_only` (with `data.id`) | no | registry | a page with neither the dev nor the debug flag (the engine's `controlRefused`). `[moku-editor] <id>: refused by this build, which has neither the dev nor the debug flag.` / `  Run the game from the dev server, or build it with --debug.` |

Deadlines: bridge `callTimeoutMs` (5000), hub `callTimeoutMs` (5000), link `CALL_TIMEOUT_MS` (10000). A `run` of `editor.series` gets `min(input.durationMs, 60000)` on top in all three, and a `run` of `editor.sheet` gets `min(input.frames × input.everyMs, 60000)`. The MCP bridge waits at most 70 s for any hub answer.

Config errors (not wire errors) are thrown at `createApp` from `onInit`, in the shape:

```
[moku-editor] <plugin>.<field> <problem>.
  <fix line, e.g. Pass pluginConfigs.channel.heartbeatMs, for example 1000.>
```

Examples: `[moku-editor] registry.game is missing.`, `[moku-editor] registry.game is not a game app.`, `[moku-editor] Duplicate registry id "<id>".`, `[moku-editor] files.root "<root>" is not a directory.`, `[moku-editor] files.allow is empty.`, `[moku-editor] Panel "<id>" is already registered.`, `[moku-editor] Key "<combo>" is already bound in <scope>.`

Websocket close codes: 1000 normal (bridge `bye`, link stop, bridge `switch`), 1001 `editor stopping` (hub stop) / `device mode off` / `replaced` (a phone reconnected with its token), 1003 binary frame, 1008 `hello first` / `bad manifest` / `hello twice` / ten malformed messages / `pair first` (a pairing socket's first message, or none within 5 s) / `pairing refused` / `pairing timed out` / `pairing busy`, 1009 frame over 32 MiB (Bun), 1012 `editor restarting` (the bin's Hot reload restart), 4401 `unpaired` (a device token the hub does not know, closed right after the open: the bridge pairs again).

Upgrade refusals of `hub.fetch` (in check order): 404 `missing`, 503 `unavailable`, 426 `upgrade`, 403 `forbidden`, 401 `unauthorized`, 400 `invalid`. The device listeners add 429 `busy` (check `cooldown`: an address that cools down after a refusal or already holds 4 open pairing sockets) and refuse `kind=tools` on the LAN listener (403, check `listener`).

---

## 5. Event catalog

Global events are declared in `src/config.ts` (section 2: `AgentEvents`, `ServerEvents`, `ToolsEvents`). An event is global only when its listener cannot depend on its emitter; the per-plugin events (second table) are declared by their emitter with `register<T>()` and reach only the plugins that list the emitter in `depends`. Payload types are in sections 2, 3 and 7.

| Core | Event | Payload type | Emitted by | When | Hooked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| agent | `bridge:status` | `{ status: LinkStatus; session?: string; link?: DeviceLink }` | bridge | at start (`connecting`), on every change of status kind, on every session change; in device mode on every change of the link's mode, address, pairing code or computer engine, and at most once a second for `seenAt`; `link` in device mode only; never from `onStop` | overlay (link light, Link tab) |
| agent | `overlay:changed` | `OverlayChanged` (`{ mode: OverlayMode; tab: OverlayTab }`) | overlay | every mode or tab change, once at a visible start; never on a place change | recorder (the `devtools` monitor event) |
| agent | `overlay:connect` | `{ address: string }` | overlay | Connect / Pair on the Link tab with a valid `host:port` | bridge (`connect(address)`) |
| server | `hub:session` | `HubSession` | hub | a valid `hello` (`open: true`); an agent close (`open: false`, `reason` `"bye"` or `"game_reloaded"`) | none in the package; for consumer plugins |
| server | `files:written` | `FilesWritten` | files | after each successful `write` or `writeBinary`, after the rename; `kind` from `classifyWrite(path)` | none in the package; for consumer plugins |
| server | `files:project` | `ProjectState` | files | the project index opened (on), a watch batch changed it (on, with `previous` and `change`), or it went off (once) | hub (`publish("project", state)`: the `editor.project` notification, kept and replayed) |
| tools | `link:status` | `{ status: LinkStatus; session?: string }` | link | status changed kind or any field, or the session changed | workspace, panels, flowView, gameView, renderView, stateView, filesView, consoleView |
| tools | `link:project` | `{ state: ProjectState; delta: ProjectDelta }` | link | a new `editor.project` state: not the held one again (on at the same revision and manifest, off with the same reason). `delta` is `projectDelta(held, next)`; at the same revision with another `manifest` it is `{ all: false, files: [old, new manifest] }` | flowView, gameView, renderView, filesView |
| tools | `workspace:changed` | `{ ws: WorkspaceId }` | workspace | `show()` changed the workspace | panels, flowView, gameView, renderView, filesView |
| tools | `workspace:ran` | `RanEvent` | workspace (origins `topbar`, `key`, `palette`), panels (origin `panel`, or the api `run` origin) | a command run from the tools page settled | stateView (taint), consoleView (error lines) |
| tools | `workspace:density` | `{ density: Density }` (`"compact" \| "comfortable"`) | workspace | the applied density changed: a choice in the palette, or `auto` crossing 820 px of window width | flowView (ELK spacing) |
| tools | `workspace:open-file` | `{ path: string; line?: number }` | flowView, gameView | "Open in Files" | filesView |
| tools | `workspace:select-node` | `{ id: string }` | filesView | a Used-by chip | flowView |
| tools | `workspace:focus-frame` | `{ frame: number }` | consoleView | a frame link, `focusFrame()` | flowView |
| tools | `workspace:reveal` | `{ ref: ElementRef }` | gameView | "Show in render tree" | renderView |
| tools | `workspace:inspect` | `{ ref: ElementRef }` | renderView | "Inspect in Game" | gameView |
| tools | `workspace:open-sheet` | `{ index: string }` | filesView | "Open contact sheet" on a series `index.json` | gameView |

`files:written` kind rules (`classifyWrite`, first match wins): starts with `.moku/captures/` → `capture`; equals `.moku/editor/layout.json` → `layout`; ends with `.css`, basename `styles.ts`/`styles.tsx`, ends with `.styles.ts`/`.styles.tsx`, or a `.ts`/`.tsx` module directly in a `styles/` folder (`shared/styles/text.ts`) → `style`; other `.ts`/`.tsx` → `code`; else `other`.

`LinkStatus` semantics: `connecting` (socket open or session attached, no heartbeat yet); `live`/`paused` (the chosen session beats; `paused` from the heartbeat flag); `silent` (no heartbeat for 6 s, or 65 s after a `paused: true` beat); `lost` (socket closed, chosen session closed, or no boot tag `no_boot`); `empty` (connected, no game session, also 10 s after a lost session; inside an expected reload window, at the end of the window). The bridge reports only `connecting`, `live`, `paused`, `lost`.

Per-plugin events:

| Core | Event | Payload type | Emitter | When | Hooked by (through `depends`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| agent | `registry:command` | `RegistryCommandEvent` `{ id, input, via, ok }` | registry | a command run settled (door, module or editor command; `via` `"overlay"`, `"bridge"` or `"local"`; not for an input refused with -32602) | recorder (the `command` monitor event) |
| agent | `recorder:status` | `RecorderStatusEvent` `{ state, lines, bytes, sent, pending }` | recorder | start, stop, share (exporting and back), remove, and a flush tick that changed a number | overlay (REC, Record tab), bridge (ships the pending lines) |
| server | `hub:device` | `HubDeviceEvent` | hub | `listening` (`listenDevices`), `connected` (a pairing or a token reconnect), `lines` (a `perf.lines` batch with new items or a gap), `closed` (`bye`, `lost`, `replaced`, `stopped`), `stopped` (`stopDevices`); never from `onStop` | collector |
| server | `collector:session` | `CollectorSessionEvent` `{ device, file, state, lines, lost, last }` | collector | a log's first written batch, then at most once a second per log; after a close on `away` and `done` | pages (the perf CLI's live lines) |

Not events: heartbeats are a callback api (`channel.onHeartbeat`), and so are taps (`link.onTap`); `ctx.log` lines such as `hub:refused`, `bridge:lost`, `registry:watch-failed`, `registry:source-unavailable`, `link:watch-failed`, `panels:view-failed` are log events, listed in each plugin README.

---

## 6. Configuration reference

All options are set per plugin through `createApp({ pluginConfigs: { <plugin>: { … } } })`, shallow-merged over the defaults (arrays replace). Global configs are empty. Bad values throw at `createApp`.

### Agent

| Plugin | Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| registry | `game` | `GameLike \| undefined` | `undefined` | Required. The app the game made with `createApp`. `onInit` throws without it. |
| registry | `modules` | `readonly DevModule[]` | `[]` | The game's `.dev` modules: extra sources and commands, added after the doors. |
| registry | `name` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | `Manifest.game`. Falls back to trimmed `document.title`, then `"game"`. |
| channel | `heartbeatMs` | `number` | `1000` | Ms between two beats. Whole number ≥ 100. |
| perf | `readEveryMs` | `number` | `250` | How often perf reads the monitor's frame ring (4 Hz). 50–1000. |
| perf | `windowMs` | `number` | `6000` | The window the graph, the spike index and every spike count cover. 1000–30000. |
| perf | `frames` | `number` | `1024` | Rows perf keeps: at least `windowMs` at 120 Hz (720). Whole number, 64–16384. |
| recorder | `autoStart` | `boolean` | `true` | Start a log when the plugin starts (on the first flush tick with the engine's header, after at most 10 ticks). |
| recorder | `keepMb` | `number` | `64` | Most MB in memory: unconfirmed outbox lines, memory-store logs, pending text. 1–512. |
| recorder | `flushEveryMs` | `number` | `1000` | How often the queue is serialized. 100–10000. |
| recorder | `persistEveryMs` | `number` | `5000` | How often text is written to the store (also at 64 KB pending, and at stop). 1000–60000. |
| recorder | `storage` | `"auto" \| "memory"` | `"auto"` | OPFS when the page has it, or never on disk. |
| recorder | `keepFiles` | `number` | `10` | Finished logs kept; the oldest beyond go when a log starts. Whole number, 1–100. |
| overlay | `mode` | `"hidden" \| "pill" \| "card"` | `"hidden"` | Mode at start when the device remembers none (or `remember` is false). The engine's `config.debug.overlay` opens it later through the global channel. The old `open` throws a `TypeError` naming `mode`. |
| overlay | `dock` | `"left" \| "right"` | `"right"` | Edge the window docks to until the person drags it. The old `corner` throws a `TypeError` naming `dock`. |
| overlay | `remember` | `boolean` | `true` | Remember place, mode and tab in `localStorage["moku-editor:overlay"]`. |
| overlay | `mount` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | CSS selector of the element the host is appended to; `undefined` = `document.body`. |
| bridge | `hello` | `string` | `"/__editor/hello"` | Hello route: same-origin path or absolute URL. Non-empty. |
| bridge | `retryMs` | `number` | `1000` | First reconnect delay; doubles per failure up to `MAX_RETRY_MS` (30000), ±20 % jitter. Whole number ≥ 100. |
| bridge | `callTimeoutMs` | `number` | `5000` | Deadline of one `read` or `run`, and of one `perf.ack`. Whole number ≥ 100. |
| bridge | `device` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | Device mode at this computer address (`host:port`, `[v6]:port`). `undefined`: page mode on a served page; device mode with `__MOKU_GAME_EDITOR__` or on a native page, at the remembered address, else the build's, else `"127.0.0.1:47600"`. |
| bridge | `linesPerBatch` | `number` | `200` | Most log lines in one `perf.lines` message. Whole number 1–1000. |
| capture | `maxDurationMs` | `number` | `20000` | Longest series accepted. More → -32602 field `durationMs`. |
| capture | `minIntervalMs` | `number` | `16` | Shortest interval accepted. Less → -32602 field `intervalMs`. |

### Server

| Plugin | Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| files | `root` | `string` | `"."` | Project root, absolute or relative to the working folder. Resolved once with `realpathSync`; must be an existing folder. |
| files | `allow` | `readonly string[]` | `["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx", "**/*.json", "**/*.md", "**/*.css", ".moku/**"]` | Globs a file must match to be read or written. Case-sensitive. Not empty. |
| files | `deny` | `readonly string[]` | `["**/node_modules/**", "**/.git/**", "**/dist/**", "**/.env*"]` | Globs never listed, read or written. Case-insensitive. |
| files | `project` | `boolean` | `true` | Open the project index of `root` on start. `false` leaves it off with reason `"disabled"`; the index is never loaded. |
| hub | `path` | `string` | `"/__editor"` | URL prefix of every editor route. Starts with `/`; letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `/`; no trailing or double slash. |
| hub | `allowOrigins` | `readonly string[]` | `[]` | Extra exact http(s) origins allowed to upgrade and call same-origin routes. No path, no trailing slash. |
| hub | `callTimeoutMs` | `number` | `5000` | Deadline of a forwarded call before -32002. Integer ≥ 100. |
| hub | `silentAfterMs` | `number` | `6000` | No heartbeat this long → silent. 65 s after a `paused: true` beat. Integer ≥ 100. |
| hub | `devicePort` | `number` | `47600` | Port of the device listeners (127.0.0.1 and, with `deviceLan`, the LAN address). Integer 0–65535; 0 picks a free port (tests). |
| hub | `deviceLan` | `boolean` | `false` | Also listen on the computer's LAN address: device upgrades only, pairing confirmed by the person. |
| hub | `lanAddress` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | The LAN address to bind: an IPv4 literal, or an IPv6 literal in canonical lower case without a zone id. Unset picks the first non-internal IPv4 of an `en*`, `wl*` or `eth*` interface, else of any interface. |
| hub | `deviceOrigins` | `readonly string[]` | `["tauri://localhost", "https://tauri.localhost", "http://tauri.localhost"]` | Exact Origins a device's WebView sends: scheme `tauri:`, `http:` or `https:`, a host, no path, lower case. Never added to the normal listener's origins. |
| hub | `pairing` | `"lan" \| "always"` | `"lan"` | `"lan"`: only LAN phones are asked; an adb phone is confirmed at once. `"always"`: every phone is asked. |
| hub | `pairTimeoutMs` | `number` | `60000` | How long a pairing waits for the person before it is refused. Integer ≥ 1000. |
| collector | `out` | `string` | `".moku/perf"` | Folder of the device logs: relative to the files root, or absolute. Created on the first log. Non-empty. |
| collector | `everyS` | `number` | `10` | Seconds between two adb readings (heat, system frames) of a phone. Whole number, 1–3600. |
| collector | `reverseEveryMs` | `number` | `2000` | Ms between two `adb devices` + `adb reverse` rounds. Whole number ≥ 500. |
| collector | `adb` | `string` | `"adb"` | The adb command (a name on PATH or a path). Non-empty. |
| collector | `adbTimeoutMs` | `number` | `5000` | The longest one adb command may run before it is killed. Whole number ≥ 500. |
| collector | `appId` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | The game's Android package; `<appId>.debug` is preferred when installed. Undefined: no gfx lines. |
| pages | `title` | `string` | `"moku editor"` | Tools page `<title>` and `ToolsBoot.title`. 1–120 characters. |
| pages | `editorUrl` | `string` | `"vscode://file/{path}:{line}"` | "Open in editor" template. Must contain `{path}`; scheme cannot be `javascript`, `data`, `vbscript`. |
| pages | `pageDir` | `string \| undefined` | `undefined` | Built page folder. `undefined` tries `dist/tools` next to the bundled module, then the repo `dist/tools`. |
| pages | `gameUrl` | `string` | `"/"` | Same-origin URL of the game page. Starts with `/`, not `//`, no `\`. |
| pages | `toolsPage` | `boolean` | `true` | Serve the tools page and its assets. `false` (`moku-editor perf --no-ui`) answers 404 on `P`, `P/` and `P/assets/*`; `P/hello` and `P/hmr` are unchanged. |

### Tools

| Plugin | Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| link | `retryMs` | `number` | `1000` | Base of the reconnect backoff `min(retryMs × 2^n, 8000)`. |
| link | `boot` | `string` | `"#moku-editor-boot"` | CSS selector of the boot JSON tag `pages` injects. |
| link | `reloadGraceMs` | `number` | `8000` | How long an expected reload (U7: close 1012, a reload the editor started, a game that said bye) reads `lost` with `reloading: true`. Without a heartbeat of the game by then the status is a plain `lost`, or `empty` when the window is still open 10 s after a session loss and no session came back (no upper bound). Positive; `onInit` throws `[moku-editor] link.reloadGraceMs is invalid.` otherwise. |
| workspace | `defaultWorkspace` | `WorkspaceId` | `"game"` | Shown at start when the URL hash names none. |
| workspace | `storageKey` | `string` | `"moku-editor"` | localStorage key of the preferences record. |
| workspace | `reloadTimeoutMs` | `number` | `15000` | How long `reload()` waits for the new session. |
| workspace | `hotReloadWaitMs` | `number` | `1500` | After a save with Bun hot reload on: how long `gameFrame().reload()` waits for the page Bun reloads before it reloads the frame itself. Positive. |
| workspace | `toastMs` | `number` | `2600` | How long one toast stays; hover or focus pauses it. |

| gameView | `capturesDir` | `string` | `".moku/captures"` | Screenshots, series and the two pictures of a pick (`<key>-f<frame>-crop.jpg`, `f<frame>-full.jpg`), each in a day folder `<yyyy-mm-dd>/` (local date; a Shot is `<hhmm>-<flow>.jpg`, a series `series-<hhmm>/`). `.moku/captures` or a folder under it (the files sandbox); `onInit` throws `[moku-editor] gameView.capturesDir must be .moku/captures or a folder under it.` otherwise. |
| gameView | `captureCardMs` | `number` | `10000` | Capture card hides after this unless hovered or focused. |

| gameView | `seriesIntervalsMs` | `readonly number[]` | `[16, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000]` | Interval chips. |

### Bin

```
moku-editor [--root DIR] [--preload FILE]… [--serve-plugin FILE]… [--port 3000] [--no-hmr]
moku-editor <game-html> [--port 3000] [--root .] [--no-hmr] [--help]
moku-editor mcp [<game-html>] [--port N] [--root DIR] [--no-hmr]
moku-editor mcp-config [<game-html>] [--port N]
moku-editor e2e -c <playwright config> [playwright args…]
moku-editor perf [--lan] [--port 47600] [--out DIR] [--every 10] [--no-ui]
moku-editor perf mark "<label>" | perf summary <log.jsonl> | perf compare <a.jsonl> <b.jsonl>
```

| Flag | Short | Default | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--port` | `-p` | `3000` | Digits, 0–65535. `0` picks a free port. |
| `--root` | `-r` | `.` | Project root the editor reads and writes; the moku-game folder of the engine page. Not empty. |
| `--no-hmr` | | hot reload on | Serves with `development: { hmr: false, console: true }`; `hotReload()` reports `{ hmr: false, owner: "bin" }`. |
| `--preload` | | none | A file Bun preloads in the serving process. Repeatable. Engine page only. |
| `--serve-plugin` | | none | A Bun plugin the engine page bundles with, after the engine's hot plugin. Repeatable. Engine page only. |
| `--help` | `-h` | | Prints usage, exit 0. |

Engine page (B5, D-49 … D-51; keys watch D-54, D-55): without an html file the bin serves a moku-game folder (`index.ts` + `config.ts`). (0) Checked first: without the real process (`deps.reexec`, unit seams): "[moku-editor] the engine page needs the real process: pass the game HTML file", exit 1. (1) Not a moku-game folder: "[moku-editor] <root> has no index.ts and config.ts: pass the game HTML file, or run in a moku-game folder", exit 2. (2) It imports `@moku-labs/game/cli` as the game root resolves it, once, for `preparePage` and `watchKeys` (both required, D-54); when it does not resolve or lacks either: "[moku-editor] @moku-labs/game/cli does not resolve from <root>: install @moku-labs/game >=0.13.1 in the game", exit 1. (3) `preparePage(root, { agents: ["@moku-labs/editor/agent/page"], preload, servePlugins })`, the flag paths resolved against the cwd; a throw prints the engine's `[game] …` text, exit 1. (4) From an editor working tree (its package root, found from `Bun.main`, is not under `realpath(<root>)/node_modules` and has `scripts/tree/bundle.ts`) that plugin is appended to `servePlugins`: `@moku-labs/editor`, `/agent`, `/agent/page` and `/tools` bundle from the tree's `dist/`, whose imports of the engine, Pixi, core, common and preact are rewritten in `onLoad` to the game's copies (never `onResolve`, demos#46). (5) Keys watch (D-54, D-55): the parent bin calls `watchKeys(root, { onError })` of the same cli import. It resolves after the engine's first scan, so `generated/` is fresh before the child serves; later a save of an asset or of a `strings/<locale>.json` scans again. A failed scan, the first one too, is one warning (`ui.warn` with the engine's message) and the bin keeps running. A rejection prints the engine's `[game] …` text, exit 1, and no child is spawned. The html form never watches keys; the child never imports the engine's cli. (6) The bin always re-runs itself (D-51): `[execPath, "--config=<root>/.moku/bunfig.toml", Bun.main, "<root>/.moku/index.html", "--root", root, "--port", port, "--no-hmr"?]`, `cwd: root`, `MOKU_EDITOR_REEXEC=1`, signals forwarded, the parent exits with the child's code. The keys watch is closed in a `finally` around the child, so it stops with the child; a throw of `close()` is one warning. Before the spawn the parent has no signal handlers of its own (`main` installs the early ones only with an html file): a SIGINT or SIGTERM while the page is written or the first scan runs ends it with the default action, exit 130 or 143, no child is spawned, and the keys watch ends with the process. The child serves that html as any re-spawned bin; the discovery file's `html` is `<root>/.moku/index.html`. `--preload` and `--serve-plugin` with an html file: "--preload and --serve-plugin need the engine page: drop the html file"; on `mcp` and `mcp-config`: "--preload and --serve-plugin belong to the serving bin". The MCP launcher restarts a gone engine bin in the engine form (no html), so the page is written again and served under that bunfig. Limit: `--preload` and `--serve-plugin` are not in the discovery file, so the restarted bin has none.

Hot reload (D-23, round 2 R6): by default the bin serves with `development: { hmr: true, console: true }` and calls `pages.attachServer(options)` right after `Bun.serve`. A save of a game source makes Bun reload the game page; before it reloads, the bridge stores a `game.bookmark` checkpoint in `sessionStorage`, and the new page restores it (and pauses again when it was paused) and says so in its hello (`manifest.restored`). Bun 1.3.14 cannot switch HMR on a running server, so the bin gives `attachServer` its restart and the Hot reload switch restarts the server with HMR flipped on the same port (D-32): `POST {P}/hmr` answers 200 with the asked state, then the server restarts (A1); the token, the sessions table and `.moku/editor.json` stay, every socket drops for about a second, and the tools page reloads the game frame with its checkpoint so the page gains or drops `/_bun/client`. While HMR is off a save on disk does not reload the game. A failed restart publishes the old state and serves the old options again. Before the restart serves with HMR on, the bin waits, at most 5 s, until Bun's bundler is idle (D-57): Bun 1.3.14 froze its main thread, or crashed, when the page rebundle of the server without HMR (Bun starts one on every page request) and the dev server's first bundle ran at once, and a page request that reaches the old server during the switch set that up. The floor is now Bun 1.4.2 (D-58): the freeze did not reproduce there in 241 runs, and the wait stays as a guard of about 2 ms. Hot swap (game 0.5.0): with `[serve.static] plugins = ["@moku-labs/game/hot"]` in the game root's `bunfig.toml`, a save of a view module (`.tsx`, `styles.ts`, `view.ts`, `animations.ts`, `effects.ts`, `generated/strings.<locale>.ts`) swaps in place: same session, no reload, toast "Game updated"; a logic module still reloads and restores. Bun reads that bunfig once at process start from the process cwd, so a `run` whose `--root` has a `[serve.static]` bunfig and whose cwd is another folder re-spawns the bin in the root (`reexec.ts`: absolute html and root, `MOKU_EDITOR_REEXEC=1` loop guard, SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP forwarded, the parent exits with the child's code, the discovery file names the child). The MCP launcher spawns the bin with `cwd: root`.

e2e (D-52, D-53, `e2e.ts`): one Playwright process, so one fresh editor bin, per project and spec file, because Bun's dev server degrades after many hot reloads in one process (also within one project: merge-game failed from the ~90th reload-heavy spec). `splitRest(rest)` sorts the user's words into `projects` (`--project X Y…` takes every next word not starting with `-`, as Playwright's variadic option, up to a path-like word (a `/`, or `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.mjs` at the end), which is a file filter, so a project named like a path needs `--project=X`; `--project=X` one), `files` (any other word not starting with `-` that is not a flag's value), `reporters` (`--reporter`, `--add-reporter`), `listOnly` (`--shard`, `--last-failed`) and `other`; a flag with a required value (`-g`, `-G`, `-j`, `--repeat-each`, `--timeout`, …) keeps its next word, `-u` / `--update-snapshots` only `all|changed|missing|none`, `--debug` only `inspector|cli`, `--only-changed` a word not starting with `-` and not ending in `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`; `--flag=v` is one word. The plan comes from `bun x playwright test -c <config> --list --reporter=json --pass-with-no-tests <files> --project=<p>… <other> <listOnly>` (JSON output env vars removed; a failed or unparsable list: "[moku-editor] could not list the tests of <config>: <reason>", exit 1). `listPlan(json)` answers `{ rootDir: config.rootDir, pairs }`: one (project, file) pair per named project and spec file with at least one listed test, projects in config order, files in list order (`specs[].file`, relative to `rootDir`), unnamed projects skipped. Each pair runs as `bun x playwright test -c <config> --project=<p> <fileFilter(file, rootDir)> --pass-with-no-tests <other> <reporters>` with `PORT` = `PORT` (an integer 1-65535, else 4417) + its index, one after another, all of them; `fileFilter` = `^<rootDir>/<file>$`, regex-escaped with `/` separators (Playwright tests a file argument as a regex on the absolute path). `--project=<p>` is one word because the variadic `--project <p>` would read the file regex as a project. After each run `ui.info("<project> · <file> · passed|failed (code N) · <s> s")`, at the end `ui.info("e2e: <n> runs · <failed> failed · <s> s")` (`E2eDeps.now`, default `performance.now`). A failed run's line and a failing summary print as errors; a warning names the tests of an unnamed project that did not run. Exit = the first non-zero code, else 0. A `--list`, an empty plan (no test matched, or only an unnamed project) runs once as given, without `--pass-with-no-tests`, so Playwright's "No tests found" tells the user. Lock (`E2eDeps.lock`: `take(): Promise<number | undefined>`, `release(): Promise<void>`; `processE2eDeps` sets `fileLock(process.cwd())`): before the CI install `runE2e` creates `.moku/e2e.lock` in the cwd with the bin's pid (`wx`, folder created); while a live pid (`process.kill(pid, 0)`) holds it: "[moku-editor] another e2e run (pid N) holds .moku/e2e.lock: wait for it, or delete the file when no run is left", exit 1, nothing runs; a dead or unreadable pid is taken over; released in a `finally` after the last run, also after a failure, and only while the file holds this pid; a `--list` takes no lock. `CI=true` runs `bun x playwright install chromium` first. Only `-c X` / `--config X` / `--config=X` is read, before `--help` (missing: "[moku-editor] e2e needs the Playwright config: -c <file>", exit 2); no signal handlers, a Ctrl+C reaches Playwright through the process group.

perf (`src/plugins/pages/perf/`, device mode): a first word `perf` picks the perf CLI before the global `--help` scan. `runPerf` starts the server core (files, hub, collector, pages) without a game, with `files.root` the cwd, `files.project: false` and `collector.appId` from `native.identifier` of the game's `config.ts`; the switches map onto plugin fields through the pure `perfConfigOf` (`--lan` → `hub.deviceLan`, `--port`/`-p` → `hub.devicePort` (default 47600, 0 random), `--out`/`-o` → `collector.out` (default `.moku/perf`), `--every` → `collector.everyS` (1–3600, default 10), `--no-ui` → `pages.toolsPage: false`). It calls `hub.listenDevices({ confirm, routes: { "/": the no-game page } })`, prints the ready block (Phones `127.0.0.1:<port> · adb reverse every 2 s`, LAN, Tools `http://127.0.0.1:<port><path>/#render`, Logs, Engine; the token never), then `pages.attachPerf(output)`: per phone log a header line (`◉ <model> · <backend> · engine <id> · build <id> · adb <address>`, `● REC → <file>`), a STALE warning once when the phone's engine differs from `files.engine().id`, a digest line at most every 5 s (`garden/boss  @60  54 fps  p90 18.2  gpu 6.1  spikes 2 (upload, gc?)  38.0 °C  · 1 840 lines`), `○ <model> left …` on `away`, `■ <model> · <n> lines → <file>` on `done`. The pairing prompt (`perf/prompt.ts`) asks for the four-digit code a LAN phone shows (`node:readline/promises` behind `PerfDeps.ask`, the known MC1 exception); an empty Enter, another code or a cut question refuses; a phone that prints its own code into its model, engine or build is refused without a question. Ctrl+C: `.moku/perf.json` goes first, then `hub.stopDevices()` → `collector.settled()` → `editor.stop()`, then one summary table per log. `.moku/perf.json` `{ version: 1, pid, port, path, token, lan, startedAt }` (0600, temp file and rename, removed on stop): `perf mark` reads it, checks the pid, refuses a host other than 127.0.0.1, and posts the label to `http://127.0.0.1:<port><path>/perf/mark` with `authorization: Bearer <token>` (200 `✓ mark "boss" in N log(s)`; 401 `The running perf has another token.`; no run `No moku-editor perf runs in this folder.`). `perf summary <log>` prints `summaryText(summarize(parsePerfLog(text)))` (a file without a header or sample: `<log> is not a moku perf log (v1).`); `perf compare <a> <b>` prints `compareText` by screen and rate, then one warning counting the screens that got worse by 10 % or more (exit 0). Every argument error is two lines with the usage, exit 2.

Exit codes: 0 help, `mcp-config`, `mcp` after stdin ended or a SIGINT/SIGTERM, or serving; the child's code after a re-spawn or the engine page's re-run; 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) when the engine form gets the signal before its child is spawned, no child; 1 missing or bad HTML file, start failed, port in use, the engine page not written or its keys watch not started; 2 bad arguments, or no html file and a root that is not a moku-game folder. Binds 127.0.0.1 only; the token is never printed.

Discovery file: (`moku-editor perf` never touches it, so the MCP bridge never mistakes a perf run for a served game.) After `Bun.serve` the bin writes `<root>/.moku/editor.json` `{ version: 1, pid, port, url, ws, token, root, html, startedAt }` (type `EditorDiscovery`, mode 0600, temp file then rename) and removes it on SIGINT/SIGTERM and in an `exit` listener, only while it still carries this pid. A bin killed with SIGKILL leaves it; the MCP bridge treats a dead pid as no bin. Add `.moku/` to the game's `.gitignore`.

`mcp-config` prints the `.mcp.json` snippet, a blank line and the `claude mcp add` line, then exits 0:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "moku-editor": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "bunx",
      "args": ["moku-editor", "mcp", "web/index.html", "--port", "3000"]
    }
  }
}

claude mcp add moku-editor -- bunx moku-editor mcp web/index.html --port 3000
```

MCP bridge (`moku-editor mcp`, `src/plugins/pages/mcp/`, D-31): a separate process, not a plugin; a hub **tools client** (`${ws}?token=…&kind=tools`, `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<port>`), so the hub's session choice, input checks and files sandbox apply as for the tools page. Newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio; stdout carries only protocol frames, logs go to stderr.

- `initialize` → `{ protocolVersion, capabilities: { tools: { listChanged: true }, logging: {} }, serverInfo: { name: "moku-editor", version }, instructions }` (`instructions`: which tools are generic, which are command doors, that cheat_* and raw_* change the game outside its rules, that the list changes when the game reloads, and that `moku_device`, `moku_show`, `moku_select` and `moku_hot_reload` drive the editor itself while `moku_files_find` and `moku_project` read the project index); versions `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26` (the client's when listed, else `2025-11-25`). `ping` and `logging/setLevel` → `{}`. An unknown method → -32601, bad params → -32602, a line that is not JSON → -32700. Notifications are never answered; `notifications/cancelled { requestId }` aborts that call. `notifications/progress` during `moku_wait` and `moku_series` when the request has `_meta.progressToken`; `notifications/tools/list_changed` only when the door tools change (below); a change before `notifications/initialized` is sent once right after it. `tools/list` is the generic tools, then the door tools; the first one waits at most 3 s for the door tools. A door tool that is gone answers `isError` "`<name>` is gone: the game changed. Call moku_manifest, or moku_run { id }."
- Claude Code 2.1.280 (recorded in `src/plugins/pages/__tests__/fixtures/claude-*.json`): it sends `server/discover` (draft protocol 2026-07-28) first, gets -32601, then `initialize` with `protocolVersion: "2025-11-25"` and id 0, `notifications/initialized` and `tools/list`.
- Which bin: a live `.moku/editor.json` under `--root` (default the working directory) wins. Without one the bridge starts `moku-editor <html> --port <port> --root <root> [--no-hmr]` detached (output in `.moku/editor.log`, 0600), when it knows a game html (argv, else the last discovery file it saw, else, in a moku-game folder, the engine page `<root>/.moku/index.html`: a root with `index.ts` and `config.ts`, `isGameFolder` of `pages/discovery.ts`, D-63; so `moku-editor mcp --root <game>` with no html and no `.moku/` starts the engine page, at startup and on `moku_start {}`); the html `<root>/.moku/index.html` (the engine page) is left out, so the bin starts in the engine form `moku-editor --port <port> --root <root> [--no-hmr]` and re-runs under `--config=<root>/.moku/bunfig.toml` (D-51); port `--port`, else the last port, else 3000; it waits at most 15 s for the discovery file and owns that bin. Without an html, in a root that is no moku-game folder, tools answer `isError` "moku-editor is not running. Start it (`bunx moku-editor web/index.html --port 3000`) or call moku_start." After a closed hub socket the bridge reads the discovery file again and reconnects: one try at the close, then at most three more, 1, 2 and 4 s apart (0, 1, 3 and 7 s after the close, like the link), while the file names a live bin; the bin's restart keeps its port closed for up to about 6 s (D-57). A connection the hub drops within 5 s of opening (`STABLE_MS`) counts as a failed try: the next try waits, and the count starts over only after a connection held 5 s, so a bin that accepts and drops every socket is tried at most four times in 7 s, not in a loop. The tries end with a connection, without a live bin, after the last wait, on `moku_stop` and on stdin end or a signal; a tool call in between tries one connect. A connect that opens after the teardown began is closed and not followed. stderr (D-59): a close prints one info line (`moku-editor mcp: the moku-editor connection closed; reconnecting`, `… closed after less than 5 s`, or `… closed; no running moku-editor` when no bin runs), a failed try prints nothing (its message is kept for the "not running" answer), a connect prints `moku-editor mcp: connected to <url>`, and tries that end without a connection print exactly one warning: `[moku-editor] mcp: could not reconnect to moku-editor; the next tool call tries again.` with `Last attempt: <error>` on the next line.
- Teardown on stdin end, SIGINT or SIGTERM (the same steps): pending calls are aborted, every watch is dropped, the socket closes, an owned bin gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 2 s; a bin the bridge did not start keeps running. After a signal it lets go of stdin, so the process exits 0 while the client keeps the pipe open.
- Generic tools (22, all `moku_*`, closed input schemas, optional `session` on every game tool, static annotations): `moku_status`, `moku_sessions` (heartbeat `{ frame, paused, silent }` and `manifestHash`), `moku_manifest`, `moku_read`, `moku_wait` (`until` / `changedFrom` / first change, `timeoutMs` 100–25000, default 10000), `moku_run` (text starts `effect: <effect>`), `moku_screenshot` (`{ maxWidth?, key?, format? }`: `editor.capture { maxWidth, format, key? }`, default 1080 px and JPEG, `key` crops to one ui element plus 8 px; above 300 KB taken once more at half width; the image `mimeType` follows the data URL), `moku_series` (`editor.sheet { frames, everyMs, maxWidth: 1080, format: "jpeg" }`, or `game.capture { sheet }` at full size when the agent has no `editor.sheet`; needs game ≥ 0.4), `moku_reference` (a card and its crop: `"latest"` is the newest card of `.moku/captures/<yyyy-mm-dd>/*.md` (only `YYYY-MM-DD` folder names, newest day first) and the older flat `.moku/captures/*.md`; a name is the newest card with that name; a path is that card), `moku_selection` (hub `editor.selection`: the editor page's `SelectionInfo` and its crop; the JSON has `edits` when the element has pending style edits, `{ path, from, to }` each, for the agent to apply in the source; null answers "Nothing is selected in the editor."), `moku_select` (`{ key?, rect?, node?, card? }`, exactly one of `key`, `rect` or `node`; `key` and `rect`: hub `editor.select` relayed to the editor page, which picks it like the element picker without the clipboard; the selection and its crop; no editor page: -32003 `no_editor_page`; `node` (1–256 chars, D-61): `editor.show { workspace: "flow" }`, then `editor.node { id }`, then `files.find { key: "node:<id>" }`, skipped while the project index is off; text JSON `{ id, selected, places }`, no crop and no card (`card` with `node` is an `isError`); -32003 `no_graph` reads `isError` "the Flow view has no graph yet; try again in a moment"), `moku_device` (`{ preset?, orientation? ("portrait" | "landscape"), folded? }`: hub `editor.device`, relayed to the editor page; only the given fields change, `{}` reads; text JSON `DeviceInfo` `{ preset, orientation, folded, w, h, presets }`; not destructive, idempotent), `moku_show` (`{ workspace? }`, one of `flow`, `game`, `render`, `state`, `files`, `console`: hub `editor.show`; `{ workspace, workspaces }`; not destructive, idempotent), `moku_files_list`, `moku_files_read`, `moku_files_write` (`.moku/editor.json` and `.moku/editor.log` are hidden and refused), `moku_files_find` (`{ key }`, 1–512 chars, such as `node:board/merge`, `flow:board`, `jsx:coins`, `textStyle:ui.title`, `style:features/ui/popup.tsx#popupScreen`: hub `files.find { key }`; the places as JSON `{ path, binding?, line, hash, broken? }`; none: "No place for <key>."; index off: the hub's -32008 as `isError` "project index off: <reason>"; read-only), `moku_project` (`{ path?, prefix? }`, at most one: the project state the hub published as `editor.project`, kept by the hub client, no request; no argument: `{ state, revision, manifest?, keys, broken, prefixes }` with the key count and the count per prefix; `prefix`: the keys that start with it → def paths, and for `jsx:` the text "jsx keys are not in the index state; use moku_files_find"; `path`: `{ defines, uses, broken? }` of that file; off: `{ state: "off", reason }`; read-only), `moku_reload` (`editor.reload { restore }`, waits ≤ 15 s for the game to reconnect), `moku_hot_reload` (`{ on }`, D-62: already in that state → `{ hmr, owner, restarted: false }` with no POST; owner `"server"` → `isError` "hot reload is owned by the game's server; it cannot be switched"; else `POST <tools page>hmr` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` of the discovery file and the body `{ "hmr": <on> }`, where another status than 200 is `isError` with the status and an answer the restart cut off counts as sent; then it polls the bridge's connection at most 15 s until a connection opened after the POST carries the asked state and held 1.5 s (the old server of the restarting bin can take the first reconnect try and drops it when it stops): `{ hmr, owner, restarted: true }`; the token is in no result and on no stderr line; the game page loads again only with `moku_reload`; not destructive, idempotent), `moku_start` (`{ html?, port? }`; no html needed in a moku-game folder), `moku_stop` (owned bin only). Editor requests (D-60): `editor.device`, `editor.show` and `editor.node` ride the relay of `editor.select`; a -32601 (the hub of an older bin does not relay the method, or the page was loaded before the bin was updated and has no handler) reads `isError` "moku-editor or its editor page is older than the bridge; restart moku-editor and reload the page".
- Door tools (`door-tools.ts`, D-35, D-36, D-37): one tool per command door of the selected session (the one `moku_run` uses without `session`: the only one, else the embedded one; several sessions and none embedded: no door tools). Sources stay behind `moku_read`.
  - Name: the id with `.` as `_` (`game.tap` → `game_tap`, `timber.openShop` → `timber_openShop`); `cheat` and `raw` doors get the prefix `cheat_` / `raw_` (`cheat_game_fill`, `raw_game_restore`).
  - No tool (logged once per hash on stderr as `[moku-editor] mcp: no tool for <id>: <reason>; use moku_run`): `COVERED_DOORS` = `game.capture`, `editor.capture`, `editor.sheet`, `editor.series`, `editor.seriesStop`, `editor.reload` (screenshots go only through `moku_screenshot`, JPEG by default, about 300 KB at most; data URL answers and the `game_reloaded` end of a reload stay with the generic tools); a final name starting with `moku_`; a name longer than 40 characters (so `mcp__moku-editor__<name>` fits 64); an id outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; an input field `_session` or outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`; two doors whose names collide (`a.b` and `a_b`: both dropped).
  - Input schema: closed object, one property per field (`string`, `number` finite, `boolean`, `json` any JSON), fields without `?` required, plus the optional `_session`. A call sends hub `run { id, input }` in that session (`input` left out when empty); the text reads like `moku_run`.
  - Description `[<effect>] <title>. Command door <id> of <game>. Same as moku_run { id: "<id>" }.`; annotations: `read` read-only, `route` and `cosmetic` not destructive, `cheat` and `raw` destructive, never open-world. Claude Code ignores annotations for permissions; deny with `{ "permissions": { "deny": ["mcp__moku-editor__cheat_*", "mcp__moku-editor__raw_*"] } }`.
  - Change: the set follows the hub's `sessions` by `SessionInfo.manifestHash`. The same hash changes nothing; a new hash fetches the manifest, rebuilds the set and sends `notifications/tools/list_changed` once. No session chosen, or no hub connection: the set stays 8 s (a hot reload of the same game and the bin's restart blink nothing: the bridge's last reconnect try lands 7 s after the close), then empties, with one `list_changed` when it held doors. The 8 s count again from each new hub connection that has no session yet (the game page's third reconnect try lands 5.6 to 8.4 s after the close, which can be after the bridge is back); a `sessions` list without a session does not start them again. A bin without `manifestHash` is fetched once per session. A failed manifest fetch keeps the old set. A client that does not refresh after `list_changed` keeps the old list; `moku_run` runs every door.
- Liveness (M7): screenshot and series read the session heartbeat first; paused or silent answers `isError` "game paused or hidden at frame N — bring the editor pane to front or resume". Pictures need a visible game page.

---

## 7. Plugins

Each section: core, tier, depends, lifecycle, then the Config, Api, event and constant types verbatim from `types.ts`. Core order: agent (registry, channel, perf, recorder, overlay; opt-in bridge, capture), server (files, hub, collector, pages), tools.

### 7.1 registry — agent, Complex

- depends: none (first agent plugin). Lifecycle: `onInit` (`buildCatalogue`), `onStart` (`refreshManifest`: drops the manifest cache and builds it again, so the door sources are probed once the game runs; start the editor after the game).
- Imports from the game: `read`, `watch`, `sources` from `@moku-labs/game/inspect`; `run`, `commands` from `@moku-labs/game/control`.
- Manifest order: door entries, then modules in config order, then editor commands in `add` order. Sources and commands share one id namespace. `add` takes editor commands and editor sources (perf's `editor.perf.*`, the recorder's `editor.recorder`).
- Sources the game does not have: every manifest build probes each door source once with its default input `{}` (a source with a required input, the element locators of `UNPROBED_SOURCES` — `game.rect` and `game.locate`, which throws on `{}` — and module sources are not probed). A door that throws (a game without `effectsPlugin`; a screenless game without `ui`, `world`, a renderer, audio or assets; game 0.4.2's `game.sounds` without `audioPlugin`, reason `[game] The source game.sounds needs audioPlugin.`) is listed with `available: false` and `reason`, and its `read`/`watch` throw -32008 `not_installed` (`[moku-editor] source <id> is not available in this game: <reason>`, not retryable) without a door call or a warn. The next build probes again. An editor source with a probe (perf's) is listed the same way.
- Build profile (engine spec 10 C1): the registry reads the page's flags from `globalThis` (a string `"true"` is not a flag): `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__` → `dev`, else `__MOKU_GAME_CONTROL__` → `full`, else `__MOKU_GAME_AGENT__` → `read`, else `none`; `__MOKU_GAME_BUILD__` is `id`, `__MOKU_GAME_ENGINE__` is `engine`. `build()` and `Manifest.build` carry it. Every command descriptor gets `allowed` (`refusalOf(profile, effect)`: dev and full run everything, read runs `read` and `cosmetic`, none nothing) and `reason` (`"read-only"` | `"dev-only"`) when refused; the game's `overlay` marker (`"toggle"` | `"button"`) is copied from a door or module command, and an editor command that sets one throws a `TypeError`. A run the engine refuses answers -32009: `read_only` (the engine's `controlReadOnly`, a `--debug` page) or `dev_only` (`controlRefused`, a page with neither flag), logged `registry:command-refused` at info.
- The run event: every door, module and editor command is wrapped once; when its run settles it emits the per-plugin `registry:command { id, input, via, ok }` (`via` from `run(raw, via)`: `"overlay"`, `"bridge"`, or `"local"` when absent; `ok` false on any reject, -32009 included). An input refused by `checkInput` (-32602) is not a run and emits nothing. The recorder hooks it.
- Events: emits `registry:command` (per-plugin, through `depends`). Logs: `registry:source-failed`, `registry:command-failed`, `registry:watch-failed`, `registry:value-failed` (warn); `registry:source-unavailable`, `registry:command-refused` (info); `registry:emit-failed`.

~~~ts
/**
 * Registry ids: camelCase words joined by dots, the pattern the game's defineCommand uses.
 */
export const ID_PATTERN = /^[a-z][\dA-Za-z]*(?:\.[a-z][\dA-Za-z]*)+$/;

/**
 * What the doors need of an app: the headless app plus the committed model (the game's WatchApp),
 * and the pause stack when the game has one. `lifecycle` is optional: `HeadlessApp` has no such
 * member and the engine exports no type for it.
 */
export type GameLike = HeadlessApp & {
  readonly model: { readonly store: { snapshot(): Model.Snapshot } };
  /** The game's pause stack: the reasons why the clock stands, in push order. */
  readonly lifecycle?: { reasons(): readonly string[] };
};

/**
 * A game's `.dev` module: extra sources and commands, merged after the door catalogue.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const mergeDev: DevModule = { commands: [addCoins, refillEnergy] };
 * ```
 */
export type DevModule = {
  readonly sources?: readonly DoorSource[];
  readonly commands?: readonly DoorCommand[];
};

/**
 * Registry configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { registry: { game: app, modules: [mergeDev], name: "merge-game 0.0.0" } } });
 * ```
 */
export type RegistryConfig = {
  /** The running game app. Required: onInit throws when it is undefined. */
  game: GameLike | undefined;
  /** The game's dev modules: extra sources and commands, merged after the door catalogue. */
  modules: readonly DevModule[];
  /** Display name for Manifest.game; falls back to document.title, then "game" (R6). */
  name: string | undefined;
};

/**
 * A closure-erased source: raw Json in, wire-safe Json out. Editor sources may give a probe.
 */
export type SourceEntry = {
  readonly descriptor: SourceDescriptor;
  read(raw: Json): Json;
  watch(raw: Json, fn: (value: Json) => void): () => void;
  /** Editor sources only: why the source is not available now, or undefined. Run at each manifest build. */
  probe?(): string | undefined;
};

/**
 * A closure-erased command: raw Json in, RunResult out. An overlay toggle of the game has value().
 */
export type CommandEntry = {
  readonly descriptor: CommandDescriptor;
  /** Runs it; `via` names the source for `registry:command` (absent: "local"). */
  run(raw: Json, via?: CommandVia): Promise<RunResult>;
  /** Overlay toggles of the game only: the switch's state now; undefined when value(app) failed. */
  value?(): boolean | undefined;
};

/**
 * Payload of the registry's per-plugin event `registry:command`: one command run settled.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const ran: RegistryCommandEvent = { id: "garden.glow", input: { on: false }, via: "overlay", ok: true };
 * ```
 */
export type RegistryCommandEvent = {
  readonly id: string;
  /** The raw input as the caller gave it (null when none). */
  readonly input: Json;
  readonly via: CommandVia;
  /** True when the run resolved; false when it rejected (a refusal included). */
  readonly ok: boolean;
};

/**
 * The registry's own events: declared in its `index.ts`, hooked through `depends` (not in
 * `AgentEvents`).
 */
export type RegistryEvents = {
  readonly "registry:command": RegistryCommandEvent;
};

/**
 * The game clock and why it stands. The channel heartbeat sends `frame` and `paused` only (R6);
 * the reload checkpoints read `held`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // The game tab is hidden: the clock stands, but nobody paused the game.
 * const hidden: Clock = { frame: 1840, paused: true, held: false, reasons: ["background"] };
 * // The developer paused it in the editor, in a hidden tab.
 * const kept: Clock = { frame: 1840, paused: true, held: true, reasons: ["background", "devtools"] };
 * ```
 */
export type Clock = {
  /** The frame of the game clock. */
  readonly frame: number;
  /** True while the clock does not run, for any pause reason. */
  readonly paused: boolean;
  /**
   * True while the developer holds the pause: the reasons include `"devtools"`, the one `game.pause`
   * pushes. A game without `lifecycle.reasons` answers `paused` here.
   */
  readonly held: boolean;
  /** A copy of `game.lifecycle.reasons()`, in push order; empty for a game without it. */
