  readonly reasons: readonly string[];
};

/**
 * The registry api (`app.registry`, `ctx.require(registryPlugin)`): the catalogue of every source
 * and command the editor can read, watch or run.
 */
export type RegistryApi = {
  /**
   * The frozen manifest: descriptors only, no functions. Cached until the next `add`; `game`, `page`
   * and `embedded` are computed at call time. Each build probes the door sources and the editor
   * sources that have a probe first: one that is not available is listed with `available: false` and
   * its `reason`. Every command descriptor carries `allowed` (and `reason` when refused) for this
   * page's build; the manifest carries `build`.
   *
   * @returns The manifest the bridge sends in `hello`.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A plain --debug build of the merge game on a phone:
   * app.registry.manifest().build; // { profile: "read", id: "debug-20261014T160000Z", engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0" }
   * app.registry.manifest().commands.find(command => command.id === "game.tap");
   * // { id: "game.tap", title: "Tap", input: { key: "string?", target: "json?" }, effect: "route", allowed: false, reason: "read-only" }
   * ```
   */
  manifest(): Manifest;
  /**
   * Looks up a source entry: door, module, registry or editor. Callers map `undefined` to -32601.
   *
   * @param id - The source id, e.g. "game.position".
   * @returns The entry, or undefined for an unknown id or a command id.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.registry.source("game.position")?.read(null); // { path: "home", … }
   * app.registry.source("editor.perf.second")?.read(null); // { state: "on", fps: { loop: 60, drawn: 54 }, spikes: 6, … }
   * ```
   */
  source(id: string): SourceEntry | undefined;
  /**
   * Looks up a command entry: door, module or editor. An overlay toggle's entry has `value()`.
   *
   * @param id - The command id, e.g. "game.step".
   * @returns The entry, or undefined for an unknown id or a source id.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The overlay draws the game's "Glow" switch, then flips it.
   * app.registry.command("garden.glow")?.value?.(); // true
   * await app.registry.command("garden.glow")?.run({ on: false }); // { value: …, state: { path: "garden/boss", frame: 4812, tainted: false } }
   * ```
   */
  command(id: string): CommandEntry | undefined;
  /**
   * Adds an editor-owned command or source. Call it in `onInit`: the tools page sees a later add only
   * on the next bridge hello. Drops the manifest cache. A source may give a `probe`: the registry runs
   * it at each manifest build, and an answer lists the source as not available.
   *
   * @param entry - The editor command (descriptor, run) or source (descriptor, read, watch, probe?).
   * @throws {Error} For an invalid or used id, an unknown input kind or changes, a `cheat` or `raw`
   *   effect, or an `overlay` marker on a command (the overlay lists only the game's commands).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // perf, in its onInit: the frame graph's window for the tools page and MCP (spec 03).
   * ctx.require(registryPlugin).add({
   *   descriptor: { id: "editor.perf.window", title: "Frame graph", input: {}, changes: "frame" },
   *   read: () => toWireValue(writeWireWindow(state.window)),
   *   watch: (_raw, fn) => watchTicks(state, () => fn(toWireValue(writeWireWindow(state.window)))),
   *   probe: () => offText(state) // "the game has no renderer (headless)" on a headless game
   * });
   * ```
   */
  add(entry: CommandEntry | SourceEntry): void;
  /**
   * Where the game stands now, for editor commands that run no door (R2, R6).
   *
   * @returns `{ path, frame, tainted }` from game.position, the clock and game.tainted.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] registry.game is missing.\n  Pass pluginConfigs.registry.game.` when no game is
   *   configured (a lifecycle error, two lines).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.registry.envelope(); // { path: "home", frame: 1840, tainted: false }
   * ```
   */
  envelope(): RunState;
  /**
   * The game clock and why it stands (R6). `paused` is true for any pause reason; `held` only
   * while the reasons include `"devtools"`, the pause of `game.pause`. The channel heartbeat reads
   * `frame` and `paused`; a reload checkpoint reads `held`, so a hidden tab's `"background"` pause
   * is not restored. A game without `lifecycle.reasons` answers `reasons: []` and `held` equal to
   * `paused`. See README "Clock".
   *
   * @returns `{ frame, paused, held, reasons }`; `reasons` is a copy.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] registry.game is missing.\n  Pass pluginConfigs.registry.game.` when no game is
   *   configured (a lifecycle error, two lines).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * await registry.command("game.pause")?.run(null);
   * registry.clock(); // { frame: 1840, paused: true, held: true, reasons: ["devtools"] }
   * ```
   */
  clock(): Clock;
  /**
   * The game app the registry wraps, for an editor plugin that reads the engine directly (the renderer
   * monitor's rings are not a door).
   *
   * @returns The configured game app.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] registry.game is missing.\n  Pass pluginConfigs.registry.game.` when no game is
   *   configured (a lifecycle error, two lines).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // perf, in onInit: find the engine's performance monitor.
   * const monitor = monitorOf(ctx.require(registryPlugin).game()); // undefined on a headless game
   * ```
   */
  game(): GameLike;
  /**
   * The build of this page: its profile (dev, full, read, none) from the engine's build flags, the build
   * id and the engine fingerprint when the page has them. Read once; the flags of a page never change.
   *
   * @returns The frozen BuildInfo.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The overlay's engine line on a plain --debug build.
   * app.registry.build(); // { profile: "read", id: "debug-20261014T160000Z", engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0" }
   * ```
   */
  build(): BuildInfo;
};
~~~

### 7.2 channel — agent, Standard

- depends: `[registryPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` (`checkConfig`), `onStart` (`startHeartbeat`, unref'd interval), `onStop` (`stopChannel`).
- `watch` delivers the current value before it returns; `run` dispatches in a microtask; the heartbeat runs on `setInterval`, so a paused game still beats.
- `run(id, input?, via?)`: `via` names who runs the command for the registry's `registry:command` (`"overlay"` from the overlay's Game tab, `"bridge"` for a hub request, absent `"local"`).
- In Chromium the beat also carries `heap { usedMb, limitMb }` from `performance.memory` (MB, rounded to 0.1); elsewhere `heap` is absent.
- Events: none. Log: `channel:heartbeat-listener-failed` (warn, `{ message }`).

~~~ts
/**
 * Channel configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { channel: { heartbeatMs: 500 } } });
 * ```
 */
export type ChannelConfig = {
  /** Milliseconds between two heartbeats. Finite integer ≥ 100. */
  heartbeatMs: number;
};

/**
 * A heartbeat listener (the bridge pushes beats, samples frame sources, flushes its backlog).
 */
export type HeartbeatListener = (beat: Heartbeat) => void;

/**
 * The channel api (`app.channel`, `ctx.require(channelPlugin)`): the in-process EditorChannel of
 * the game page plus the heartbeat. `read`, `watch` and `status` are documented on EditorChannel;
 * `run` takes who runs the command as well (still assignable to EditorChannel). Here `watch`
 * delivers the current value before it returns, and an unknown id, an invalid input or a throwing
 * first `onValue` throws synchronously and opens no watch.
 */
export type ChannelApi = Omit<EditorChannel, "run"> & {
  /**
   * Runs a command in a microtask, off the game's frame loop. `via` names who runs it for the
   * registry's `registry:command` event: the overlay's Game tab passes `"overlay"`, the bridge
   * `"bridge"`; absent, the registry records `"local"`.
   *
   * @param id - The command id, e.g. "game.step".
   * @param input - The command input; omit it for a command without input.
   * @param via - Who runs it; omit it for an in-process caller.
   * @returns A promise of the command's value and where the game stands after it.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The bridge runs a hub `run` request from the tools page or MCP.
   * (await ctx.require(channelPlugin).run("game.step", { frames: 1 }, "bridge")).state; // { path: "home", frame: 1841, tainted: false }
   * ```
   */
  run(id: string, input?: Json, via?: CommandVia): Promise<RunResult>;
  /**
   * A fresh frozen beat now, from the registry clock. In Chromium it also carries the page heap
   * from `performance.memory`, in MB rounded to 0.1; elsewhere `heap` is absent.
   *
   * @returns `{ frame, paused, at }` plus `heap` when present, `at` in epoch ms.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The bridge sends a beat right after the socket opens.
   * ctx.require(channelPlugin).heartbeat(); // { frame: 1840, paused: false, at: 1790000000000 } in Bun
   * // In Chromium: { frame: 1840, paused: false, at: 1790000000000, heap: { usedMb: 12.8, limitMb: 4095.8 } }
   * ```
   */
  heartbeat(): Heartbeat;
  /**
   * Adds a listener called on every interval tick (`heartbeatMs`), in subscription order. A
   * throwing listener is logged at warn and the others still run. No beat is sent at start.
   *
   * @param fn - The listener.
   * @returns An idempotent remover.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The bridge pushes every beat to the editor server until it stops.
   * const off = ctx.require(channelPlugin).onHeartbeat(beat => {
   *   socket.send(encode(notification("game", "heartbeat", beat)));
   * });
   * off();
   * ```
   */
  onHeartbeat(fn: HeartbeatListener): () => void;
};
~~~

### 7.3 perf — agent, Complex

- depends: `[registryPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` (checks the config, adds the five sources), `onStart` (finds `app.renderer.monitor`; starts the read timer every `readEveryMs` and the stream listener), `onStop` (clears both). A start whose first read throws leaves no stream listener behind.
- The read model of the last `windowMs` (6 s): typed arrays allocated once (`frames` rows), read on perf's own timer, never inside a frame, between `monitor.beginAgent()` and `endAgent()`, so perf never makes the spike it measures. Only frames after its cursor are read; a full window drops its oldest quarter; late GPU times are picked up from the same ring slot. A row's frame time is `max(gap, js + gpu)`, its JS time `workMs − agentMs`. No allocation per read.
- Causes: perf never classifies a frame. The engine's `causes` bits say a frame is a spike and why; perf ranks them gpu › upload › compile › longFrame › js › gc? › gap and writes a one-line `why`.
- The per-frame budget: the engine's `budgetMs` column (one frame of the frame's rate under `renderer.monitor.budgetMs: "rate"`, else the fixed number) and `rateMs` go into every row; a ring without `budgetMs` falls back to `rateMs`.
- Without a monitor (a headless game, an engine before block 2b) perf is off: `status()` answers `{ state: "off", reason: "no-renderer" | "no-monitor" }`, the reads answer empty values, the sources are listed `available: false` (-32008).
- Sources (all `changes: "frame"`, each with a probe): `editor.perf.second` (`PerfSecond`), `editor.perf.window` (`PerfWindowWire`), `editor.perf.spikes` (`PerfSpikeSummary[]`), `editor.perf.spike { frame }` (`PerfSpikeRecord` or `null`), `editor.spikes { lastMs? }` (the MCP mirror). Each watch is isolated: a throw is caught and warned once per streak.
- Runtime-free modules: `perf/protocol/` (section 3b) and `perf/graph/`, the canvas-2D frame graph painter on the structural `GraphContext2D` (`paintGraph`, `createGraphState`, `resetGraphText`, `spikeAt`, `rowAt`, `CAUSE_STYLE`; no DOM type, no Preact, no allocation per paint). The overlay and renderView's device strip paint with it.
- Why perf and recorder are two plugins: perf is the read model of the last 6 s; the recorder is the persistence and outbox pipeline. The bridge depends on the recorder alone; the recorder reaches the monitor through `perf.monitor()` only.
- Events: none. Logs: `perf:off` (info), `perf:started` (debug), `perf:watcher-failed` (warn).

~~~ts
/**
 * perf configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { registry: { game }, perf: { windowMs: 10_000, frames: 2048 } } });
 * ```
 */
export type PerfConfig = {
  /** How often perf reads the ring, ms: 250 (4 Hz; the overlay never repaints faster). 50 to 1000. */
  readEveryMs: number;
  /** The window the graph, the spike index and every spike count cover, ms: 6000. 1000 to 30000. */
  windowMs: number;
  /** Rows perf keeps: at least windowMs at the fastest display (720 at 120 Hz). 1024. 64 to 16384. */
  frames: number;
};

/**
 * The perf API (`app.perf`, `ctx.require(perfPlugin)`): the performance model of the page for the
 * overlay and the recorder. The tools page and MCP read the same through the `editor.perf.*` sources.
 */
export type PerfApi = {
  /**
   * What perf can measure now: on (with frames lost since start and whether the page has a GPU
   * timer), waiting (a monitor without frames yet), or off (no renderer, or an engine without a
   * monitor).
   *
   * @returns The status; a fresh object.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The overlay's Frames tab on a headless test game.
   * app.perf.status(); // { state: "off", reason: "no-renderer" }
   * ```
   */
  status(): PerfStatus;
  /**
   * Hands the last `windowMs` of frames to `visit`, synchronously, once. The window is perf's own
   * state, rewritten by every read (4 Hz): it is valid only inside `visit` — read it there, never
   * write it, never keep the reference (copy the numbers you keep); `version` tells whether it
   * changed since the last paint. Off or waiting: `visit` gets a window with `count` 0.
   * Allocation-free: the caller makes its visitor once (per mount). A throw of `visit` reaches the
   * caller and leaves the window unchanged.
   *
   * @param visit - Called with the live window as a read-only `PerfWindowView`.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The overlay paints its graph on its own timer; the visitor was made once at mount.
   * const paintVisitor = (window: PerfWindowView): void => {
   *   if (window.version !== painted) paintGraph(g, window, view, graphState); // 358 rows at 60 fps
   * };
   * app.perf.readWindow(paintVisitor);
   * ```
   */
  readWindow(visit: (window: PerfWindowView) => void): void;
  /**
   * This second: fps of the window's last second, spikes in the window, the newest frame's budget
   * and the loop's rate, `renderer.stats()`, and the newest sample and screen facts from the
   * engine. Built when asked, cached until the next read, and frozen with its `fps`, `rate`,
   * `render` (and `render.kept`): a write fails and the next `second()` is unchanged.
   *
   * @returns The frozen PerfSecond (the same object until the next read).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The pill: fps now and spikes in the last 6 s.
   * app.perf.second().fps; // { loop: 60, drawn: 54 }
   * app.perf.second().rate; // { fps: 60, mode: "auto", reason: "missed", displayHz: 120, switches: 1 }
   * ```
   */
  second(): PerfSecond;
  /**
   * The spikes of the window, oldest first, each with its primary cause and the one-line why.
   * Copies.
   *
   * @param query - Which spikes: all of the window by default.
   * @param query.lastMs - Only spikes that started that many ms before the newest frame; default and
   *   maximum `windowMs`, a value that is not a finite number counts as `windowMs`.
   * @returns The spike summaries; [] while off.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // MCP: "what stuttered in the last five seconds?"
   * app.perf.spikes({ lastMs: 5000 }); // [{ frame: 4812, ms: 41.3, cause: "upload", path: "garden/boss", … }]
   * ```
   */
  spikes(query?: { readonly lastMs?: number }): readonly PerfSpikeSummary[];
  /**
   * The record of one spike of the window: its numbers from the ring (or, once the slot was
   * overwritten, from the engine's spike line) and, once the spike line arrived, its full detail.
   * Copies.
   *
   * @param frame - The frame number.
   * @returns The record; undefined when the frame is not a spike of the window.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The overlay opens the record of the tapped flag.
   * app.perf.spike(4812)?.why; // "41.0 MB of textures uploaded this frame (bundle garden-boss)"
   * ```
   */
  spike(frame: number): PerfSpikeRecord | undefined;
  /**
   * The engine monitor perf found, for the plugin that logs through it (the recorder).
   *
   * @returns The monitor; undefined when perf is off.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // recorder, at start: subscribe to the log of the page.
   * const off = ctx.require(perfPlugin).monitor()?.stream(line => queue.push(line));
   * ```
   */
  monitor(): MonitorLike | undefined;
};
~~~

### 7.4 recorder — agent, Complex

- depends: `[registryPlugin, perfPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` (checks the config, adds `editor.record`, `editor.mark`, `editor.recorder`), `onStart` (opens the store, subscribes `monitor.stream`, starts the flush timer; `autoStart` starts a log), `onStop` (finishes the running log: stop event, queue drained, pending text written; no emit, no log).
- Pipeline: the stream listener keeps each line as a reference in a ring of 4096 slots (a full ring drops its oldest and counts it); the flush tick (`flushEveryMs`) serializes inside the agent bracket into the log's pending text and the outbox; a chunk is written every `persistEveryMs` or at 64 KB pending, one write in flight per log. Three failed writes in a row move the log to the memory store.
- Log format: one JSON object per line, exactly the engine's `PerfLogLine` v1; file `perf-<yyyymmdd>-<hhmm>-<model>.jsonl`. Order: the context lines (`header`, `startup`, the newest `display`), the `recorder` start event, every stream line, the stop event.
- Store: OPFS (`moku-editor-perf/`, a sub-directory per log with `meta.json` and chunk files `000001.jsonl`, …) when the page has `navigator.storage.getDirectory`, else memory. `keepMb` bounds memory: the oldest finished memory log goes first, then the oldest outbox lines (`recorder:dropped`). `keepFiles` finished logs are kept.
- Share: `share(name)` answers `"shared"` / `"cancelled"` through the native share sheet, else `"downloaded"`; a log over 32 MiB is refused for the native share (an `Error` naming its size): pull it with `moku-editor perf`.
- Outbox: `unsentRun(max)` peeks the oldest unconfirmed lines of one log; `ack(log, next)` confirms below `next` (idempotent, monotonic). The bridge ships with it; the recorder never imports the bridge.
- Monitor events it writes: `devtools { mode, tab }` (hooking the global `overlay:changed`; never `overlay`, which is the game's), `command { id, input, via, ok }` (hooking the registry's per-plugin `registry:command`: every run once, whoever ran it) and `recorder` (start, stop, export). `command(id, input, label)` is the overlay's automatic mark of a press: a mark only, never a second `command` line.
- Registry entries: `editor.record { on: "boolean", label: "string?" }` (cosmetic) → `{ on, file }`; `editor.mark { label: "string" }` (cosmetic) → `{ marked }`; source `editor.recorder` (`changes: "frame"`, no probe) → `status()`.
- Without a monitor `start` throws; earlier logs can still be listed, shared and removed.
- Events: emits `recorder:status` (per-plugin, hooked by overlay and bridge); hooks `overlay:changed` (global), `registry:command` (per-plugin). Logs: `recorder:started`, `recorder:stopped`, `recorder:shared`, `recorder:storage`, `recorder:dropped-log`, `recorder:no-monitor` (info); `recorder:persist-failed`, `recorder:dropped`, `recorder:remove-failed`, `recorder:list-failed`, `recorder:flush-failed`, `recorder:watcher-failed` (warn).

~~~ts
/**
 * recorder configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { registry: { game }, recorder: { autoStart: false, keepMb: 32 } } });
 * ```
 */
export type RecorderConfig = {
  /** Start a log when the plugin starts: a debug build is for measuring, and the bridge ships only what is recorded. true. */
  autoStart: boolean;
  /** Most MB kept in memory: lines the computer has not confirmed, plus the logs of the memory store. 64. 1 to 512. */
  keepMb: number;
  /** How often the queue is serialized, ms: 1000. 100 to 10000. */
  flushEveryMs: number;
  /** How often serialized text is written to the store, ms: 5000; also when 64 KB wait, and at stop. 1000 to 60000. */
  persistEveryMs: number;
  /** "auto": OPFS when the page has it, memory otherwise; "memory": never on disk. */
  storage: "auto" | "memory";
  /** Finished logs kept in the store; the oldest beyond are removed when a log starts. 10. 1 to 100. */
  keepFiles: number;
};

/**
 * One log as the recorder lists it.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const file: LogFileInfo = { name: "perf-20261014-1402-sm-a266b.jsonl", label: "garden, A26",
 *   startedAt: 1792000920000, lines: 9_840, bytes: 2_202_009, sent: 9_840, current: false, storage: "opfs" };
 * ```
 */
export type LogFileInfo = {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly label: string | null;
  /** Epoch ms of the start. */
  readonly startedAt: number;
  readonly lines: number;
  /** UTF-16 code units of the text plus one per newline: the UTF-8 size for ASCII JSON. */
  readonly bytes: number;
  /** Lines of this log the computer confirmed (`ack`). */
  readonly sent: number;
  /** The log being recorded now. */
  readonly current: boolean;
  readonly storage: "opfs" | "memory";
};

/**
 * A mark of the current (or last) log: one the user added, or an automatic one for a game command
 * the overlay ran (then `command` names it).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const mark: LogMark = { atMs: 150_000, label: "Glow off", auto: true, command: { id: "garden.glow", input: { on: false } } };
 * ```
 */
export type LogMark = {
  /** ms since the log started. */
  readonly atMs: number;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly auto: boolean;
  readonly command?: { readonly id: string; readonly input: Json };
};

/**
 * One run of the outbox: the oldest unconfirmed lines of one log, as the bridge sends them in
 * `perf.lines` (spec 01 C8 `PerfLinesParams`). `lines` are the JSON texts the flush already made,
 * one complete object each; the bridge splices them into the message, so the hub receives objects.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const run: OutboxRun = { log: "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", from: 1790, lines: ['{"v":1,"kind":"mark","t":64000.5,"build":"debug-20261014T160000Z","label":"boss","auto":false}'] };
 * ```
 */
export type OutboxRun = {
  /** The log's file name (the hub's `log`). */
  readonly log: string;
  /** Index of `lines[0]` within that log, 0-based, counted when the line was serialized. */
  readonly from: number;
  readonly lines: readonly string[];
};

/**
 * The payload of the recorder's per-plugin event `recorder:status` (registered in
 * `recorder/index.ts`): the state of the log and of the outbox. Emitted on start, stop, share and
 * remove, and after a flush that changed a number (at most once per flushEveryMs).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * ctx.emit("recorder:status", { state: "recording", lines: 1840, bytes: 412_000, sent: 1790, pending: 50 });
 * ```
 */
export type RecorderStatusEvent = {
  readonly state: "idle" | "recording" | "exporting";
  /** Lines of the current log (the last one while idle; 0 before any). */
  readonly lines: number;
  readonly bytes: number;
  /** Lines the computer confirmed since the recorder started. */
  readonly sent: number;
  /** Lines in the outbox, waiting for the computer. */
  readonly pending: number;
};

/**
 * Everything the Record tab shows: the event's numbers plus the log's name, label and age.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.recorder.status(); // { state: "recording", lines: 1840, bytes: 412_000, sent: 1790, pending: 50, monitor: true,
 *                        //   file: "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", label: "garden, A26", sinceMs: 192_000, storage: "opfs", dropped: 0 }
 * ```
 */
export type RecorderStatus = RecorderStatusEvent & {
  /** perf found a monitor: recording is possible. */
  readonly monitor: boolean;
  /** The current log's name (the last one while idle; null before any). */
  readonly file: string | null;
  readonly label: string | null;
  /** ms since the current log started; 0 while idle. */
  readonly sinceMs: number;
  readonly storage: "opfs" | "memory";
  /** Lines dropped since start: the queue overflowed or the outbox passed keepMb. */
  readonly dropped: number;
};

/**
 * What `share` did.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const how: ShareResult = "downloaded";
 * ```
 */
export type ShareResult = "shared" | "cancelled" | "downloaded";

/**
 * The recorder's own events: declared in its `index.ts`, hooked through `depends` (not in
 * `AgentEvents`).
 */
export type RecorderEvents = { readonly "recorder:status": RecorderStatusEvent };

/**
 * The recorder API (`app.recorder`, `ctx.require(recorderPlugin)`): the performance log on the
 * device for the overlay's Record tab, and its outbox for the bridge.
 */
export type RecorderApi = {
  /**
   * Starts a log: writes the context lines (header, startup, newest display) and a `recorder` start
   * event, then every line of the stream until `stop`. While a log runs it answers that log and
   * changes nothing. Removes the oldest finished logs beyond `keepFiles`.
   *
   * @param options - How to start.
   * @param options.label - A name for this run, written into the start event and the file list
   *   (trimmed; empty is no label).
   * @returns The new (or running) log.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] recorder.start: this game has no performance monitor.\n  Run a dev or debug build
   *   of `@moku-labs/game` with the monitor (block 2b).` when perf found none (a lifecycle error).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A tester starts a run on the phone before the boss.
   * app.recorder.start({ label: "garden, A26" }); // { name: "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", current: true, lines: 0, … }
   * ```
   */
  start(options?: { readonly label?: string }): LogFileInfo;
  /**
   * Stops the log: writes the `recorder` stop event, serializes what is queued, writes everything to
   * the store and marks the log finished. When the store fails, the log stays in memory and
   * `recorder:persist-failed` warns.
   *
   * @returns The finished log; undefined when no log was running.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * const file = await app.recorder.stop(); // { name: "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", lines: 1840, bytes: 412_000, current: false, … }
   * ```
   */
  stop(): Promise<LogFileInfo | undefined>;
  /**
   * Writes a mark into the log through the engine (`monitor.mark`), so what follows has a name, and
   * adds it to the marks of the current log.
   *
   * @param label - What follows: "boss enters".
   * @returns True when a log is running and the mark went into it; false while idle, without a
   *   monitor or for an empty label (nothing written).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.recorder.mark("boss enters"); // true; marks() ends with { atMs: 64_000, label: "boss enters", auto: false }
   * ```
   */
  mark(label: string): boolean;
  /**
   * Adds the automatic mark of a game command the overlay ran: while recording, a `mark` line with
   * `label` through the engine (`monitor.mark`) and `{ atMs, label, auto: true, command: { id, input } }`
   * in `marks()`. It writes no `command` event: the registry's `registry:command` (via "overlay")
   * already made the recorder log the run once. Called by the overlay after a press resolved.
   *
   * @param id - The command id.
   * @param input - The input it ran with.
   * @param label - The mark's words, e.g. "Glow off".
   * @returns True when a log is running and the mark went into it; false while idle or without a monitor.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // overlay, after the "Glow" toggle ran with { on: false }:
   * ctx.require(recorderPlugin).command("garden.glow", { on: false }, "Glow off"); // true; marks() ends with the auto mark
   * ```
   */
  command(id: string, input: Json, label: string): boolean;
  /**
   * The state of the log and the outbox, for the Record tab.
   *
   * @returns A fresh RecorderStatus.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.recorder.status().pending; // 50: lines the computer has not confirmed yet
   * ```
   */
  status(): RecorderStatus;
  /**
   * The marks of the current log, or of the last one while idle, in time order.
   *
   * @returns A copy.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.recorder.marks(); // [{ atMs: 64_000, label: "boss enters", auto: false }, { atMs: 150_000, label: "Glow off", auto: true, … }]
   * ```
   */
  marks(): readonly LogMark[];
  /**
   * The logs on this device, oldest first, the current one last. A log a page left "current" when it
   * died lists as finished.
   *
   * @returns A copy.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.recorder.files().map(file => file.name); // ["perf-20261014-1402-sm-a266b.jsonl", "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl"]
   * ```
   */
  files(): readonly LogFileInfo[];
  /**
   * Hands a log to the user: the native share sheet when the shell offers `share`, else a download
   * link (works in a browser, not in a WebView). The current log is written to the store first, so
   * the shared file has every line so far. The status shows `exporting` meanwhile.
   *
   * @param name - The log's file name.
   * @returns "shared" or "cancelled" (share sheet), or "downloaded".
   * @throws {TypeError} For an unknown name (argument validation).
   * @throws {Error} When the page has neither a document nor a native share.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * await app.recorder.share("perf-20261014-1402-sm-a266b.jsonl"); // "shared" on the phone
   * ```
   */
  share(name: string): Promise<ShareResult>;
  /**
   * Removes a finished log from the device.
   *
   * @param name - The log's file name.
   * @throws {TypeError} For an unknown name (argument validation).
   * @throws {Error} For the log being recorded (stop it first).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * await app.recorder.remove("perf-20261014-1402-sm-a266b.jsonl");
   * app.recorder.files().length; // 1
   * ```
   */
  remove(name: string): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * The oldest unconfirmed lines of **one** log (the log of the outbox's oldest line), without taking
   * them: the bridge sends them as `perf.lines { log, from, lines }` and confirms with `ack(log, next)`.
   * A peek, so a lost connection needs nothing: after a reconnect the same run is answered again, and
   * the hub drops what it already has by index. Lines the recorder dropped under `keepMb` leave a jump
   * in the index, which the hub reports as a gap (spec 01 C5).
   *
   * @param max - Most lines to answer (a whole number ≥ 1; anything else counts as 1).
   * @returns The run, a fresh object; undefined when the outbox is empty.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // bridge, with 50 lines of the current log pending:
   * recorder.unsentRun(200); // { log: "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", from: 1790, lines: [ …50 JSON texts ] }
   * ```
   */
  unsentRun(max: number): OutboxRun | undefined;
  /**
   * Confirms every outbox line of `log` whose index is below `next`: the hub took them (its
   * `perf.ack { log, next }`). They leave the outbox and count as sent (for their log and in status).
   * Idempotent and monotonic: an older or repeated ack removes nothing more; an unknown log changes
   * nothing. The status event follows on the next flush tick.
   *
   * @param log - The log's file name, as `unsentRun` gave it.
   * @param next - The hub's next expected index of that log.
   * @throws {TypeError} When `next` is not a whole number from 0 (argument validation).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // bridge, after the hub answered { log, next: 1840, n: 50 }:
   * recorder.ack("perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", 1840);
   * recorder.status().pending; // 0
   * ```
   */
  ack(log: string, next: number): void;
};
~~~

### 7.5 overlay — agent, Complex

- depends: `[registryPlugin, channelPlugin, perfPlugin, recorderPlugin]`; presence check `ctx.has("bridge")` for the Link tab. Lifecycle: `onInit` (checks the config, refusing the old keys `corner` and `open`; adds `editor.overlay`), `onStart` (mounts the host, listeners and observers, sets `globalThis.__MOKU_GAME_OVERLAY__`, applies the start mode over the remembered one), `onStop` (removes them; deletes the global only while it holds this overlay's object).
- Modes: `hidden` (nothing drawn, no tick), `pill` (fps now, the spikes of the last 6 s, link light, REC; a tap opens the card) and `card` (docked left or right, dragged by its grip, snapped inside the safe area; tabs Frames, Game, Record, Link). It remembers place, mode and tab in `localStorage["moku-editor:overlay"]` (`remember`).
- The game opens it: the engine's `debug` plugin calls the global channel (`app.debug.overlay.open({ mode })` / `close` / `toggle` / `isOpen`, `DebugTrigger()`, `config.debug.overlay` applied by `startPage` after the agents). `open({ mode: "pill" })` opens the pill, any other mode the card. No gesture, no debug button of the editor's own.
- Frames tab: the frame graph of the last 6 s painted by `perf/graph` through `perf.readWindow` visitors made once, prev / next spike keys, counters, More, the spike record; the engine fingerprint and build, STALE when the phone's engine differs from the computer's. Game tab: only `overlay: "toggle" | "button"` commands (`commands()`), run with `channel.run(id, input, "overlay")` and marked through `recorder.command`; a command the build refuses is greyed with "needs a --debug=full build". Record tab: the recorder. Link tab: the bridge's `link` from `bridge:status`; Connect / Pair emits `overlay:connect`.
- Cheapness: opaque surfaces only, one canvas, one `setInterval(PAINT_MS)`, no `requestAnimationFrame`, one 120 ms slide, every render and paint between `monitor.beginAgent()` and `endAgent()`; a hidden page stops the tick.
- Fonts: three woff2 faces in `fonts/` (Barlow Condensed 500 and 600, Barlow 500, SIL OFL 1.1), subset by `bun run fonts:overlay` to the glyphs the overlay prints; registered at the first visible mode. The tools build copies the same files.
- Registry command: `editor.overlay`, title `Overlay in game`, input `{ mode: "string" }`, effect `cosmetic`, value `{ mode }` (the mode after the call); a mode other than `"hidden"`, `"pill"`, `"card"` answers -32602; the old `{ on }` is refused.
- Events: emits `overlay:changed` (global; the recorder logs it as `devtools`) and `overlay:connect` (global; the bridge dials it); hooks `bridge:status` (global) and `recorder:status` (per-plugin). Logs: `overlay:mount-missing`, `overlay:no-dom`, `overlay:paint-failed`, `overlay:command-failed` (warn); `overlay:storage-failed`, `overlay:fonts-unavailable` (debug).

~~~ts
/**
 * The tick: numbers, text and canvas change at most 4 times a second.
 */
export const PAINT_MS = 250;

/**
 * The one-shot slide when the card or the pill opens, ms.
 */
export const SLIDE_MS = 120;

/**
 * How long a toast line stays, ms.
 */
export const TOAST_MS = 3000;

/**
 * Card width, CSS px.
 */
export const CARD_W = 344;

/**
 * Card width on a viewport narrower than `COMPACT_BELOW`, CSS px.
 */
export const CARD_W_COMPACT = 300;

/**
 * Viewport CSS width below which the card is compact.
 */
export const COMPACT_BELOW = 384;

/**
 * Card height, CSS px: `min(CARD_H, max(CARD_H_MIN, round(0.45 × viewport height)))`.
 */
export const CARD_H = 372;

/**
 * The least card height (a landscape phone), CSS px.
 */
export const CARD_H_MIN = 240;

/**
 * Pill width, CSS px.
 */
export const PILL_W = 138;

/**
 * Pill height, CSS px; its hit area extends 5 px on every side.
 */
export const PILL_H = 36;

/**
 * Space between the window and the top / bottom safe inset, CSS px.
 */
export const EDGE_GAP = 8;

/**
 * Pointer travel in CSS px before a grip press counts as a drag.
 */
export const DRAG_SLOP = 4;

/**
 * CSS px one arrow key moves the window.
 */
export const KEY_STEP = 16;

/**
 * localStorage key of the remembered window.
 */
export const STORE_KEY = "moku-editor:overlay";

/**
 * z-index of the host.
 */
export const Z_INDEX = 2_147_483_000;

/**
 * The attribute that marks the host element. It lives in the protocol, so the bridge's tap watch
 * reads the same marker; re-exported here for `Overlay.*`.
 */
export { HOST_ATTRIBUTE } from "../registry/protocol";

/**
 * The three modes of the window: nothing drawn, the small pill, the card.
 */
export type OverlayMode = "hidden" | "pill" | "card";

/**
 * The two visible modes; `open({ mode })` takes one of them.
 */
export type VisibleMode = "pill" | "card";

/**
 * The tabs of the card. "game" exists only when the game registered overlay commands.
 */
export type OverlayTab = "frames" | "game" | "record" | "link";

/**
 * The screen edge the window docks to.
 */
export type Dock = "left" | "right";

/**
 * The payload of `overlay:changed`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const changed: OverlayChanged = { mode: "card", tab: "frames" };
 * ```
 */
export type OverlayChanged = { readonly mode: OverlayMode; readonly tab: OverlayTab };

/**
 * Overlay configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { registry: { game }, overlay: { mode: "pill", dock: "left" } } });
 * ```
 */
export type Config = {
  /**
   * Mode at start when the device remembers none (or `remember` is false). The engine's
   * `config.debug.overlay` opens the window later through `__MOKU_GAME_OVERLAY__.open({ mode })`.
   * Default "hidden".
   */
  mode: OverlayMode;
  /** Edge the window docks to until the person drags it. Default "right". */
  dock: Dock;
  /** Remember place, mode and tab on the device (localStorage). Default true. */
  remember: boolean;
  /** CSS selector of the element the host is appended to; undefined = document.body. */
  mount: string | undefined;
};

/**
 * One command of the game shown on the Game tab.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const glow: OverlayCommand = { id: "garden.glow", title: "Glow", kind: "toggle", value: false, effect: "cosmetic", allowed: true, reason: undefined };
 * ```
 */
export type OverlayCommand = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly kind: "toggle" | "button";
  /** A toggle's current value (`value(app)` of the engine command); undefined for a button. */
  readonly value: boolean | undefined;
  readonly effect: Effect;
  /** False when this build refuses it (a route / cheat / raw command on a `--debug` page). */
  readonly allowed: boolean;
  /** Why not, when not allowed: "needs a --debug=full build". */
  readonly reason: string | undefined;
};

/**
 * The object the overlay sets as `globalThis.__MOKU_GAME_OVERLAY__` (engine spec 12 H4.1).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // The engine's app.debug.overlay.toggle() calls it.
 * globalThis.__MOKU_GAME_OVERLAY__?.toggle();
 * ```
 */
export type OverlayChannel = {
  open(options?: { mode?: "pill" | "card" }): void;
  close(): void;
  toggle(): void;
  isOpen(): boolean;
};

/**
 * The overlay api (`app.overlay`): the editor's window over the running game. The engine's
 * `app.debug.overlay.*` reaches it through `globalThis.__MOKU_GAME_OVERLAY__`; the tools page and
 * MCP through the `editor.overlay` command.
 */
export type OverlayApi = {
  /**
   * Shows the window: the card, or the pill with `{ mode: "pill" }`; `tab` picks the card's tab
   * ("game" falls back to "frames" when the game registered no overlay commands). Slides in once
   * (120 ms) when it was hidden, or from the pill to the card. Emits `overlay:changed` when the
   * mode or the tab changed. Before start it only records the mode; `onStart` applies it over the
   * remembered one. Idempotent.
   *
   * @param options - The visible mode and the tab.
   * @param options.mode - "pill" or "card" (default "card").
   * @param options.tab - The card's tab (default: the current one).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A game's own "Perf" button in its debug menu, through the engine's app.debug.overlay.open():
   * app.overlay.open({ mode: "pill" });
   * app.overlay.mode(); // "pill"
   * ```
   */
  open(options?: { readonly mode?: VisibleMode; readonly tab?: OverlayTab }): void;
  /**
   * Hides the window: nothing of the editor stays on the game, the tick stops. Emits
   * `overlay:changed` when it was visible. Idempotent.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Before a screenshot of the game alone.
   * app.overlay.close();
   * app.overlay.isOpen(); // false
   * ```
   */
  close(): void;
  /**
   * Hidden → the last visible mode (the card by default); pill or card → hidden.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Five taps on the version line (the engine's DebugTrigger) call this through app.debug.overlay.toggle().
   * app.overlay.toggle();
   * app.overlay.mode(); // "card" the first time; "pill" when the pill was the last visible mode
   * ```
   */
  toggle(): void;
  /**
   * Whether the window shows, as the pill or the card.
   *
   * @returns True for "pill" and "card".
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.overlay.isOpen(); // false on a fresh start with nothing remembered
   * ```
   */
  isOpen(): boolean;
  /**
   * The current mode.
   *
   * @returns "hidden", "pill" or "card".
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The window was collapsed to the pill with its header key.
   * app.overlay.mode(); // "pill"
   * ```
   */
  mode(): OverlayMode;
  /**
   * The game's commands marked for the overlay, in manifest order, with a toggle's value read now.
   * Empty: the card has no Game tab.
   *
   * @returns Fresh copies.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A Memory Missing on a `--debug` (read-only) build.
   * app.overlay.commands().map(command => [command.id, command.value, command.allowed]);
   * // [["garden.glow", false, true], ["garden.fog", false, true], ["story.skipDialogue", undefined, false]]
   * ```
   */
  commands(): readonly OverlayCommand[];
};
~~~

### 7.6 bridge — agent, Complex, opt-in

- depends: `[registryPlugin, channelPlugin, recorderPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` (`checkConfig`, adds `editor.reload` and `editor.clock`), `onStart` (`startBridge`: reads the remembered links, decides the mode, connects without awaiting), `onStop` (`stopBridge`: `bye`, close 1000).
- Modes (decided at start, first match wins): device when `__MOKU_GAME_EDITOR__` is a non-empty string (a debug build's `--editor`), when config `device` is set, on a page URL that is not http(s) (`tauri://localhost`, `file:`) or is the native WebView's own host (`http://tauri.localhost`), or with no page URL and a `hello` that is not an absolute http(s) URL; else page mode (a headless agent in Bun whose `hello` names its server too). A remembered address (`localStorage["moku-editor:link"]`, at most four) wins over `device` and the build's; an address `parseAddress` refuses is skipped (`bridge:bad-address`). `connect(address)` and `overlay:connect` switch to device mode.
- Device connect: no hello fetch; `ws://<address>{path}/ws?kind=agent&role=device` plus `&device=&token=` with credentials. Without them the socket pairs: a four-digit code from `crypto.getRandomValues` (kept across retries), `pair { code, device: { model?, os?, engine?, build? } }` first, `bridge:status` with `link: { mode: "connecting", address, pairing: { code } }`; `paired { device, token, engine }` stores the credentials and runs the link step (hello, heartbeat, shipping). A 4401 `unpaired` on a credentialed socket drops them and pairs at once; 1008 `pairing refused` stops retrying until `connect()`. Until the computer first answers a hello with a `session`, the first failure of a streak logs `bridge:no-computer` at info; in device mode the streak and its backoff start over only on a `session`, so a hub that closes every link before it cannot cycle the phone faster than the backoff.
- Log shipping (device mode, while open): `recorder.unsentRun(linesPerBatch)` goes out as `perf.lines { log, from, lines }` (the recorder's JSON texts spliced in, so the hub receives objects), one batch in flight; every `perf.ack { log, next, n }` goes to `recorder.ack(log, next)`; no ack within `callTimeoutMs` stalls shipping on that link (`bridge:lines-unacked`). At-least-once: the hub drops what it already has.
- Every connect starts a new generation (`dial`): a hello answer or failure that arrives after a newer connect opens nothing and fails nothing.
- Backoff with defaults and `random() = 0.5`: 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 30000, 30000.
- Lost reasons: `no WebSocket in this runtime` (no retry), `no page URL for <hello>` (no retry), `pairing refused` (no retry), `no socket URL for <address>` (no retry), `hello unreachable`, `hello <status>`, `hello answered without ws and token`, `hello answered a bad ws URL`, `socket failed`, `socket closed (<code>)[: <reason>]`, `stopped` (no retry).
- Taps: a `pointerdown` on the page window sends the `tap { x, y, at }` notification (page CSS px, `at` = `performance.now()`), at most one per 50 ms, passive, never for events inside the overlay host. The tools page draws a ripple at the tap point.
- Commands `editor.reload` (`{ restore: "boolean?" }`, default true, effect `route`, MCP `moku_reload`): with restore it stores the checkpoint below exactly as on `bun:beforeFullReload`, answers `{ scheduled: true }`, sends `bye` and calls `location.reload()` on the next macrotasks; `restore: false` skips the checkpoint. `editor.clock` (`{}`, read): `{ frame, paused, held, reasons }`.
- Long calls: a `run` of `editor.series` waits `min(input.durationMs, 60000)` and a `run` of `editor.sheet` `min(input.frames × input.everyMs, 60000)` on top of `callTimeoutMs` (`deadlineFor`).
- Checkpoint across Bun's reload (round 2 R6): on `import.meta.hot.on("bun:beforeFullReload")` the bridge runs `game.bookmark` synchronously through the registry door and stores `{ v: 1, doc, at, frame, paused, bookmark }` in `sessionStorage["moku-editor:checkpoint"]` (`paused` is the devtools pause only, `clock.held`). On start it restores a stored checkpoint (`game.restore`, then `game.pause` when it was paused), removes it, and only then connects: its first hello carries `manifest.restored = { bookmark, frame }`. A checkpoint older than 30 s or malformed is dropped; a failed restore logs `bridge:restore-failed` and workspace's D-07 restore is the fallback.
- A hub `run` request reaches the registry with `via: "bridge"`.
- Events: emits `bridge:status` (global; `link` in device mode only, at most once a second for `seenAt` alone); hooks `overlay:connect` (global) and `recorder:status` (per-plugin). Logs: `bridge:connected`, `bridge:no-computer`, `bridge:paired`, `bridge:unpaired`, `bridge:restored` (info), `bridge:lost` (warn then debug), `bridge:pairing-refused`, `bridge:bad-address`, `bridge:lines-unacked` (warn), `bridge:disabled`, `bridge:connect-crashed`, `bridge:request-crashed` (error), others at debug.

~~~ts
export type { DeviceLink } from "../hub/protocol";

/**
 * Default first reconnect delay (config `retryMs`).
 */
export const DEFAULT_RETRY_MS = 1000;

/**
 * Default deadline of one hub request (config `callTimeoutMs`).
 */
export const DEFAULT_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000;

/**
 * Cap of the reconnect backoff.
 */
export const MAX_RETRY_MS = 30_000;

/**
 * Backoff jitter: ±20 %.
 */
export const JITTER = 0.2;

/**
 * Buffered bytes above which the socket counts as congested (1 MiB).
 */
export const HIGH_WATER = 1_048_576;

/**
 * Buffered bytes below which the backlog is flushed (256 KiB).
 */
export const LOW_WATER = 262_144;

/**
 * Cap of the extension of a long call (R1: the same rule in bridge, hub and link).
 */
export const DEADLINE_EXTRA_CAP_MS = 60_000;

/**
 * The long call that waits its `durationMs` on top.
 */
export const SERIES_ID = "editor.series";

/**
 * The long call that waits its `frames × everyMs` on top (the contact sheet).
 */
export const SHEET_ID = "editor.sheet";

/**
 * The command the bridge adds to the registry: store the checkpoint and reload the page.
 */
export const RELOAD_ID = "editor.reload";

/**
 * The computer address when nothing else names one: adb reverse to the hub's device port (engine
 * spec 10 default of `--editor`).
 */
export const DEFAULT_DEVICE_ADDRESS = "127.0.0.1:47600";

/**
 * Default of config `linesPerBatch`.
 */
export const DEFAULT_LINES_PER_BATCH = 200;

/**
 * Upper bound of config `linesPerBatch`.
 */
export const MAX_LINES_PER_BATCH = 1000;

/**
 * While linked in device mode, at most one `bridge:status` per this many ms for a `seenAt` change
 * alone.
 */
export const SEEN_EMIT_MS = 1000;

/**
 * The `localStorage` key of the remembered links.
 */
export const PAIRING_STORE_KEY = "moku-editor:link";

/**
 * Most remembered addresses; the oldest is dropped.
 */
export const MAX_REMEMBERED = 4;

/**
 * The hub's 1008 close reason after the person refused the pairing: no retry.
 */
export const PAIRING_REFUSED = "pairing refused";

/**
 * Bridge configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ plugins: [bridgePlugin], pluginConfigs: { bridge: { device: "192.168.1.5:47600" } } });
 * ```
 */
export type BridgeConfig = {
  /**
   * Hello route of the editor server (page mode): same-origin path or absolute URL. Non-empty. Its
   * path, with the last segment replaced by `ws`, is also the socket path in device mode.
   */
  hello: string;
  /** First reconnect delay in ms; doubles per failure up to MAX_RETRY_MS. Integer ≥ 100. */
  retryMs: number;
  /**
   * Deadline of one hub request in ms; a run of editor.series or editor.sheet waits longer (R1).
   * Also the deadline of one `perf.lines` acknowledgement. Integer ≥ 100.
   */
  callTimeoutMs: number;
  /**
   * Device mode at this computer address (`host:port`). Undefined: mode and address follow the
   * remembered address, `__MOKU_GAME_EDITOR__` and the page URL.
   */
  device: string | undefined;
  /** Most log lines in one `perf.lines` message. Integer 1–1000. */
  linesPerBatch: number;
};

/**
 * The credentials the hub gave this device for one address (`paired`). Never logged.
 */
export type RememberedLink = { readonly device: string; readonly token: string };

/**
 * What `localStorage["moku-editor:link"]` holds (JSON, `v: 1`). Never logged.
 */
export type RememberedLinks = {
  readonly v: 1;
  /** The address the person chose or paired last. */
  last: string | undefined;
  /** address → the hub's device id and token; at most MAX_REMEMBERED, insertion order = age. */
  links: Record<string, RememberedLink>;
};

/**
 * The bridge api (`app.bridge`): the state of the link from the game page to the editor server,
 * and the switch to another computer in device mode.
 */
export type BridgeApi = {
  /**
   * The link status: connecting before the socket opens, live or paused from the channel
   * heartbeat while open, lost with the reason and the retry delay after a failure, lost
   * "stopped" after stop. Never `silent` or `empty`: those are tools-side kinds.
   *
   * @returns A fresh LinkStatus.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A dev entry shows the editor link next to the fps counter.
   * app.bridge.status(); // { kind: "connecting" } right after start, then { kind: "live", frame: 12 }
   * ```
   */
  status(): LinkStatus;
  /**
   * The session id the hub gave this page after its hello (R6).
   *
   * @returns The id, or undefined before it arrives and after the socket closes.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Wait for the editor server to accept the page.
   * app.bridge.session(); // "s-7f3a" once the hub answered; undefined before and after stop
   * ```
   */
  session(): string | undefined;
  /**
   * The device link as the overlay's Link tab shows it: no computer, connecting (with the pairing
   * code while the computer has not confirmed), live over adb (a loopback address) or live over the
   * LAN. The same object the last `bridge:status` carried as `link`, as a fresh copy.
   *
   * @returns The link, or undefined in page mode (a page the dev server served).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A debug build on a phone, waiting for the person to type the code on the computer.
   * app.bridge.link(); // { mode: "connecting", address: "192.168.1.5:47600", pairing: { code: "4821" } }
   * ```
   */
  link(): DeviceLink | undefined;
  /**
   * Dials another computer: switches to device mode at `address`, remembers it as the last address
   * on the device, closes the current socket (1000 "switch") and connects now with the failure
   * streak reset. Remembered credentials for that address are used; without them the bridge pairs.
   * The same as the event `overlay:connect { address }`. Calling it with the address that is
   * already live does nothing.
   *
   * @param address - `host:port`, e.g. "192.168.1.5:47600"; `[v6]:port` for IPv6.
   * @throws {TypeError} `[moku-editor] bridge.connect needs host:port, got "<address>".` for an
   *   address `parseAddress` refuses (argument validation); nothing changes then.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The phone moves from the USB cable to the office Wi-Fi.
   * app.bridge.connect("192.168.1.5:47600");
   * app.bridge.link(); // { mode: "connecting", address: "192.168.1.5:47600" } until the socket opens
   * ```
   */
  connect(address: string): void;
};
~~~

### 7.7 capture — agent, Standard, opt-in

- depends: `[registryPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `createState`, `onInit` (adds four commands), `onStop` (ends a running series). No app api.
- Commands: `editor.capture` (`{ maxWidth: "number?", key: "string?", rect: "json?", format: "string?", quality: "number?" }`, effect `read`, value `Shot`; JPEG 0.8 by default, `key` (through `game.locate`/`game.rect`) or `rect` crops plus 8 px, unknown key -32602; `png` keeps the lossless path; a picture that fails to decode stays PNG), `editor.series` (`{ durationMs: "number", intervalMs: "number" }`, effect `read`, value `SeriesValue`), `editor.seriesStop` (`{}`, effect `read`, value `{ stopped: boolean }`), `editor.sheet` (`{ frames: "number", everyMs: "number", maxWidth: "number?", format: "string?", quality: "number?" }`, effect `read`, value `Sheet`, JPEG by default).
- Every shot runs the door command `game.capture` (needs `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__`). The picture is the PNG data URL the door answers (game 0.1) or the string `png` of `{ png, legend? }` (game 0.4); anything else is -32000 "gave no picture". A series plans `max(1, floor(durationMs / intervalMs))` shots, never overlapping, one series at a time.
- `maxWidth` (a whole number 64–4096, else -32602 field `maxWidth`): a wider picture is shrunk in the page to `maxWidth` pixels wide, aspect kept (`createImageBitmap`, then an `OffscreenCanvas` or a canvas element, PNG data URL). A page that cannot do it answers the full picture and logs `capture:downscale-failed`.
- `editor.sheet` runs `game.capture { sheet: { frames, everyMs } }` once (game ≥ 0.4: the game lays the frames out in `ceil(sqrt(frames))` columns) and shrinks the sheet to `maxWidth`. `frames` is a whole number 2–12, `everyMs` a number 1–5000, else -32602 naming the field. `frame` is the frame after the last picture. MCP `moku_series` sends `maxWidth: 1080`.
- Events: none. Logs: `capture:series-large`, `capture:shots-skipped`, `capture:downscale-failed` (warn).

~~~ts
/**
 * A plan above this many shots logs `capture:series-large` and still runs.
 */
export const WARN_SHOTS = 200;

/**
 * The door command every shot runs.
 */
export const CAPTURE_ID = "game.capture";

/**
 * The id of the one-shot command, named in its errors.
 */
export const SHOT_ID = "editor.capture";

/**
 * The id of the contact-sheet command, named in its errors.
 */
export const SHEET_ID = "editor.sheet";

/**
 * The fewest pictures a contact sheet takes (the game's own limit).
 */
export const MIN_SHEET_FRAMES = 2;

/**
 * The most pictures a contact sheet takes (the game's own limit).
 */
export const MAX_SHEET_FRAMES = 12;

/**
 * The shortest game time between two pictures of a contact sheet, in ms.
 */
export const MIN_SHEET_EVERY_MS = 1;

/**
 * The longest game time between two pictures of a contact sheet, in ms.
 */
export const MAX_SHEET_EVERY_MS = 5000;

/**
 * The smallest `maxWidth` editor.capture and editor.sheet accept, in pixels.
 */
export const MIN_MAX_WIDTH = 64;

/**
 * The largest `maxWidth` editor.capture and editor.sheet accept, in pixels.
 */
export const MAX_MAX_WIDTH = 4096;

/**
 * Capture configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ plugins: [capturePlugin], pluginConfigs: { capture: { maxDurationMs: 10_000 } } });
 * ```
 */
export type Config = {
  /** Longest series accepted, in ms. Default 20000. */
  maxDurationMs: number;
  /** Shortest interval accepted, in ms. Default 16. */
  minIntervalMs: number;
};

/**
 * The game page viewport of a shot (not the tools-side DeviceSpec).
 */
export type Device = {
  readonly w: number;
  readonly h: number;
  readonly orientation: "portrait" | "landscape";
};

/**
 * Value of `editor.capture`.
 */
export type Shot = { readonly image: string; readonly frame: number; readonly device: Device };

/**
 * Value of `editor.sheet`: the contact sheet (one JPEG or PNG data URL), the frame of the last picture and
 * the device.
 */
export type Sheet = { readonly image: string; readonly frame: number; readonly device: Device };

/**
 * One shot of a series, tagged with its real frame and real time.
 */
export type SeriesShot = { readonly image: string; readonly frame: number; readonly atMs: number };

/**
 * Value of `editor.series` (R2).
 */
export type SeriesValue = { readonly shots: readonly SeriesShot[]; readonly device: Device };
~~~

### 7.8 files — server, Standard

- depends: none (first server plugin). Lifecycle: `onInit` (`validateFilesConfig`), `onStart` (opens the project index of the root, not awaited; `find` waits for it), `onStop` (ends the watch, closes the index, state off `"stopped"`, nothing emitted).
- Node built-ins only; no `Bun.*`. Limits (`io.ts`): `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` 2 MiB, `MAX_BINARY_BYTES` 16 MiB, `MAX_PATH_LENGTH` 1024. Image extensions: `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.webp`, `.gif`.
- Sandbox order: lexical → deny → allow (files only; image and `.moku/captures/` rules for binaries) → real path under the real root → kind.
- `writeDataUrl(path, dataUrl)` decodes the files-channel data URL (`decodeDataUrl` in `binary.ts`, not exported from the plugin) for `hub`.
- Project index (D-38, D-40, D-48): `openProject({ root })` of `@moku-labs/game/project`; its watch emits every batch of file changes. The index is the only source of code locations; off is an error state, not a fallback. On: `defs` (every key but `jsx:` → def paths), `uses` (`node:`/`style:` keys → use paths), `broken` (path → first parse error), `manifest`, `revision`, `previous`, `change`. Off reasons: `"disabled"` (`project: false`), `"@moku-labs/game 0.7.0 or newer is needed for the project index"`, the bare message of a rejected open (no `typescript`, bad root), `"not opened"` before start, `"stopped"` after stop.
- `find(key)` (files channel `find { key }`): the `ProjectFound[]` of a key, `line` and `range` read from disk now, `hash` = the `version` of `read`, `broken: true` when the file does not parse now; answers outside the sandbox are dropped; `[]` for an unknown key; key over 512 chars -32602; index off -32008 `"project index off: <reason>"`. `project()` is the last state. The editor's own writes are not fed to the index; other tabs hear them through the next watch batch.
- Version check (D-45): `write(path, text, version)` compares the version right before the rename, after the temp file is written; a conflict removes the temp file and rejects -32005. An external write between that hash and the rename is still overwritten (window narrowed, not closed).
- Engine fingerprint (engine spec 10 E2): `engine()` answers the computer's `EngineInfo` `{ id, version, dist, patch? }` of the `@moku-labs/game` the root resolves (`id` `"unknown"` when none); `refreshEngine()` reads it again (the hub calls it after a pairing). The hub publishes it as `editor.engine`; a phone's `__MOKU_GAME_ENGINE__` that differs reads STALE.
- Events: emits `files:written`, `files:project`. Logs: `files:emit-failed`, `files:project-on { files, keys, ms }` (info; the bin prints it), `files:project-off { reason }` (error, once).

~~~ts
/**
 * Resolved config of the files plugin. Shallow-merged; arrays replace the default entirely.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { files: { root: `${import.meta.dir}/..` } } });
 * ```
 */
export type FilesConfig = {
  /** Project root. Absolute, or relative to process.cwd() at init. Default ".". */
  root: string;
  /** Globs (relative to root, posix) a file must match to be read or written. */
  allow: readonly string[];
  /** Globs that are never listed, read or written. Matched case-insensitively. */
  deny: readonly string[];
  /** Open the project index of the root on start. `false` leaves it off as `"disabled"`. */
  project: boolean;
};

/**
 * What a write was about, classified from its path.
 */
export type WrittenKind = "code" | "style" | "layout" | "capture" | "other";

/**
 * Payload of the global server event `files:written`.
 */
export type FilesWritten = {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly bytes: number;
  readonly kind: WrittenKind;
};

/**
 * The files api (`app.files`, `ctx.require(filesPlugin)`). Every rejection is an
 * `Error & WireError` built with the protocol's wireError.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const { text, version } = await app.files.read("features/ui/styles.ts");
 * ```
 */
export type FilesApi = {
  /**
   * Lists the direct children of a folder inside the project root.
   *
   * @param dir - Relative folder path; `""` or `"."` for the root.
   * @returns Folders first, then allowed files, each sorted by path. `size` is 0 for folders.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path` when a sandbox rule refuses the path, -32601
   * `unknown_id` when the folder is missing.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The files panel opens the `src/nodes` folder of the tree.
   * await app.files.list("src/nodes"); // [{ path: "src/nodes/await-intent.ts", kind: "file", size: 812 }, …]
   * ```
   */
  list(dir: string): Promise<FileEntry[]>;

  /**
   * Reads a regular file as UTF-8 (invalid bytes become U+FFFD) with its version: the lowercase
   * hex sha1 of the bytes. Max 2 MiB.
   *
   * @param path - Relative file path.
   * @returns `{ text, version }`.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path`, -32601 `unknown_id` when missing, -32000 over 2 MiB.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Load a style file before editing it; keep the version for the save.
   * const { text, version } = await app.files.read("features/ui/styles.ts");
   * ```
   */
  read(path: string): Promise<FileText>;

  /**
   * Atomic text write. Missing parent folders are created inside the root. Emits `files:written`
   * after the rename. Max 2 MiB.
   *
   * @param path - Relative file path.
   * @param text - The new content.
   * @param version - Optional version from the last read; a stale one fails with -32005.
   * @returns `{ path, bytes, version }` of the written file.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path`, -32005 `version_conflict` when the file changed
   * meanwhile, -32602 `invalid_input` (`field: "text"`) over 2 MiB.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Save the edited text only if nobody changed the file since it was read.
   * const { version } = await app.files.read("features/ui/styles.ts");
   * await app.files.write("features/ui/styles.ts", edited, version); // { path, bytes, version }
   * ```
   */
  write(path: string, text: string, version?: string): Promise<WriteResult>;

  /**
   * Atomic image write, only under `.moku/captures/` and only for png, jpg, jpeg, webp and gif.
   * Missing parent folders are created. Emits `files:written` with `kind: "capture"`. Max 16 MiB.
   *
   * @param path - Relative capture path.
   * @param bytes - The image bytes.
   * @returns `{ path, bytes, version }` of the written image.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path` outside `.moku/captures/` or without an image
   * extension, -32602 `invalid_input` (`field: "data"`) over 16 MiB.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Store a board screenshot the capture panel took.
   * await app.files.writeBinary(".moku/captures/2026-10-05/0846-board.png", bytes);
   * ```
   */
  writeBinary(path: string, bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<WriteResult>;

  /**
   * Decodes a `data:image/(png|jpeg|webp|gif);base64,…` URL and writes the image with
   * `writeBinary`. The mime must match the extension of `path`. Same limits, errors and event as
   * `writeBinary`.
   *
   * @param path - Relative capture path; its extension must match the mime of the data URL.
   * @param dataUrl - The image as a base64 data URL.
   * @returns `{ path, bytes, version }` of the written image.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path` for a path that is not an image, outside
   * `.moku/captures/`; -32602 `invalid_input` (`field: "data"`) for a data URL that is not a
   * base64 image, a mime that does not match the path, or over 16 MiB.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // hub serves the files-channel `writeBinary { path, data }` of a tools page.
   * const files = ctx.require(filesPlugin);
   * await files.writeDataUrl(".moku/captures/2026-10-05/f12-full.jpg", "data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQ…");
   * // { path: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/f12-full.jpg", bytes: 48213, version: "3f7a…" }
   * ```
   */
  writeDataUrl(path: string, dataUrl: string): Promise<WriteResult>;

  /**
   * Reads an image back as a data URL with its version (R3). Emits nothing. Max 16 MiB.
   *
   * @param path - Relative image path.
   * @returns `{ dataUrl, version }`.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path` without an image extension, -32601 `unknown_id` when
   * missing, -32000 over 16 MiB.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Show a stored capture again.
   * const { dataUrl } = await app.files.readBinary(".moku/captures/2026-10-05/0846-board.png");
   * // dataUrl: "data:image/png;base64,…"
   * ```
   */
  readBinary(path: string): Promise<FileBinary>;

  /**
   * Synchronous full sandbox check, as for a write. A missing file gives the path it would have.
   *
   * @param path - Relative file path.
   * @returns The real absolute path.
   * @throws {Error} -32004 `forbidden_path` when a sandbox rule refuses the path.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Turn a project path into the absolute path an "Open in editor" link needs.
   * app.files.resolve("src/main.ts"); // "/home/dev/game/src/main.ts"
   * ```
   */
  resolve(path: string): string;

  /**
   * The real, symlink-resolved project root (R3), for "Open in editor" links.
   *
   * @returns The absolute root.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // pages puts the root into the tools boot JSON.
   * const files = ctx.require(filesPlugin);
   * const boot = { root: files.root() }; // { root: "/home/dev/game" }
   * ```
   */
  root(): string;

  /**
   * Where a key of the project index lives, with lines read from the files on disk now. Waits
   * for the open that started with the app. Answers the files the sandbox lets it read only.
   *
   * @param key - A project-index key, at most 512 characters: `node:board/merge`,
   *   `jsx:settingsBoard`, `textStyle:ui.title`, `style:features/ui/popup.tsx#popupScreen`.
   * @returns One answer per place, in the index's order; `[]` for a key the index does not know.
   *   `hash` equals the `version` of `read`; `broken` when the file does not parse now.
   * @throws {Error} -32602 `invalid_input` (`field: "key"`) for a key that is not a string or is
   *   too long, -32008 `not_installed` (`project index off: <reason>`) while the index is off.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // hub serves the files-channel `find { key }` of a tools page.
   * const files = ctx.require(filesPlugin);
   * await files.find("node:main/open"); // [{ path: "features/settings/nodes.ts", binding: "open", line: 3, … }]
   * ```
   */
  find(key: string): Promise<ProjectFound[]>;

  /**
   * The project state last announced with `files:project`: on with its revision and key maps, or
   * off with a reason (`"not opened"` before start, `"disabled"`, `"stopped"`, why the open failed).
   *
   * @returns The state.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A server plugin checks the index before it answers a location.
   * const state = ctx.require(filesPlugin).project();
   * if (state.state === "on") state.defs["node:board/merge"]; // ["nodes/merge.ts"]
   * ```
   */
  project(): ProjectState;

  /**
   * The engine of this computer's project: the installed `@moku-labs/game`, by the recipe of the
   * engine's `__MOKU_GAME_ENGINE__` (version + hash of its dist and patch). Computed on start;
   * `refreshEngine()` renews it. The hub publishes it as `editor.engine`.
   *
   * @returns The fingerprint; `{ id: "unknown", … }` when the game is not installed under the root.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] files.engine() needs a started app.` before the first start (a
   * lifecycle error).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The perf command prints the computer's engine next to each phone's.
   * editor.files.engine().id; // "0.14.12+9c41e0"
   * ```
   */
  engine(): EngineInfo;

  /**
   * Computes the fingerprint again when the last run is older than 2 s (ENGINE_REFRESH_MS), else
   * answers the kept one. The hub calls it when a device pairs or reconnects (a reinstall during a
   * long perf run).
   *
   * @returns The fingerprint, fresh or kept.
   * @throws {Error} The `engine()` lifecycle error before the first start.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The hub, when a phone pairs: publish the engine again only when its id changed.
   * const info = await ctx.require(filesPlugin).refreshEngine(); // { id: "0.14.13+1ab7f2", version: "0.14.13", dist: "1ab7f2…" }
   * ```
   */
  refreshEngine(): Promise<EngineInfo>;
};
~~~

### 7.9 hub — server, Complex

- depends: `[filesPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` (validate config, allowed origins), `onStart` (new token, silent check every `min(1000, silentAfterMs / 2)` ms, publishes `files.engine()` as `engine`), `onStop` (tears device mode down without emit, closes every socket with 1001 `editor stopping`).
- `serve` throws: before start, on a second call, with a `websocket` option, with `unix` or `tls`, with a hostname other than `127.0.0.1`/`localhost`, with a game route under the editor path.
- Guard modes: `upgrade` (Origin required), `same-origin` (Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site checked when present), `navigate`.
- Session choice for a game request without `session`: one open session wins; with several, the only embedded one wins; else -32003.
- Heartbeats (with a well-formed `heap` kept) and `tap { x, y, at }` notifications are forwarded to every tools connection with `session`. A malformed heartbeat, value or tap is one strike; ten strikes close with 1008.
- Liveness readout (M4): each `SessionInfo` of `sessions()` and of the `sessions` notification carries `heartbeat: { frame, paused, silent }` once the session has sent a heartbeat. The list is re-sent when a session's `paused` or `silent` flips, not on every frame.
- Manifest hash (D-37): on `hello` the hub sets `manifestHash = commandsHash(manifest)` on the session; every `SessionInfo` of `sessions()` and of the `sessions` notification carries it. The MCP bridge rebuilds its door tools only when it moves. A refused command (`allowed: false`) hashes with its `reason`, so a read-only build's hash differs from the dev page's.
- Deadline of a forwarded call: `callTimeoutMs`, plus `input.durationMs` for a `run` of `editor.series` and `input.frames × input.everyMs` for a `run` of `editor.sheet`, capped at +60 s (the same rule as bridge and link).
- `publish(method, params)`: `hotReload`, `selection`, `project` and `engine` go to every tools connection now as `editor` notifications; the last value per method is kept and replayed right after each tools hello.
- Project index: hooks `files:project` and publishes it as the `editor` notification `project`. The files channel routes `find { key }` to `files.find` (missing key -32602). The MCP bridge ignores `editor.project`.
- Device mode (`listenDevices({ confirm, routes? })`, the `moku-editor perf` command): an adb listener on `127.0.0.1:<devicePort>` (the tools page and `{path}/ws`) and, with `deviceLan`, a LAN listener on `<lanAddress>:<devicePort>` (`{path}/ws` only). A device upgrade needs `kind=agent role=device`, a Host of the listener and an Origin in `deviceOrigins`. Without credentials the socket pairs: `pair { code, device }` first within 5 s (`PAIR_FIRST_MS`), the person confirms (`confirm(request, signal)`, one ticket at a time; an adb phone under `pairing: "lan"` at once), then `paired { device, token, engine }`. A stale token is upgraded and closed 4401 `unpaired`. A paired socket is an ordinary agent session with `SessionInfo.device` plus `perf.lines` (checked: `log` `^[\w.-]{1,128}$`, `from` a safe integer, 1–5000 lines; duplicates below the next index skipped, a jump forward is a `gap`), always answered with `perf.ack { log, next, n }`. Limits: 16 paired devices, 4 waiting pairings, 4 open pairing sockets per address (429 `busy`), a 10 s cooldown after a refusal, 32 logs per device. `stopDevices()` emits `closed` per device, then `stopped`.
- Runtime-free `hub/protocol/`: the device-link types and their parsers (section 3), imported by bridge and overlay as `../hub/protocol`, never the hub index.
- Events: emits `hub:session` (global) and `hub:device` (per-plugin: `listening`, `connected`, `lines`, `closed`, `stopped`; the collector hooks it); hooks `files:project`. Logs: `hub:started`, `hub:refused`, `hub:session-open`, `hub:session-silent`, `hub:session-alive`, `hub:emit-failed`, `hub:devices-on`, `hub:devices-off`, `hub:paired`, `hub:pair-refused`, `hub:pair-failed`, `hub:device-unpaired`, `hub:engine-refresh-failed`, debug lines.

~~~ts
/**
 * Hub configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { hub: { devicePort: 47600, deviceLan: true } } });
 * ```
 */
export type HubConfig = {
  /** URL prefix of every editor route. Starts with "/", no trailing slash. */
  path: string;
  /**
   * Extra exact origins allowed to upgrade and to call same-origin routes (normal and adb
   * listener; never devices).
   */
  allowOrigins: readonly string[];
  /** Deadline of a forwarded call before it fails with -32002 (retryable). */
  callTimeoutMs: number;
  /** A session with no heartbeat for this long is marked silent (65 s after a paused beat, R6). */
  silentAfterMs: number;
  /** Port of the device listeners (127.0.0.1 and, with deviceLan, the LAN address); 0 = a random free port. */
  devicePort: number;
  /** Also listen on the computer's LAN address (device upgrades only, pairing confirmed by the person). */
  deviceLan: boolean;
  /** The LAN address to bind; undefined picks the first non-internal IPv4 (en*, wl*, eth* first). */
  lanAddress: string | undefined;
  /** Exact Origins a device's WebView sends (scheme + host, lower case). */
  deviceOrigins: readonly string[];
  /** "lan": only LAN phones are asked, an adb phone is confirmed at once; "always": every phone is asked. */
  pairing: "lan" | "always";
  /** How long a pairing waits for the person before it is refused, in ms. */
  pairTimeoutMs: number;
};

/**
 * Payload of the global server event `hub:session`, and params of the `session` notification.
 */
export type HubSession = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly game: string;
  readonly open: boolean;
  readonly reason?: "bye" | "game_reloaded";
};

/**
 * Editor routes registered through addRoutes (pages) and merged by serve.
 */
export type EditorRoutes = Readonly<Record<string, Response | RouteHandler>>;

/**
 * Which request check guard applies (R3).
 */
export type GuardMode = "upgrade" | "same-origin" | "navigate";

/**
 * What the game passes to serve(). Unknown keys pass through to Bun untouched.
 */
export type ServeOptions = {
  readonly port?: number;
  readonly hostname?: string;
  readonly development?: boolean | { readonly hmr?: boolean; readonly console?: boolean };
  readonly routes?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  readonly fetch?: (req: Request, server: HubServer) => Response | Promise<Response>;
  /** Refused at runtime too: the editor owns the one websocket handler. */
  readonly websocket?: undefined;
  readonly [key: string]: unknown;
};

/**
 * A method `publish` sends to the tools pages (R6, A5): `"hotReload"`, `"selection"`, `"project"`
 * or `"engine"`, the keys of the protocol's PublishParams. The hub publishes `project` (from
 * `files:project`) and `engine` (from `files.engine()`) itself. The protocol's PublishMethod,
 * re-exported under hub's name.
 */
export type { PublishMethod } from "../registry/protocol";

/**
 * What the CLI's pairing callback is asked: the code the phone shows (to compare with what the
 * person types), what the phone is and where it came from.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const request: PairRequest = { code: "4821", model: "SM-A266B", address: "192.168.1.23", link: "lan", engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z" };
 * ```
 */
export type PairRequest = {
  /** The code the phone shows, to compare with what the person types. */
  readonly code: string;
  /** The normalized model, e.g. "SM-A266B"; null when the phone sent none. */
  readonly model: string | null;
  /** The phone's address as the hub saw it. */
  readonly address: string;
  readonly link: DeviceLinkKind;
  /** The phone's engine fingerprint, as it reported it. */
  readonly engine: string | null;
  /** The phone's build id, as it reported it. */
  readonly build: string | null;
};

/**
 * Asks the person whether a phone may link. Resolves true to pair it. The signal aborts when the
 * phone leaves, the wait runs out or device mode stops; the answer is then ignored. A throw or a
 * rejection counts as a refusal.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const confirm: PairConfirm = async (request, signal) =>
 *   (await ask(`${request.model ?? "A phone"} at ${request.address} asks to link. Type its code: `, signal)) === request.code;
 * ```
 */
export type PairConfirm = (request: PairRequest, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<boolean>;

/**
 * Options of `listenDevices`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const options: DeviceListenOptions = { confirm: askInTerminal, routes: { "/": new Response("No game is served here.") } };
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceListenOptions = {
  /** The pairing callback (the CLI's terminal prompt). */
  readonly confirm: PairConfirm;
  /** Non-editor routes of the adb listener (e.g. "/" for a page that says no game is served here). */
  readonly routes?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
};

/**
 * Where device mode listens.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const listen: DeviceListen = { port: 47600, adb: "127.0.0.1:47600", lan: "192.168.1.5:47600" };
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceListen = {
  /** The real port of both listeners (the random one under `devicePort: 0`). */
  readonly port: number;
  /** The loopback listener, `127.0.0.1:<port>`. */
  readonly adb: string;
  /** The LAN listener, `<address>:<port>` (IPv6 in brackets); null without deviceLan. */
  readonly lan: string | null;
};

/**
 * A paired device as the hub reports it: a frozen copy, never the token.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const device: LinkedDevice = { id: "d-7f3a", model: "SM-A266B", link: "adb", address: "127.0.0.1", port: 47600, engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z", pairedAt: 1791986083963, online: true };
 * ```
 */
export type LinkedDevice = SessionDevice & {
  /** Epoch ms of the pairing. */
  readonly pairedAt: number;
  /** Whether a connection is open now. */
  readonly online: boolean;
};

/**
