 * A batch of a device's log, as the hub accepted it.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const lines: DeviceLines = { log: "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", from: 200, rx: 1791986090000, items: [], gap: 0, rejected: 0 };
 * ```
 */
export type DeviceLines = {
  /** The device log's name ("perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl"). */
  readonly log: string;
  /** Index of the first item in that log (after duplicates were skipped). */
  readonly from: number;
  /** Computer epoch ms when the batch arrived. */
  readonly rx: number;
  /**
   * The accepted PerfLogLine v1 objects, frozen. The hub's shallow guard vouches for `v` (a finite
   * number) and `kind` (1–32 characters) only, not a line's body: a reader switches on `kind` and
   * reads the fields it needs defensively.
   */
  readonly items: readonly PerfLogLine[];
  /** Lines the device lost before sending (from − next). */
  readonly gap: number;
  /** Items dropped as malformed. */
  readonly rejected: number;
};

/**
 * Why a device connection ended: a bye, a lost socket, a newer connection of the same device, or
 * device mode stopping.
 */
export type DeviceCloseReason = "bye" | "lost" | "replaced" | "stopped";

/**
 * Payload of the per-plugin event `hub:device`: device mode listening, a device connected, a log
 * batch, a device left, device mode stopped.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const event: HubDeviceEvent = { kind: "connected", device: { id: "d-7f3a", model: "SM-A266B", link: "adb", address: "127.0.0.1", port: 47600, engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z", pairedAt: 1791986083963, online: true } };
 * ```
 */
export type HubDeviceEvent =
  | { readonly kind: "listening"; readonly listen: DeviceListen }
  | { readonly kind: "connected"; readonly device: LinkedDevice }
  | { readonly kind: "lines"; readonly device: LinkedDevice; readonly lines: DeviceLines }
  | { readonly kind: "closed"; readonly device: LinkedDevice; readonly reason: DeviceCloseReason }
  | { readonly kind: "stopped" };

/**
 * The hub's per-plugin events, visible to plugins that list `hubPlugin` in `depends`.
 */
export type HubEvents = { readonly "hub:device": HubDeviceEvent };

/**
 * The hub api (`app.hub`, `ctx.require(hubPlugin)`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * Bun.serve(app.hub.serve({ port: 3000, routes: { "/": index }, fetch: serveAsset }));
 * ```
 */
export type HubApi = {
  /**
   * Wraps the game's `Bun.serve` options: `127.0.0.1` forced, then the game's routes, the routes
   * from `addRoutes` and `{path}/ws` merged, and the websocket handler added. Without a game
   * `fetch` the fallback answers 404. Unknown option keys pass through to Bun.
   *
   * @param options - The game's serve options.
   * @returns Options ready for `Bun.serve`.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] …` before start, on a second call, with a `websocket`, `unix` or
   * `tls` option, with a hostname other than `127.0.0.1` / `localhost`, and with a game route
   * under the editor path.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The game's dev server: one Bun.serve for the game and the editor, after await app.start().
   * Bun.serve(app.hub.serve({ port: 3000, routes: { "/": index }, fetch: serveAsset }));
   * ```
   */
  serve(options: ServeOptions): BunServeOptions;

  /**
   * The token of this start: 32 random bytes, base64url, 43 characters. A new one on every
   * start. Never logged.
   *
   * @returns The token.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] hub.token() needs a started app.` before start and after stop.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // pages puts the token into the tools boot JSON on every page request.
   * const hub = ctx.require(hubPlugin);
   * const token = hub.token(); // 43 characters, e.g. "Hk3…"
   * ```
   */
  token(): string;

  /**
   * A fresh list of the open game sessions ordered by `connectedAt`. Each carries `manifestHash`,
   * the `commandsHash` of its manifest computed on hello (D-37). A session that has sent a
   * heartbeat carries the readout `heartbeat: { frame, paused, silent }`; a device session (a paired
   * phone) carries `device` with the device listener's port. Mutating the result does not change
   * the next call.
   *
   * @returns The open sessions.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // After the game page connected its bridge and sent its first heartbeat.
   * app.hub.sessions(); // [{ id: "s-7f3a", game: "merge-game 0.0.0", page: "http://127.0.0.1:3000/", embedded: true, connectedAt: 1790000000000, manifestHash: "4f528e73", heartbeat: { frame: 1840, paused: false, silent: false } }]
   * // A paired phone's session adds: device: { id: "d-7f3a", model: "SM-A266B", link: "adb", address: "127.0.0.1", port: 47600, engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z" }
   * ```
   */
  sessions(): SessionInfo[];

  /**
   * The `{path}/ws` upgrade handler; `serve` already mounts it. Checks the path (404), the start
   * (503), the upgrade request (426), `guard(…, "upgrade")` (403), the token (401), the kind and
   * the role (400: `role=page` only with `kind=tools`), then upgrades.
   *
   * @param req - The request.
   * @param server - The Bun server.
   * @returns `undefined` after an upgrade, else the plain-text refusal.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A game with its own Bun.serve mounts the upgrade itself.
   * Bun.serve({
   *   fetch: (req, server) => app.hub.fetch(req, server) ?? new Response("upgraded"),
   *   websocket: app.hub.websocket
   * });
   * ```
   */
  fetch(req: Request, server: HubServer): Response | undefined;

  /**
   * The one websocket handler of the server: 32 MiB frames, 60 s idle, no deflate.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A game's own Bun.serve passes the editor's handler on.
   * Bun.serve({
   *   fetch: (req, server) => app.hub.fetch(req, server) ?? new Response("upgraded"),
   *   websocket: app.hub.websocket
   * });
   * ```
   */
  readonly websocket: HubWebSocketHandler;

  /**
   * Registers editor routes, merged by `serve` and by the adb listener of `listenDevices` (R3).
   * Call it in `onInit`. Keys are checked first, so a refused batch registers nothing.
   *
   * @param routes - Routes keyed by `path` or under `path + "/"`.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] …` after `serve` or `listenDevices`, on a key registered before,
   * on `{path}/ws`, and on a key outside the editor path.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // pages registers its routes in onInit, before hub.serve() freezes them.
   * const hub = ctx.require(hubPlugin);
   * hub.addRoutes({ [`${hub.path()}/hello`]: helloRoute });
   * ```
   */
  addRoutes(routes: EditorRoutes): void;

  /**
   * The shared Host / Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site check (R3). `upgrade` requires an allowed Origin;
   * `same-origin` and `navigate` check it when present; `same-origin` also wants Sec-Fetch-Site
   * `same-origin` or `none` when present. The origin `null` never matches.
   *
   * @param req - The request.
   * @param server - The Bun server (its port).
   * @param mode - Which rules apply.
   * @returns A 403 response, or `undefined` when allowed.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A pages route refuses a cross-site request before it answers.
   * const refused = ctx.require(hubPlugin).guard(req, server, "same-origin");
   * if (refused) return refused; // 403 "forbidden"
   * ```
   */
  guard(req: Request, server: HubServer, mode: GuardMode): Response | undefined;

  /**
   * Sends server state to every tools page as the editor-channel notification `<method>` and
   * keeps it: a tools page that connects later gets the last value right after its
   * `sessions {list}`. Works before start too; the value waits for the first tools page. The value
   * is stored through `toWireValue`. A `null` selection goes out as a `selection` notification
   * without params (the wire refuses null params).
   *
   * @param method - The state: `"hotReload"`, `"selection"`, `"project"` or `"engine"`.
   * @param params - Its value: a HotReload, a SelectionInfo or null for the selection, a
   * ProjectState (the hub publishes `project` itself from `files:project`), or an EngineInfo (the
   * hub publishes `engine` itself from `files.engine()` on start and when a phone pairs).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // pages tells every tools page whether Bun reloads the game page on a save.
   * ctx.require(hubPlugin).publish("hotReload", { hmr: true, owner: "bin" });
   * // each tools socket gets {"jsonrpc":"2.0","channel":"editor","method":"hotReload","params":{"hmr":true,"owner":"bin"}}
   * ```
   */
  publish<M extends PublishMethod>(method: M, params: PublishParams[M]): void;

  /**
   * Closes every open socket, agent, tools and device, with one code and reason (a phone reconnects
   * with its device token), and resolves when Bun
   * reported every close (at most 500 ms). The hub keeps running: the token stays, and each
   * connection is forgotten when Bun reports its close, so its session or subscriptions end as on
   * any close. Clients reconnect on their own. Stop a server only after it resolves: a stop before
   * drops the close frame, and the client sees 1006 instead of the code.
   *
   * @param code - The close code: 1012 (service restart) for the bin's restart.
   * @param reason - The close reason the clients see.
   * @returns When every socket closed, or the wait ran out.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The bin, right before Bun's stop on a Hot reload switch (pages serve.ts).
   * await editor.hub.closeAll(1012, "editor restarting");
   * // the bridge and every tools page see close 1012 "editor restarting", log it at info and reconnect
   * ```
   */
  closeAll(code: number, reason: string): Promise<void>;

  /**
   * The editor path, `config.path` (R3).
   *
   * @returns The URL prefix of every editor route.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // pages keys its routes under the hub path.
   * ctx.require(hubPlugin).path(); // "/__editor"
   * ```
   */
  path(): string;

  /**
   * Turns device mode on: listens on 127.0.0.1:<devicePort> (the editor routes, the tools page and
   * the socket) and, with deviceLan, on the LAN address (device upgrades only). Phones connect as
   * `kind=agent role=device` from a deviceOrigins Origin and pair through `confirm`. Freezes the
   * editor routes. Emits `hub:device { kind: "listening" }`.
   *
   * @param options - The pairing callback and extra non-editor routes of the adb listener.
   * @returns The real port and the two addresses.
   * @throws {Error} The two-line `[moku-editor] …` lifecycle errors before start, when device mode
   * is on already, when deviceLan finds no LAN address, on a route under the editor path, and when
   * the port is in use (the error keeps `code: "EADDRINUSE"`).
   * @throws {TypeError} When `options.confirm` is not a function.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // moku-editor perf --lan, after await editor.start().
   * const listen = await editor.hub.listenDevices({ confirm: askInTerminal });
   * // { port: 47600, adb: "127.0.0.1:47600", lan: "192.168.1.5:47600" }
   * ```
   */
  listenDevices(options: DeviceListenOptions): Promise<DeviceListen>;

  /**
   * Turns device mode off: pending pairings are refused, device connections close with 1001
   * "device mode off", device tokens are forgotten, both listeners stop. Emits `closed` per
   * connected device, then `stopped`. A call while device mode is off does nothing. The editor
   * routes stay frozen.
   *
   * @returns When both listeners stopped (at most 500 ms).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The perf command's Ctrl+C turns phones off before it stops the editor.
   * await editor.hub.stopDevices();
   * editor.hub.devices(); // []
   * ```
   */
  stopDevices(): Promise<void>;

  /**
   * The paired devices of this device-mode run, ordered by pairedAt, as fresh frozen copies
   * without tokens.
   *
   * @returns The devices; [] while device mode is off.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // After a Galaxy A26 paired over adb reverse.
   * editor.hub.devices(); // [{ id: "d-7f3a", model: "SM-A266B", link: "adb", address: "127.0.0.1", port: 47600, engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z", pairedAt: 1791986083963, online: true }]
   * ```
   */
  devices(): LinkedDevice[];
};
~~~

### 7.10 collector — server, Complex

- depends: `[filesPlugin, hubPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` (checks the config; registers the mark route `{path}/perf/mark` on every server, before `serve()` or `listenDevices()` freeze the routes), no `onStart` (nothing runs before `hub:device { kind: "listening" }`), `onStop` (clears the adb and throttle timers, marks every log done, awaits every queue bounded by 2 s; a queue still running is recorded as `stopTimedOut`).
- One JSONL file per device log, `perf-<yyyymmdd-hhmm>-<model>.jsonl` under `out`: every line the hub hands over is appended with `rx` (the computer's epoch ms at receipt); a reconnect with the token appends to the same file; one write queue per log, at most 8 MiB waiting (`QUEUE_MAX_BYTES`; beyond, lines are dropped and counted `lost`); at most 32 live logs per device (`MAX_LIVE_LOGS`). A device gap becomes one `gap` line.
- adb, only while device mode is on: every `reverseEveryMs` `adb devices` and `adb -s <serial> reverse tcp:<port> tcp:<port>`; every `everyS` seconds `dumpsys battery` + `dumpsys thermalservice` (a `thermal` line, `source: "collector"`) and `dumpsys gfxinfo <appId>` (`<appId>.debug` preferred when installed; a `gfx` line). Collector lines carry `t` on the phone's page clock and `rx` on the computer's. Without adb: `collector:adb-missing` once, no reverse, no heat or gfx lines; a LAN phone still logs.
- Clean text: every phone string passes `cleanText` (`perf/protocol/text.ts`: C0, C1, DEL and bidi controls dropped, 128 characters) before the editor shows it; the file keeps the lines as sent.
- The computer mark: `mark(label)` writes `{ v: 1, kind: "mark", t, build, rx, label, auto: false, from: "computer" }` into every live log and answers how many got it; the route `POST {path}/perf/mark` (hub guard same-origin, `authorization: Bearer <hub token>` compared timing-safe, plain-text body at most 4 KiB, label 1–200 characters) answers `{"marked":<n>}`; `moku-editor perf mark` posts it.
- `settled()` resolves when every step queued before the call is done (writes, closes, the `collector:session` that follows): the perf command awaits it between `hub.stopDevices()` and `editor.stop()`.
- Runtime-free `collector/report/` (imports only `perf/protocol` and its own files): `parsePerfLog`, `isPerfLog`, `bucketUpper`, `histPercentile`, `gfxPercentile`, `summarize` (one row per screen and rate; pool trims, warm-ups and the game's overlay changes per screen), `compare` / `COMPARE_THRESHOLD` (▲/▼ at ±10 %), `table`, `summaryText`, `compareText`, `primaryOf`, `headerRate`, `rankCauses`. pages' `perf summary` / `perf compare` print them.
- Events: emits `collector:session` (per-plugin: the first written batch at once, then at most once a second per log, and after `away` / `done`; pages hooks it); hooks the hub's `hub:device`. Logs: `collector:reversed`, `collector:adb-missing`, `collector:adb-ambiguous`, `collector:reverse-failed` (info); `collector:write-failed`, `collector:queue-full`, `collector:log-cap` (warn, once per streak).

~~~ts
/**
 * Collector configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { collector: { out: "logs/perf", everyS: 5, appId: "com.example.garden" } } });
 * ```
 */
export type CollectorConfig = {
  /** Folder of the logs: relative to the files root, or absolute. Created on the first log. */
  out: string;
  /** Seconds between two adb readings (heat, system frames) of a phone. 1–3600. */
  everyS: number;
  /** Milliseconds between two `adb devices` + `adb reverse` rounds. ≥ 500. */
  reverseEveryMs: number;
  /** The adb command (a name on PATH or a path). */
  adb: string;
  /** The longest one adb command may run before it is killed. ≥ 500. */
  adbTimeoutMs: number;
  /**
   * The Android package of the game (its base identifier). The collector prefers `<appId>.debug` when
   * the phone has it (the debug build installs beside the store build), else `<appId>`. Undefined: no
   * gfx lines.
   */
  appId: string | undefined;
};

/**
 * The newest second of a device log, for a live line.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const last: SessionDigest = { t: 5917.4, path: "garden/boss", fps: 118, loopFps: 120, p90Ms: 9.1, gpuMs: 4.8, rate: 120, spikes: 1, causes: ["upload"], thermal: { status: 1, batteryC: 36.1 }, model: "SM-A266B", backend: "webgpu", engine: "0.14.12+9c41e0", build: "debug-20261014T160000Z" };
 * ```
 */
export type SessionDigest = {
  /** Page epoch ms of the newest sample. */
  readonly t: number;
  /** Flow path of the newest sample. */
  readonly path: string;
  /** Frames drawn per second (whole number). */
  readonly fps: number;
  /** Loop frames per second (whole number). */
  readonly loopFps: number;
  /** p90 of the loop gap of the newest second (its `gapMs.p90`), null when not measured. */
  readonly p90Ms: number | null;
  /** p50 GPU ms of the newest second, null without a GPU timer. */
  readonly gpuMs: number | null;
  /**
   * The loop's rate in fps now (the newest `rate` event's `to`, else the header's `rate.fps`, else
   * `header.config.maxFps` when > 0); null when unknown.
   */
  readonly rate: number | null;
  /** Spikes of the newest second. */
  readonly spikes: number;
  /** Primary causes of the spikes of the last 6 s, most frequent first. */
  readonly causes: readonly PerfCause[];
  /** The newest heat reading (device shell or adb). */
  readonly thermal: {
    readonly status: number | string | null;
    readonly batteryC: number | null;
  } | null;
  readonly model: string;
  readonly backend: "webgpu" | "webgl" | "none" | null;
  readonly engine: string | null;
  readonly build: string | null;
};

/**
 * What the adb loop knows of one phone.
 */
export type AdbPhone = {
  readonly serial: string;
  /** getprop ro.product.model, normalized; null until read. */
  model: string | null;
  reversed: boolean;
  /** The resolved app package, re-read after 60 s. */
  package: { name: string | null; at: number } | undefined;
  /** The previous gfxinfo reading. */
  gfx: { totals: GfxTotals; at: number } | undefined;
};

/**
 * Payload of the collector's per-plugin event `collector:session`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * ctx.emit("collector:session", { device, file: "/game/.moku/perf/perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", state: "live", lines: 1840, lost: 0, last: null });
 * ```
 */
export type CollectorSessionEvent = {
  readonly device: LinkedDevice;
  readonly file: string;
  /** live: the phone is connected; away: it left and may come back; done: device mode stopped. */
  readonly state: "live" | "away" | "done";
  readonly lines: number;
  readonly lost: number;
  readonly last: SessionDigest | null;
};

/**
 * The collector's per-plugin events, visible to plugins that list `collectorPlugin` in `depends`.
 */
export type CollectorEvents = { readonly "collector:session": CollectorSessionEvent };

/**
 * A log as the API reports it (fresh copy).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const info: CollectorSessionInfo = { device, log: "perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", file: "/game/.moku/perf/perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl", state: "done", lines: 1840, lost: 0, last: null, stopTimedOut: false };
 * ```
 */
export type CollectorSessionInfo = {
  readonly device: LinkedDevice;
  readonly log: string;
  readonly file: string;
  readonly state: "live" | "away" | "done";
  readonly lines: number;
  readonly lost: number;
  readonly last: SessionDigest | null;
  /**
   * True when the app stopped while this log was still being written (onStop's 2 s bound ran out);
   * its last lines may be missing from the file. False otherwise.
   */
  readonly stopTimedOut: boolean;
};

/**
 * What the adb loop sees now.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const status: AdbStatus = { state: "on", phones: [{ serial: "R5CX30ABCDE", model: "SM-A266B", reversed: true }] };
 * ```
 */
export type AdbStatus = {
  readonly state: "off" | "on" | "missing";
  readonly phones: readonly {
    readonly serial: string;
    readonly model: string | null;
    readonly reversed: boolean;
  }[];
};

/**
 * The collector api (`app.collector`, `ctx.require(collectorPlugin)`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * await editor.collector.mark("boss"); // 1
 * ```
 */
export type CollectorApi = {
  /**
   * Every device log of this run, oldest first, as fresh copies. Still answers after `stop()`: a
   * log whose writes outlived onStop's 2 s flush bound carries `stopTimedOut: true` (teardown
   * cannot log it, so this is where it shows).
   *
   * @returns The logs; [] before any phone sent a line.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The perf command, after Ctrl+C, prints the summary of each file written in this run.
   * editor.collector.sessions().map(session => session.file);
   * // ["/game/.moku/perf/perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl"]
   * ```
   */
  sessions(): CollectorSessionInfo[];

  /**
   * Writes a mark from the computer into every live log: `{ v: 1, kind: "mark", t, build, rx,
   * label, auto: false, from: "computer" }`, with `t` on that log's page clock. The label is
   * trimmed.
   *
   * @param label - 1–200 characters after trimming.
   * @returns How many logs got the mark (0 when no phone is live).
   * @throws {TypeError} `[moku-editor] collector.mark: the label must be 1-200 characters.` with the
   * fix `Give a short name, for example "boss".` for an empty or long label.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // `moku-editor perf mark "boss"` reaches this through the mark route.
   * await editor.collector.mark("boss"); // 1
   * ```
   */
  mark(label: string): Promise<number>;

  /**
   * The adb loop now: off while device mode is off, missing when adb could not run, else the
   * phones it sees.
   *
   * @returns A fresh status.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The perf command names the phones whose port it reversed.
   * editor.collector.adb(); // { state: "on", phones: [{ serial: "R5CX30ABCDE", model: "SM-A266B", reversed: true }] }
   * ```
   */
  adb(): AdbStatus;

  /**
   * Resolves when every step queued on a log before the call is done: its writes, the close of
   * its file and the `collector:session` that follows. After `hub.stopDevices()` that is every
   * log's `done` event, which the collector emits from the log's queue a few ticks after the hub's
   * `stopped`. Resolves at once when nothing is pending.
   *
   * @returns When the logs' queues have drained.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The perf command's Ctrl+C: device mode off, every done line printed, then the editor stops.
   * await editor.hub.stopDevices();
   * await editor.collector.settled(); // each log's collector:session { state: "done" } went out
   * await editor.stop();
   * ```
   */
  settled(): Promise<void>;
};
~~~

### 7.11 pages — server, Complex

- depends: `[filesPlugin, hubPlugin, collectorPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` only (`initPages`: check config, find the built page, `hub.addRoutes`).
- Routes (`P = hub.path()`): `P` → 308 to `P/`; `P/` → tools page with the boot tag (503 when not built or before start); `P/hello` → `HelloBody` JSON (same-origin); `P/hmr` → `HotReload` JSON on GET, a change on POST `{ hmr: boolean }` with `Authorization: Bearer <boot.token>` (200 with the state afterwards: the asked state when the bin switches, the unchanged one for a refused change, which the caller compares with what it asked, round 2b R16; 400 for a bad body; 401 without the token); `P/assets/*` → hashed assets, immutable cache. With `toolsPage: false` (`moku-editor perf --no-ui`) `P`, `P/` and `P/assets/*` answer 404 after the guard.
- Hot reload (D-23, round 2 R6): the bin serves with `development: { hmr: true, console: true }` (`--no-hmr`: `hmr: false`) and calls `attachServer(options)` right after `Bun.serve`. `hotReload()` is `{ hmr, owner }`, owner `"server"` with `hmr: false` until `attachServer`. Bun 1.3.14 cannot apply `development.hmr` on `server.reload` (spike in the pages README), so the bin passes `attachServer(options, restart)` and `setHotReload(on)` restarts its server with HMR flipped on the same port (D-32, `serve.ts`: stop bounded to 500 ms, then, only before a server with HMR, a wait of at most 5 s until Bun's bundler is idle (D-57, `waitForBundler`: an empty in-memory `Bun.build` that Bun queues behind a page rebundle still in flight; a wait that is cut or fails is one warning and the restart goes on), then `Bun.serve`); it answers true, sets and publishes the asked state at once and restarts after the answer went out (A1); a failure logs `pages:hot-reload-restart-failed`, publishes the old state and serves the old options again. A game's own server answers false.
- Boot tag: `<script type="application/json" id="moku-editor-boot">` with `ToolsBoot` `{ v: 1, ws, token, path, title, editorUrl, gameUrl, root }`.
- `PAGE_CSP` (exported from `routes.ts`): `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; worker-src 'self' blob:; img-src 'self' data: blob:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'self' ws://127.0.0.1:* ws://localhost:*; frame-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`.
- Home of the `moku-editor` bin, its `mcp` and `mcp-config` subcommands, the `.moku/editor.json` discovery file and the stdio MCP bridge in `mcp/`, and of the perf CLI in `perf/` (`perf`, `perf mark`, `perf summary`, `perf compare`; see "Bin" in section 6). `attachPerf(output)` (called once by `runPerf` after `hub.listenDevices`) makes each `collector:session` print the live lines through the bin's console.
- Events: hooks the collector's per-plugin `collector:session`. Logs: `pages:not-built` (warn at init, error at first request), `pages:hot-reload` (info, `attachServer`), `pages:hot-reload-read-only` (info, a refused change).

~~~ts
/**
 * Pages configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { pages: { editorUrl: "cursor://file/{path}:{line}", toolsPage: false } } });
 * ```
 */
export type PagesConfig = {
  /** Tools page <title> and boot title. */
  title: string;
  /** "Open in editor" link template (D-08): {path} absolute file path, {line} 1-based line. */
  editorUrl: string;
  /** Folder with the built tools page; undefined = dist/tools next to the module. */
  pageDir: string | undefined;
  /** Same-origin URL of the game page the tools page embeds (R3). */
  gameUrl: string;
  /** Serve the tools page and its assets; false answers 404 there (moku-editor perf --no-ui). */
  toolsPage: boolean;
};

/**
 * The server the bin attaches: Bun's Server is one. Pages reads nothing of it; a Hot reload switch
 * goes through the bin's restart, which reaches the current server (A9).
 */
export type AttachedServer = {
  /** The real port, undefined for a unix socket. */
  readonly port?: number | undefined;
  /**
   * Stops the server.
   *
   * @param closeActiveConnections - True closes the open connections at once.
   * @returns Resolves once the server stopped.
   */
  stop(closeActiveConnections?: boolean): Promise<void>;
};

/**
 * The bin's restart (D-32): stops its game server and serves these options on the same port. The
 * hub keeps running, so its token stays. Rejects when the new server cannot start.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const restart: RestartServer = next => game.restart(next);
 * await restart({ ...options, development: { hmr: false, console: true } });
 * ```
 */
export type RestartServer = (options: BunServeOptions) => Promise<void>;

/**
 * The pages api (`app.pages`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * Object.keys(app.pages.routes()); // ["/__editor", "/__editor/", "/__editor/hello", "/__editor/hmr", "/__editor/assets/*"]
 * ```
 */
export type PagesApi = {
  /**
   * A copy of the routes this plugin registered with the hub in onInit, keyed by URL path under
   * the hub path.
   *
   * @returns The five routes `P`, `P/`, `P/hello`, `P/hmr` and `P/assets/*`.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Check which editor URLs the server answers.
   * Object.keys(app.pages.routes()); // ["/__editor", "/__editor/", "/__editor/hello", "/__editor/hmr", "/__editor/assets/*"]
   * ```
   */
  routes(): EditorRoutes;
  /**
   * Tells pages that the moku-editor bin serves the game with these options: the bin owns hot
   * reload from now on, HMR is read from `options.development`, and the state goes to every tools
   * page through `hub.publish("hotReload", …)`. With `restart`, `setHotReload` can switch HMR by
   * restarting the server (D-32). The bin calls it right after its first `Bun.serve`.
   *
   * @param options - The options it was started with (the result of `hub.serve`).
   * @param restart - Stops the bin's current server and serves new options on the same port.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The bin, after it started the game server.
   * const options = editor.hub.serve({ port, development: { hmr: true, console: true }, routes });
   * const game = createGameServer(options, (code, reason) => editor.hub.closeAll(code, reason), {
   *   warn: message => ui.warn(message)
   * });
   * editor.pages.attachServer(options, next => game.restart(next));
   * editor.pages.hotReload(); // { hmr: true, owner: "bin" }
   * ```
   */
  attachServer(options: BunServeOptions, restart?: RestartServer): void;
  /**
   * The hot reload state: whether Bun reloads the game page on a source change, and who owns the
   * server. A game's own `Bun.serve` (no `attachServer` call) is owner "server" with HMR off.
   *
   * @returns A fresh `{ hmr, owner }`.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A game's own dev server that never attached it.
   * app.pages.hotReload(); // { hmr: false, owner: "server" }
   * ```
   */
  hotReload(): HotReload;
  /**
   * Asks for Bun HMR on or off, and publishes the state. Bun cannot switch HMR on a running
   * server, so the bin's server restarts with HMR flipped on the same port (D-32): the asked state
   * is set and published at once, and the restart runs after the answer went out (A1). A failed
   * restart is logged, the old state is published again and the old options are served again. A
   * game's own server always answers false; a bin attached without a restart answers true only
   * when its HMR already equals `on`.
   *
   * @param on - The asked value.
   * @returns True when the bin owns the server and its HMR equals `on` or is switching to it; false
   * otherwise (a game's own server always answers false).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The bin serves with HMR on; the tools page asks for it off.
   * await editor.pages.setHotReload(false); // true: the server restarts without HMR
   * editor.pages.hotReload(); // { hmr: false, owner: "bin" }
   * ```
   */
  setHotReload(on: boolean): Promise<boolean>;
  /**
   * Prints a live line per phone log from now on: each `collector:session` becomes the lines of
   * the perf command (header with engine and build, STALE warning, a stats line at most every 5 s,
   * left / done). Call it once, after hub.listenDevices; without it the collector's events print
   * nothing.
   *
   * @param output - Where the lines go: the bin's brand console.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // runPerf, after the device listener is up.
   * editor.pages.attachPerf(ui);
   * // on the first log batch of a phone: "◉ SM-A266B · webgpu · engine 0.14.12+9c41e0 · build debug-20261014T160000Z · adb 127.0.0.1"
   * ```
   */
  attachPerf(output: PerfOutput): void;
};

/**
 * Arguments of `moku-editor [<game-html>] [--port 3000] [--root .] [--no-hmr] [--preload FILE]…
 * [--serve-plugin FILE]…`: serve the game. Without `html` the engine writes the page of the
 * moku-game folder at `root` (the engine page); the two lists feed only that page.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // moku-editor --root games/timber --serve-plugin plugins/marker.ts
 * const args: RunArgs = { kind: "run", port: 3000, root: "games/timber", hmr: true, preload: [], servePlugins: ["plugins/marker.ts"] };
 * ```
 */
export type RunArgs = {
  readonly kind: "run";
  /** The game HTML file, when given; the key is left out for the engine page. */
  readonly html?: string;
  /** The port on 127.0.0.1: 3000 by default, 0 for a random free port. */
  readonly port: number;
  /** The project root as given (default "."): the editor reads and writes there. */
  readonly root: string;
  /** False with `--no-hmr`: Bun serves the game without hot reload. */
  readonly hmr: boolean;
  /** Every `--preload`, as given: files Bun preloads in the serving process (engine page only). */
  readonly preload: readonly string[];
  /** Every `--serve-plugin`, as given: Bun plugins the page bundles with (engine page only). */
  readonly servePlugins: readonly string[];
};

/**
 * `run` arguments with the game HTML file: what the bin serves, itself or from a re-spawned bin.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const args: ServeArgs = { kind: "run", html: "/g/.moku/index.html", port: 0, root: "/g", hmr: true, preload: [], servePlugins: [] };
 * ```
 */
export type ServeArgs = RunArgs & { readonly html: string };

/**
 * Arguments of `moku-editor mcp [<game-html>] [--port N] [--root DIR] [--no-hmr]`: the stdio MCP
 * bridge. `html`, `port` and `hmr` only feed the bin the bridge starts when none runs; a live
 * `.moku/editor.json` under `root` wins.
 */
export type McpArgs = {
  readonly kind: "mcp";
  /** The game HTML file, when given. */
  readonly html?: string;
  /** The port, when `--port` was given. */
  readonly port?: number;
  /** The project root (default "."): where `.moku/editor.json` is read. */
  readonly root: string;
  /** False with `--no-hmr`. */
  readonly hmr: boolean;
};

/**
 * Arguments of `moku-editor mcp-config [<game-html>] [--port N]`: print the `.mcp.json` snippet
 * and the `claude mcp add` line for the same `mcp` arguments.
 */
export type McpConfigArgs = {
  readonly kind: "mcp-config";
  /** The game HTML file, when given. */
  readonly html?: string;
  /** The port, when `--port` was given. */
  readonly port?: number;
};

/**
 * Arguments of `moku-editor e2e -c <playwright config> [playwright args…]`: one Playwright run per
 * project and spec file of the config, each on its own `PORT` (D-52, D-53). Only `-c` / `--config`
 * is read here; `e2e.ts` sorts the other words for the list run and the runs.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // moku-editor e2e -c tests/browser/playwright.config.ts -g pick --headed
 * const args: E2eArgs = { kind: "e2e", config: "tests/browser/playwright.config.ts", rest: ["-g", "pick", "--headed"] };
 * ```
 */
export type E2eArgs = {
  readonly kind: "e2e";
  /** The Playwright config, as given after `-c` or `--config`. */
  readonly config: string;
  /** The other words, in order: Playwright's arguments. */
  readonly rest: readonly string[];
};

/**
 * Parsed arguments of the bin: serve, the two MCP subcommands, `e2e`, the four `perf` forms,
 * help, or an error.
 */
export type BinArgs =
  | RunArgs
  | McpArgs
  | McpConfigArgs
  | E2eArgs
  | PerfArgs
  | PerfMarkArgs
  | PerfSummaryArgs
  | PerfCompareArgs
  | { readonly kind: "help" }
  | { readonly kind: "error"; readonly message: string };

/**
 * The discovery file `<root>/.moku/editor.json` a serving bin writes (mode 0600) and removes on
 * stop: how the MCP bridge finds the running editor. Holds the hub token, so it is never printed
 * or logged.
 */
export type EditorDiscovery = {
  readonly version: 1;
  /** The bin's process id (the bridge treats a dead pid as no bin). */
  readonly pid: number;
  /** The real port on 127.0.0.1. */
  readonly port: number;
  /** `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. */
  readonly url: string;
  /** `ws://127.0.0.1:<port><P>/ws`, without the query. */
  readonly ws: string;
  /** The hub token of this start. */
  readonly token: string;
  /** The absolute project root. */
  readonly root: string;
  /** The absolute game HTML file. */
  readonly html: string;
  /** `Date.now()` when the file was written. */
  readonly startedAt: number;
};

// src/plugins/pages/perf/types.ts: the perf CLI

/**
 * `moku-editor perf [--lan] [--port 47600] [--out DIR] [--every 10] [--no-ui]`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // moku-editor perf --lan --no-ui
 * const args: PerfArgs = { kind: "perf", lan: true, port: 47600, out: ".moku/perf", every: 10, ui: false };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfArgs = {
  readonly kind: "perf";
  /** Also listen on the LAN address: a phone there pairs by its code. */
  readonly lan: boolean;
  /** The device port: 47600 by default, 0 for a random free port (tests). */
  readonly port: number;
  /** The folder of the logs, relative to the root: ".moku/perf" by default. */
  readonly out: string;
  /** Seconds between two adb readings (heat, system frames): 10 by default. */
  readonly every: number;
  /** False with `--no-ui`: the tools page is not served on the device port. */
  readonly ui: boolean;
};

/**
 * `moku-editor perf mark "<label>"`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const args: PerfMarkArgs = { kind: "perf-mark", label: "boss" };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfMarkArgs = { readonly kind: "perf-mark"; readonly label: string };

/**
 * `moku-editor perf summary <log>`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const args: PerfSummaryArgs = { kind: "perf-summary", log: ".moku/perf/perf-20261014-1532-sm-a266b.jsonl" };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfSummaryArgs = { readonly kind: "perf-summary"; readonly log: string };

/**
 * `moku-editor perf compare <a> <b>`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const args: PerfCompareArgs = { kind: "perf-compare", a: "before.jsonl", b: "after.jsonl" };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfCompareArgs = {
  readonly kind: "perf-compare";
  readonly a: string;
  readonly b: string;
};

/**
 * `.moku/perf.json`: how `perf mark` finds the running perf. Holds the hub token: never printed or
 * logged.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const record: PerfDiscovery = { version: 1, pid: 4242, port: 47600, path: "/__editor", token, lan: null, startedAt: 1791986083963 };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfDiscovery = {
  readonly version: 1;
  /** The perf run's process id (`perf mark` treats a dead pid as no run). */
  readonly pid: number;
  /** The real device port on 127.0.0.1. */
  readonly port: number;
  /** `hub.path()`, such as "/__editor". */
  readonly path: string;
  /** The hub token of this run. */
  readonly token: string;
  /** The LAN listener, `<address>:<port>`; null without `--lan`. */
  readonly lan: string | null;
  /** `Date.now()` when the file was written. */
  readonly startedAt: number;
};

/**
 * What a perf run prints through: the brand console satisfies it.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const lines: string[] = [];
 * const output: PerfOutput = { line: text => lines.push(text ?? ""), warn: message => lines.push(`! ${message}`) };
 * ```
 */
export type PerfOutput = {
  /**
   * Prints a plain line.
   *
   * @param text - The line; an empty line without it.
   */
  line(text?: string): void;
  /**
   * Prints a warning.
   *
   * @param message - The warning.
   */
  warn(message: string): void;
};
~~~

### 7.12 link — tools, Complex

- depends: none (first tools plugin). Lifecycle: `onStart` (silence check, read boot tag, open socket without waiting), `onStop` (reject pending with `link_closed`, close 1000, forget every listener).
- Session choice: sticky choice, then this page's own game frame (its `__editorFrame` id, `frameUrl`), then newest embedded, then newest. An embedded session of another tools tab is never picked on its own. Watches survive disconnects and are re-sent with new numeric subs after every reconnect or session change. `readSessions` keeps a well-typed `SessionInfo.device` (a phone); a malformed one is left out and the session reads as a browser session.
- A watch the session refuses with -32008 `not_installed` (the game does not have the source; the manifest lists it with `available: false`) is logged only at debug (`link:source-unavailable`) and never sent to that session again; a new session gets it again.
- Taps: every `tap { x, y, at }` notification of the chosen session goes to the `onTap` listeners (frozen, at most one per 50 ms from the bridge). `heap()` is the `heap` of the chosen session's last heartbeat (Chromium only).
- Hot reload (round 2 R6): `hotReload()` is the last `hotReload` notification of the hub (`undefined` before it); `onHotReload(listener)` gets every change; `setHotReload(on)` POSTs `{ hmr }` to `P/hmr` with the boot token and resolves `response.ok && state.owner === "bin" && state.hmr === on`: true when the bin owns the server and switched (D-32), false for a game's own server (as `pages.setHotReload`); a refusal is a 200 with the old state, so the page logs nothing (round 2b R16). The restart can cut the answer off: after a network failure the call waits up to 10 s for the reconnect to deliver `hotReload` and answers whether its `hmr` equals `on` (A1).
- Editor page role (D-33, A12): config `role: "page"` (default) adds `&role=page` to the socket URL; a headless client passes `"tools"`. `notify("selection", info | null)` publishes the selection (dropped while closed, the last value sent again on each open); `handle("select", handler)` answers the `select` requests the hub relays (params checked with `parseSelectParams`, no handler -32601); `selection()` is the last `editor.selection` notification.
- A game-side resume (round 2 R8): the next heartbeat (`paused: false`) turns the status live; the pill follows within one heartbeat.
- Project index: `project()` is the last `editor.project` state, frozen, kept across reconnects (`undefined` before the first). A new state emits `link:project` with its delta; the same state again (the hub's replay) emits nothing; a same-revision state with another `manifest` (the game revision hashes sources only) emits `{ all: false, files: [old, new manifest] }`. A malformed state logs `link:bad-project` (warn) and changes nothing. `files.find(key)` sends the files-channel `find`.
- Engine fingerprint: `engine()` is the id of the hub's `editor.engine` notification (`EngineInfo`), kept across reconnects; `undefined` before it and for `"unknown"`. `onEngine(listener)` is called at once when known, then on each change (a replay of the same id calls nothing). workspace shows it in the top bar; renderView compares it with a phone's for STALE.
- `frameUrl(url, { player? })`: the game URL tagged with this page's frame id; `player` (dev only) sets the `player` query parameter the engine dev page reads to start from `tests/scenarios/<player>.ts`.
- Events: emits `link:status`, `link:project`. Logs: `link:bad-project`, `link:bad-engine` (warn), `link:source-missing` (warn), `link:watch-failed` (error), `link:watch-deferred` (debug, a watch refused with `no_session` or -32001 `game_reloaded` while its session closed in a reload; sent again on the next attach), `link:source-unavailable` (debug), `link:tap-listener-failed`, `link:engine-listener-failed` (error).

~~~ts
/**
 * No heartbeat of the chosen session for this long → silent (R6).
 */
export const SILENT_AFTER_MS = 6000;

/**
 * Used instead of SILENT_AFTER_MS when the last heartbeat said paused (R6).
 */
export const SILENT_AFTER_PAUSED_MS = 65_000;

/**
 * Interval of the silence check.
 */
export const SILENCE_CHECK_MS = 1000;

/**
 * Cap of the reconnect backoff.
 */
export const MAX_RETRY_MS = 8000;

/**
 * After the chosen session closed, lost turns into empty when no session appeared for this long.
 */
export const EMPTY_AFTER_LOST_MS = 10_000;

/**
 * Local guard on every request; link's callTimeoutMs in the R1 long-call rule.
 */
export const CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

/**
 * Cap of the extension of a long call (R1): durationMs of editor.series, frames × everyMs of
 * editor.sheet.
 */
export const LONG_CALL_CAP_MS = 60_000;

/**
 * How long `setHotReload` waits, after its POST failed on the network, for the reconnect to deliver
 * the hot reload state (A1): the bin restarts the server, so the socket drops and comes back.
 */
export const HOT_RELOAD_CONFIRM_MS = 10_000;

/**
 * Link configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // A headless e2e client connects as a plain tools client, not as the editor page.
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { link: { retryMs: 500, role: "tools" } } });
 * ```
 */
export type Config = {
  /** Base delay of the reconnect backoff, in ms. Default 1000. */
  retryMs: number;
  /** CSS selector of the JSON script tag pages injects. Default "#moku-editor-boot". */
  boot: string;
  /**
   * "page": the editor page (`&role=page` on the upgrade, D-33): the hub takes its selection and
   * relays the editor requests `select`, `device`, `show` and `node` to it. "tools": a plain tools
   * client (no role sent). Default "page".
   */
  role: "page" | "tools";
  /**
   * How long an expected reload (U7) reads neutral: a server restart (close 1012), a reload the
   * editor started, a game that said bye. Without a heartbeat of the game by then, the status is a
   * plain `lost`. A positive number of ms. Default 8000: the bin's restart keeps its port closed
   * for up to 6 s (D-57) and the reconnects land 1 s, 3 s and 7 s after the close, so the window
   * outlasts the one at 7 s. No upper bound: a window still open EMPTY_AFTER_LOST_MS (10 s) after
   * a session loss ends as `empty` when no session came back, with no plain `lost` before it.
   */
  reloadGraceMs: number;
};

/**
 * The files channel as the tools views use it (R1, R4). No session: it works without a game. Each
 * method sends one files-channel request and checks the result shape. A bad shape rejects -32600;
 * server errors (`version_conflict`, `forbidden_path` …) reject as wire errors.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // The files view saves a Markdown tab while no game is connected.
 * await app.link.files.write("docs/plan.md", "# Plan\n");
 * ```
 */
export type FilesClient = {
  /**
   * Lists a folder.
   *
   * @param dir - Folder path relative to the root ("" for the root).
   * @returns The entries.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // gameView lists the captures folder before it names a new capture.
   * await app.link.files.list(".moku/captures");
   * // [{ path: ".moku/captures/a.png", kind: "file", size: 3, version: "v" }]
   * ```
   */
  list(dir: string): Promise<readonly FileEntry[]>;

  /**
   * Reads a text file.
   *
   * @param path - File path relative to the root.
   * @returns `{ text, version }`.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The files view opens a source tab.
   * await app.link.files.read("src/a.ts"); // { text: "x", version: "v1" }
   * ```
   */
  read(path: string): Promise<FileText>;

  /**
   * Writes a text file. With `version`, the write is checked against the version the edit started
   * from.
   *
   * @param path - File path relative to the root.
   * @param text - The new content.
   * @param version - The version the edit started from; omit to overwrite.
   * @returns `{ path, bytes, version }`.
   * @throws {Error} Rejects -32005 `version_conflict` when the file changed since `version`.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The files view saves a tab it read at version "v1".
   * await app.link.files.write("a.md", "hi", "v1"); // { path: "a.md", bytes: 2, version: "v3" }
   * ```
   */
  write(path: string, text: string, version?: string): Promise<WriteResult>;

  /**
   * Writes an image from a data URL (R1).
   *
   * @param path - Image path relative to the root.
   * @param dataUrl - `data:image/png;base64,…`.
   * @returns `{ path, bytes, version }`.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // gameView saves a capture of the game frame.
   * await app.link.files.writeBinary(".moku/captures/a.png", "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo=");
   * // { path: ".moku/captures/a.png", bytes: 8, version: "v" }
   * ```
   */
  writeBinary(path: string, dataUrl: string): Promise<WriteResult>;

  /**
   * Reads an image back as a data URL (R1).
   *
   * @param path - Image path relative to the root.
   * @returns `{ dataUrl, version }`.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The contact sheet shows a saved capture.
   * await app.link.files.readBinary(".moku/captures/a.png");
   * // { dataUrl: "data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo=", version: "v" }
   * ```
   */
  readBinary(path: string): Promise<FileBinary>;

  /**
   * Asks the project index where a key lives. Lines are read from disk at the call, and each
   * answer's `hash` equals the files `version` of its path. Rejects -32008 `not_installed` while
   * the index is off.
   *
   * @param key - A project-index key, e.g. `"node:board/merge"` or `"jsx:settingsBoard"`.
   * @returns Every place the key is defined; empty for a key the index does not know.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The Flow inspector opens the Code tab of the selected node.
   * await ctx.require(linkPlugin).files.find("node:board/merge");
   * // [{ path: "nodes/merge.ts", binding: "merge", line: 17, range: [17, 1, 30, 3], hash: "a1" }]
   * ```
   */
  find(key: string): Promise<readonly ProjectFound[]>;
};

/**
 * The link api (`app.link`): the remote EditorChannel plus sessions, manifest, boot and the files
 * client. On link the channel members behave so:
 *
 * - `read` and `run` reject -32003 `no_session` (not retryable) at once when no game is connected.
 * - `watch` is accepted in every state, also while disconnected, and is sent again after every
 * reconnect or session change. The first value is the agent's immediate read.
 * - `run` checks the RunResult shape; `editor.series` waits its `durationMs` and `editor.sheet`
 * its `frames × everyMs` on top of the call timeout (R1).
 * - `status` returns a copy.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // Step the attached game by one frame.
 * const ran = await app.link.run("game.step", { frames: 1 }); // ran.state.frame === 1841
 * ```
 */
export type LinkApi = EditorChannel & {
  /**
   * The cached manifest of the chosen session.
   *
   * @returns The manifest, undefined before one is attached.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Which game is attached?
   * app.link.manifest()?.game; // "merge-game 0.0.0"
   * ```
   */
  manifest(): Manifest | undefined;

  /**
   * Listens to the manifest: called at once when one exists, then on every attach, and with
   * undefined when the session is lost. A throwing listener is logged and does not stop the others.
   *
   * @param fn - The listener.
   * @returns Unsubscribe.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Count the sources of whichever game is attached.
   * const stop = app.link.onManifest(manifest => console.log(manifest?.sources.length)); // logs 2
   * stop();
   * ```
   */
  onManifest(fn: (manifest: Manifest | undefined) => void): () => void;

  /**
   * The last session list from the hub (empty while disconnected).
   *
   * @returns A copy of the list.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The session chip lists the open games.
   * app.link.sessions().map(session => session.id); // ["s-1"]
   * ```
   */
  sessions(): readonly SessionInfo[];

  /**
   * The chosen session id.
   *
   * @returns The id, undefined when none is chosen.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The session chip marks the game the tools are attached to.
   * app.link.session(); // "s-1"
   * ```
   */
  session(): string | undefined;

  /**
   * Makes a session the sticky choice and attaches it. Choosing the attached session only makes
   * it sticky.
   *
   * @param session - An id from `sessions()`.
   * @returns The manifest of the session.
   * @throws {Error} Rejects -32003 `choose_session` (not retryable) for an id that is not open.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The user picks the second open game in the session chip.
   * await app.link.choose("s-2"); // its manifest; app.link.session() is now "s-2"
   * ```
   */
  choose(session: string): Promise<Manifest>;

  /**
   * "Retry now": reconnects at once, re-picks a session when only the session was lost, or re-reads
   * the boot tag after `no_boot`. A no-op unless lost, and after stop.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The status card shows "Lost · retry in 8s"; the user clicks Retry now.
   * app.link.retry(); // reconnects without waiting for the backoff timer
   * ```
   */
  retry(): void;

  /**
   * Tells link that the game page is about to reload on purpose (U7). Until the game beats again,
   * or for `reloadGraceMs`, the loss that follows reads `lost` with `reloading: true`, which the
   * views show in a neutral tone; after that it is a plain `lost`. A loss that happened before the
   * call stays as it is. A no-op after stop.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // workspace reloads the docked game frame from the palette.
   * const link = ctx.require(linkPlugin);
   * link.expectReload();
   * iframe.src = link.frameUrl("http://127.0.0.1:3000/");
   * // the session close that follows:
   * link.status(); // { kind: "lost", reason: "game_reloaded", lastFrame: 1825, retryInMs: 1000, reloading: true }
   * ```
   */
  expectReload(): void;

  /**
   * The boot data of the tools page; its token is never to be logged.
   *
   * @returns The ToolsBoot, undefined when the tag was missing or invalid.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The game frame loads the game page from the boot data.
   * app.link.boot()?.gameUrl; // "/"
   * ```
   */
  boot(): ToolsBoot | undefined;

  /**
   * Tags a game page URL with the frame id of this tools page (the `__editorFrame` query
   * parameter; one random id per tools page) and, with `opts.player`, the dev page's scenario.
   * workspace loads its game frame from the tagged URL, so the session of that frame is this
   * page's own: the session choice prefers it and never picks the game frame of another tools tab
   * on its own.
   *
   * @param url - The game page URL, absolute or relative to the tools page.
   * @param opts - The scenario to start from (dev only).
   * @returns The absolute tagged URL; the URL unchanged when it does not parse.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // workspace loads its game frame from the scenario the person picked.
   * ctx.require(linkPlugin).frameUrl("http://127.0.0.1:3000/", { player: "full" });
   * // "http://127.0.0.1:3000/?player=full&__editorFrame=3f9a1c2b7d4e"
   * ```
   */
  frameUrl(url: string, opts?: FrameUrlOptions): string;

  /**
   * True when a page URL (`Manifest.page`, `SessionInfo.page`) is the game frame of another tools
   * tab: it carries a frame id that is not this page's. A page without a frame id is not.
   *
   * @param page - A page URL.
   * @returns Whether the page belongs to another tools tab.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // workspace's D-07 reload skips the manifest of a second tools tab's game.
   * const link = ctx.require(linkPlugin);
   * link.isOtherTab("http://127.0.0.1:3000/?__editorFrame=aaaaaaaaaaaa"); // true
   * link.isOtherTab(link.frameUrl("http://127.0.0.1:3000/")); // false: this page's own frame
   * ```
   */
  isOtherTab(page: string): boolean;

  /**
   * Listens to the taps of the attached game: every `pointerdown` on the game page, in page CSS
   * px of the game document (device px of the frame) and the page's `performance.now()`. Taps of
   * other sessions are dropped. The game page sends at most one tap per 50 ms. Each listener gets
   * the same frozen tap; a throwing listener is logged and does not stop the others.
   *
   * @param listener - Called with each tap.
   * @returns An idempotent unsubscribe.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // workspace draws a ripple where a click lands in the docked game frame.
   * const stop = ctx.require(linkPlugin).onTap(tap => ripple(tap.x, tap.y)); // { x: 206, y: 640, at: 15234.5 }
   * stop();
   * ```
   */
  onTap(listener: (tap: Tap) => void): () => void;

  /**
   * The JS heap of the attached game page from its last heartbeat, in MB rounded to 0.1. Only
   * Chromium reports it.
   *
   * @returns A copy of `{ usedMb, limitMb }`; undefined until the page reports one, when its last
   * beat had none, and after a session change.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The Render view shows the heap tile on each game.render change.
   * ctx.require(linkPlugin).heap(); // { usedMb: 12.8, limitMb: 4095.8 } in Chromium, undefined elsewhere
   * ```
   */
  heap(): { usedMb: number; limitMb: number } | undefined;

  /**
   * The hot reload state of the game server (R6): whether Bun reloads the game page on a source
   * change, and who owns the server. The hub sends it after the socket opens and on each change.
   *
   * @returns A copy of `{ hmr, owner }`; undefined until the hub sent one.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The moku-editor bin serves the game with Bun HMR on.
   * ctx.require(linkPlugin).hotReload(); // { hmr: true, owner: "bin" }
   * ```
   */
  hotReload(): HotReload | undefined;
  /**
   * Listens to the hot reload state: called at once when it is known, then on each change. Each
   * listener gets the same frozen state; a throwing listener is logged and does not stop the
   * others.
   *
   * @param listener - Called with each state.
   * @returns An idempotent unsubscribe.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // workspace shows the Hot reload switch as read-only for a game's own server.
   * const stop = ctx.require(linkPlugin).onHotReload(state => show(state.hmr, state.owner === "bin"));
   * stop();
   * ```
   */
  onHotReload(listener: (state: HotReload) => void): () => void;
  /**
   * Asks the server for hot reload on or off: `POST {path}/hmr` on the page origin with the boot
   * token. Takes the state the server answers. The bin accepts a change and restarts its server
   * (D-32); a game's own server refuses it. The restart can cut the answer off: after a network
   * failure the call waits up to 10 s for the reconnect to deliver the hot reload state and
   * answers whether its `hmr` equals `on` (A1). Never rejects: no boot, a refusal, a failed restart
   * or no reconnect in time answer false.
   *
   * @param on - The asked value.
   * @returns True when the bin owns the server and its HMR now equals `on`; false otherwise.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The bin serves with HMR on; the user flips the switch off in workspace.
   * await ctx.require(linkPlugin).setHotReload(false); // true: the bin restarted without HMR
   * ```
   */
  setHotReload(on: boolean): Promise<boolean>;
  /**
   * The selection of the editor, as the hub last sent it (`editor.selection`): this page's own
   * publish echoed back, or the one of another editor page tab.
   *
   * @returns A fresh copy; undefined when nothing is selected or the hub sent none yet.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The hub echoed the coins label the picker landed on.
   * ctx.require(linkPlugin).selection()?.key; // "coins"
   * ```
   */
  selection(): SelectionInfo | undefined;
  /**
   * Sends an editor-channel notification to the hub: `selection` publishes what the editor page
   * selected (`null`: nothing). The hub takes it only from a `role: "page"` link. Dropped while
   * the socket is closed; the last value is sent again each time the socket opens.
   *
   * @param method - "selection".
   * @param params - The selection, or null when nothing is selected.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // gameView publishes the element the picker landed on.
   * ctx.require(linkPlugin).notify("selection", {
   *   ref: { kind: "ui", path: "column#0/hudRow/coins" },
   *   key: "coins",
   *   name: "coins",
   *   type: "text",
   *   at: Date.now()
   * }); // MCP moku_selection now answers the coins label
   * ```
   */
  notify(method: NotifyMethod, params: PublishParams["selection"]): void;
  /**
   * Handles an editor-channel request the hub relays to this page: `select` (MCP `moku_select`),
   * `device`, `show` or `node`. One handler per method: a later handler replaces the earlier one
   * of the same method and leaves the other methods alone. The params are checked first with the
   * parser of the method (-32602 `invalid_input`); the handler's result is the answer, a thrown
   * error the failure. Without a handler of the method the hub gets -32601.
   *
   * @param method - "select", "device", "show" or "node".
   * @param handler - Gets the checked params of the method; returns or resolves its result.
   * @returns An idempotent remover; it removes only this handler.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // gameView answers `select` with a promise; flowView answers `node` at once.
   * const link = ctx.require(linkPlugin);
   * const offSelect = link.handle("select", params => selectByKey(params));
   * // editor.select { key: "coins" } → { key: "coins", name: "coins", card: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/coins-f1840.md", … }
   * const offNode = link.handle("node", ({ id }) => ({ id, selected: id }));
   * // editor.node { id: "main/home" } → { id: "main/home", selected: "main/home" }
   * ```
   */
  handle<M extends RelayedEditorMethod>(method: M, handler: RequestHandler<M>): () => void;
  /**
   * The project index the hub last sent (`editor.project`): on with its key maps, or off with the
   * reason. Kept across reconnects. Each new state is also the tools event `link:project`, with
   * the delta a view drops by.
   *
   * @returns The frozen state; undefined until the hub sent one.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // filesView lists the flows that use the open node file.
   * const project = ctx.require(linkPlugin).project();
   * project?.state === "on" ? project.uses["node:board/merge"] : []; // ["flows/board.ts"]
   * ```
   */
  project(): ProjectState | undefined;
  /**
   * The fingerprint id of the engine the computer serves: the project's installed
   * `@moku-labs/game` (version + dist hash, the recipe of the page's `__MOKU_GAME_ENGINE__`), as
   * the hub published it (`editor.engine`). Kept across reconnects.
   *
   * @returns The id; undefined until the hub sent one, or when it has none ("unknown").
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // renderView marks a phone that runs another engine than the computer.
   * ctx.require(linkPlugin).engine(); // "0.14.13+1ab7f2"
   * ```
   */
  engine(): string | undefined;
  /**
   * Listens to the computer's engine fingerprint: called at once when it is known, then on each
   * change. The replay of the same id after a reconnect calls nothing; a change from a known id
   * to "unknown" calls it with `undefined` (`engine()` answers undefined from then on). A
   * throwing listener is logged and does not stop the others.
   *
   * @param listener - Called with the id; with undefined when the hub no longer knows one.
   * @returns An idempotent unsubscribe.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // workspace re-renders the top bar when the fingerprint arrives.
   * const stop = ctx.require(linkPlugin).onEngine(() => state.ui.bump());
   * stop();
   * ```
   */
  onEngine(listener: (engine: string | undefined) => void): () => void;
  /**
   * The files channel client.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Another plugin saves a file through link.
   * await ctx.require(linkPlugin).files.read("src/a.ts"); // { text: "x", version: "v1" }
   * ```
   */
  files: FilesClient;
};

/**
 * Options of `frameUrl`.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const opts: FrameUrlOptions = { player: "full" };
 * ```
 */
export type FrameUrlOptions = {
  /**
   * A scenario of the engine dev page (`tests/scenarios/<name>.ts`): sets the `player` query
   * parameter, which `startPage` reads (`?player=<name>`). Dev only. Absent or "": the URL's own
   * `player` parameter is left as it is.
   */
  readonly player?: string;
};
~~~

### 7.13 workspace — tools, Complex

- depends: `[linkPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` (config, prefs, theme, hash, keys, Esc layers, palette), `onStart` (window listeners, `link.onManifest`), `mount(el)` (renders the shell, creates the frame layer once), `onStop`.
- Workspaces in rail order: Game (the default, ⌘1), Flow (⌘2), Render, State, Files, Console.
- Keys: ⌘1–⌘6 and 1–6 switch workspaces in that order; ⌘K palette; `.` step while paused; P pause/resume; O overlay in game; G preview; H hot reload; Esc unwinds layers in `EscLayer` order.
- Top bar (round 2 R1), `data-layout` on `[data-ui="top-bar"]`: from 900 px (`wide`) the game mark, game name, session chip, the computer's engine fingerprint (from 1100 px), link pill, Pause, Step, the search box, the switches Preview (G), Overlay (O) and Hot reload (H) with visible labels, Registry (icon only; counts in its title "Registry · 20 sources · 23 commands"), theme. Below 900 px (`compact`) the game mark, game name (hidden at 560 px and narrower), link pill (session id in its title; it opens the session menu), Pause and Step as icons (the labels are their accessible names, round 2b R15), the icon toggle Hot reload (`data-action="hot-reload"`, flame with a dot while on, `aria-pressed`; the one toggle of the bar at every compact width: `barToggles(width)` answers `["hot-reload"]` below 900 px and `[]` from there; inert with its reason in the title when the editor cannot change it), a search icon and the ⋯ button (`data-action="more"`): a top-layer `role="menu"` popover with Game preview, Overlay in game, Hot reload (each with its state and its key; a toggle row keeps the menu open), Registry (counts; opens the registry popover), Density (cycles auto → compact → comfortable) and Theme. Rows keep the `data-action` of the wide controls (`game`, `overlay`, `hot-reload`, `registry`, `theme`) plus `density`; Hot reload stays in the menu while its icon shows. No two controls overlap at 480, 600, 640, 720, 899, 960 and 1440 px (e2e/top-bar.spec.ts).
- Hot reload switch (D-32): mirrors `link.hotReload()`. Owner `"bin"`: a click (the switch, the ⋯ row or key H) bookmarks the game, asks `setHotReload`, toasts "Hot reload off" or "Hot reload on", waits for this tab's game on the restarted server and reloads the frame with the bookmark ("Game reloaded · state restored from the last checkpoint"), so the page gains or drops Bun's HMR client. A failed switch toasts "Could not switch · start the bin with --no-hmr to turn hot reload off" (or "…without --no-hmr to turn hot reload on") and keeps that hint in the title. Owner `"server"`: "The game's own server sets hot reload"; owner unknown: inert, the reason in the title.
- Narrow first: built for Claude's browser pane at 1/3 (480 px) and 1/2 (720 px) of the screen; every workspace works at 480 px without horizontal page scroll.
- Density: `auto` (default; compact below 820 px of window width, comfortable from there), `compact` or `comfortable`. Palette items "Density: …"; saved with the theme; `data-density` on `<html>`; `workspace:density` when the applied value changes.
- The game mark (U1): `span[data-mark]` (`aria-hidden`) is first in both layouts: a 24 px tile with the initials of the game name on a colour from the name. `markOf(name)` (`mark.ts`, pure): two words or more (split on whitespace, `-` and `_`) give the first letters of the first two words in upper case ("Tic Tac Toe" → `TT`, "merge-game" → `MG`); one word gives its first two letters ("Merge" → `ME`); no game gives `·` and no hue. The hue is the sum of every character code times its position (from 1), modulo 360, over the trimmed lower-case name, written as the inline custom property `--mark-hue`; without it the tile is neutral. While the link reloads the mark holds the last name.
- Copy on select (U5, D-68, D-70, D-72): `copyOnSelect()` and `setCopyOnSelect(on)` keep the flag in the prefs record (`copyOnSelect`, default true, also for a stored record without the field; `onPrefs` gets it). On: a picker click writes the reference and copies its line. Off: a picker click only selects the element. The palette command "Copy reference on select: turn off" / "… turn on" flips it; no key, no event. The top bar has no control for it (no ⋯ row, no switch of the wide bar): the control is the "Copy Ref" switch of gameView's game toolbar, which calls `setCopyOnSelect` and follows `onPrefs`. workspace only keeps the flag: gameView reads it at a picker click.
- Pinned preview: the header drags it (snaps to a corner); the body plays the game (taps and keys reach it); the size changes only through S/M/L.
- Tap ripples: `link.onTap` draws a ring at the tap point over the docked frame while "Show taps in the game" is on.
- Devices (round 2 R4, round 2b R9 R10, `devices()`): the presets live in `registry/protocol/devices.ts` (`DEVICES`, `DEVICE_GROUPS`, `DEFAULT_DEVICE`, `resolveDevice`, `screenOf`, `deviceById`, `presetOf`, `isDevicePresetId`); workspace and gameView both read them there. Twenty-one presets in `<optgroup>` groups. iPhone: SE 3 · small, 2022 (`iphone-se`, 375×667, safe 20/0, `frame: "home-button"`), 15 (`iphone-15`, 393×852, 59/34), 17e (`iphone-17e`, 390×844, 47/34, approx), Air (`iphone-air`, 420×912, 68/34, approx), 18 Pro (`iphone-18-pro`, default, 402×874, 62/34, approx), 18 Pro Max (`iphone-18-pro-max`, 440×956, 62/34, approx), then 15 Pro Max (430×932, 59/34), 16 Pro (402×874, 62/34), 16 Pro Max (440×956, 62/34) at the end so a stored choice keeps working. Android (no insets): Galaxy S24 (360×780), Galaxy A55 (412×892), Redmi Note 13 (393×873, approx), Pixel 8 (412×915), Xperia 1 V 21:9 (411×960). Foldable: Galaxy Z Fold 6 (cover 369×905 ⇄ inner 707×823, approx), Galaxy Z Flip 6 (412×1005), Pixel 9 Pro Fold (cover 411×923 ⇄ inner 791×820, approx), iPhone Duo (`iphone-duo`, cover 466×678 ⇄ inner 890×626, a book that opens landscape-wide; Apple's pixels divided by 3, approx). Tablet: iPad mini 7 (744×1133), iPad Air 11" (820×1180). Desktop (1440×900). Each has `dpr`, `radius`, `group` and `frame` (`"modern"` | `"home-button"`); `approx: true` marks estimated sizes or insets. `setDevice({ folded })` switches a foldable live (the game sees a resize); a new preset starts folded. An unknown stored id falls back to the iPhone 18 Pro.
- Sound flag (round 2b R11): `muted()` and `setMuted(on)` keep it in the prefs record (`muted`, default false; `onPrefs` gets it). workspace never touches the game: gameView sends `game.mute`.
- Dark theme bezel `--color-bezel: #2c2c34` with a 1 px `--border-strong` outline; the docked frame's clip-path is `inset(… round <radius>px)` in the frame's own px, on the stage and in the pinned preview.
- D-07 reload: `game.bookmark` → `iframe.src` reassigned → first manifest of an embedded session → `game.restore { bookmark }`. With Bun hot reload on, `gameFrame().reload()` after a save first waits up to `hotReloadWaitMs` (1500) for the page Bun reloads: its hello with `manifest.restored` ends the run with the toast "Game reloaded · state restored" (no second reload, restore or pause); without `restored` workspace restores its bookmark; no new session in time → the frame reloads itself. A session with `restored` after an outside edit (an agent writing a file) toasts "Game reloaded · state restored" once. Hot swap (game 0.5.0, U10): in the same wait, a `ui:hot-swap` entry of the game's `game.log` (`isHotSwapEntry`) logged after the save ends the run with `{ restored: false, reason: "hot_swap" }` and the toast "Game updated": no frame reload, no restore.
- Only the game reloads (U9): `link.expectReload()` before a frame reload; while `isReloading(status)` (a `lost` with `reloading: true`) the top bar keeps the last game name, session id and the pill text `Live · f<lastFrame>` (fixed width), the StaleBar is hidden, the panels keep their data, and the one indicator is the spinner `[data-frame-reloading]` on the game frame (counter-scaled, no layout). A real loss, or one past `reloadGraceMs`, shows the red StaleBar as an overlay at the top of the workspace, never in the layout flow. e2e/reload-quiet.spec.ts measures 0 layout shift on the tools page across Reload, Hot reload off/on and a rules save.
- Events: emits `workspace:changed`, `workspace:ran`, `workspace:density`; hooks `link:status`.
- Scenarios (dev only, spec 09 W5): the engine dev page starts from `tests/scenarios/<name>.ts` when its URL carries `?player=<name>`. workspace lists that folder through `link.files.list` once the link is open (`scenarios()`, `refreshScenarios()`, `onScenario(fn)`), keeps the chosen name (never persisted) and passes it to `link.frameUrl(url, { player })` for the first mount, the D-07 reload and the Hot reload switch's reload. `setScenario(name)` reloads the frame without restore (a bookmark on top would undo the scenario) and toasts "Game started from scenario <name>"; an unknown name rejects with a `TypeError`. gameView's game toolbar shows the picker. A debug build carries no scenarios.
- Engine in the top bar: from 900 px (shown from 1100 px of window width) `span[data-part="engine"]` reads "engine 0.14.13+1ab7f2" from `link.engine()`; the game name's `title` carries it in every layout.

~~~ts
/**
 * The six workspaces.
 */
export type WorkspaceId = "flow" | "game" | "render" | "state" | "files" | "console";

/**
 * Workspace configuration (`defaultWorkspace`, `storageKey` from contracts §5; the rest private).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { workspace: { defaultWorkspace: "game" } } });
 * ```
 */
export type WorkspaceConfig = {
  /** Workspace shown at start when the URL hash names none. */
  defaultWorkspace: WorkspaceId;
  /** localStorage key of the preferences record. */
  storageKey: string;
  /** How long reload() waits for the new session before giving up. */
  reloadTimeoutMs: number;
  /**
   * After a save with Bun hot reload on, how long `gameFrame().reload({ afterSave: true })` waits
   * for the page Bun reloads before it reloads the frame itself.
   */
  hotReloadWaitMs: number;
  /** How long one toast stays (hover or focus pauses it). */
  toastMs: number;
};

/**
 * The colour theme.
 */
export type Theme = "light" | "dark";

/**
 * The applied density: compact (tighter spacing, smaller UI text) or comfortable.
 */
export type Density = "compact" | "comfortable";

/**
 * The chosen density; `auto` is compact below 820 px of window width, comfortable otherwise.
 */
export type DensityChoice = "auto" | Density;

/**
 * A workspace that has a pinned game preview (every one but Game).
 */
export type PreviewWorkspace = Exclude<WorkspaceId, "game">;

/**
 * Preview preferences plus the float size in px.
 */
export type PreviewState = PreviewPrefs & { width: number; height: number };

/**
 * The preset id, the orientation and the resolved size live in the protocol with DeviceSpec and
 * the presets (registry/protocol/devices.ts); re-exported here for `Workspace.*`.
 */
export type { DevicePresetId, DeviceSize, Orientation } from "../registry/protocol";

/**
 * What device() returns (R4): the preset as it shows now (an unfolded foldable carries its inner
 * screen's size and radius), the orientation, and whether a foldable is folded (true = cover).
 */
export type DeviceChoice = { preset: DeviceSpec; orientation: Orientation; folded: boolean };

/**
 * A rail badge.
 */
export type Badge = { count: number; tone: "warn" | "error"; label: string };

/**
 * Result of the D-07 reload. `hot_swap`: after a save the game swapped the module in place (dev
 * hot swap of game 0.5.0), so the frame was not reloaded and nothing was restored.
 */
export type ReloadResult = {
  restored: boolean;
  reason?:
    | "not_mounted"
    | "not_embedded"
    | "no_session"
    | "bookmark_failed"
    | "restore_failed"
    | "timeout"
    | "hot_swap";
};

/**
 * The scenario picker's data: the prepared saves of the game folder and the one the game frame
 * starts from. Dev only: a debug build carries no scenarios.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const view: ScenarioView = { scenarios: ["empty", "full"], chosen: "full" };
 * ```
 */
export type ScenarioView = {
  readonly scenarios: readonly string[];
  readonly chosen: string | undefined;
};

/**
 * Where a command run started.
 */
export type RunOrigin = "topbar" | "palette" | "key" | "panel";

/**
 * Payload of the global tools event `workspace:ran` (R4).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const ran: RanEvent = { id: "game.step", input: { frames: 1 }, origin: "topbar", at: Date.now(), ok: true, result };
 * ```
 */
export type RanEvent = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly input: Json | undefined;
  readonly origin: RunOrigin;
  /** Date.now() when the call settled. */
  readonly at: number;
} & (
  | { readonly ok: true; readonly result: RunResult }
  | { readonly ok: false; readonly error: WireError }
);

/**
 * The one game frame of the tools page (R4, D-14): it never moves in the DOM.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // Reload the game page and put it back where it was.
 * await app.workspace.gameFrame().reload({ restore: true }); // { restored: true }
 * ```
 */
export type GameFrame = {
  /**
   * Absolute URL of the game page: `link.boot()?.gameUrl` resolved against the page, "/" without
   * a boot. Read again on every access, so a refreshed boot is seen.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // On the tools page http://127.0.0.1:3000/__editor with the boot gameUrl "/".
   * app.workspace.gameFrame().url; // "http://127.0.0.1:3000/"
   * ```
   */
  readonly url: string;

  /**
   * The D-07 reload: bookmark, reload in place, restore on the new session, toast. Concurrent
   * calls share one run. After a save (`afterSave: true`) with Bun hot reload on, Bun reloads the
   * page itself: the run waits up to `hotReloadWaitMs` for that session and reloads the frame only
   * when none came; a session the bridge already restored (`manifest.restored`) is not restored or
   * paused again. A game that hot swapped the saved module since `since` (a `ui:hot-swap` game.log
   * entry) ends the run with `reason: "hot_swap"` and the toast "Game updated": no frame reload,
   * no restore. Without `afterSave` the frame reloads at once.
   *
   * @param opts - Restore, afterSave and since (see `ReloadOptions`).
   * @returns The result; `{ restored: false, reason: "not_mounted" }` before the first mount.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // No save: reload the game now and keep the board.
   * await app.workspace.gameFrame().reload({ restore: true }); // { restored: true }
   * // A styles module saved with Bun hot reload on, and swapped in place by the game.
   * await app.workspace.gameFrame().reload({ restore: true, afterSave: true, since: 1_759_680_000_000 }); // { restored: false, reason: "hot_swap" }
   * ```
   */
  reload(opts?: ReloadOptions): Promise<ReloadResult>;

  /**
   * Docks the frame over a stage slot (geometry only).
   *
   * @param slot - The stage slot.
   * @param opts - `fit` and an optional clip element.
   * @param opts.fit - How the device fits the slot.
   * @param opts.clip - The element that clips the frame.
   * @returns The release function.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The Game workspace shows the game in its stage.
   * const release = app.workspace.gameFrame().dock(stage, { fit: "fit" });
   * app.workspace.gameFrame().box()?.docked; // "stage"
   * release(); // box()?.docked is "hidden"
   * ```
   */
  dock(slot: HTMLElement, opts: { fit: FrameFit; clip?: HTMLElement }): () => void;

  /**
   * The element above the iframe in device space (game CSS px, scaled with the frame). Its
   * pointer-events are none by default.
   *
   * @returns The overlay element.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // renderView draws its highlight boxes in game CSS px, wherever the frame is docked.
   * ctx.require(workspacePlugin).gameFrame().overlay().append(document.createElement("div"));
   * ```
   */
  overlay(): HTMLElement;

  /**
   * The current frame box in tools-page px.
   *
   * @returns A copy, undefined before the first mount.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The frame floats in a preview at half size.
   * app.workspace.gameFrame().box()?.scale; // 0.5
   * ```
   */
  box(): FrameBox | undefined;
};

/**
 * One palette item.
 */
export type PaletteItem = {
  id: string;
  group: PaletteGroup;
  label: string;
  mono?: boolean;
  hint?: string;
  keywords?: string;
  shortcut?: string;
  run(): void;
  /** ⇧↵, e.g. "Open in Files". */
  alt?: { label: string; run(): void };
