  /** Reason shown dimmed; the item does not run. */
  disabled?: () => string | false;
};

/**
 * A key binding (design §4).
 */
export type KeyBinding = {
  /** "mod+k" or ["shift+mod+c", "i"]. */
  keys: string | readonly string[];
  /** Shown in tooltips and the palette. */
  label: string;
  run(event: KeyboardEvent): void;
  /** Active only there; omitted = global. */
  workspace?: WorkspaceId;
  when?: () => boolean;
  inInputs?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Esc layers in unwinding rank order (design §4).
 */
export type EscLayer =
  | "palette"
  | "contactSheet"
  | "contextMenu"
  | "registry"
  | "seriesPopover"
  | "captureCard"
  | "picker"
  | "fileEdit"
  | "codeEdit"
  | "stepPopover"
  | "selection";

/**
 * The workspace api (`app.workspace`, `tools.workspace` of every panel).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // Save a style, then show the game.
 * app.workspace.toast("Saved", "src/styles.ts");
 * app.workspace.show("game");
 * ```
 */
export type WorkspaceApi = {
  /**
   * The shown workspace.
   *
   * @returns Its id.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.workspace.active(); // "game" with the default config
   * ```
   */
  active(): WorkspaceId;

  /**
   * Shows a workspace. Emits `workspace:changed` only when it changes, and writes `#<ws>` into the
   * URL.
   *
   * @param ws - The workspace.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] Unknown workspace "<ws>".` for another id.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.workspace.show("game"); // emits workspace:changed { ws: "game" }; location.hash is "#game"
   * ```
   */
  show(ws: WorkspaceId): void;

  /**
   * The effective theme: the chosen one, else the OS one.
   *
   * @returns light or dark.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.workspace.theme(); // "light" on a light OS with no choice made
   * ```
   */
  theme(): Theme;

  /**
   * Sets the theme, or toggles it when omitted; persists the choice and sets `data-theme`.
   *
   * @param theme - The theme, omitted to toggle.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.workspace.setTheme(); // light → dark
   * app.workspace.theme(); // "dark"
   * ```
   */
  setTheme(theme?: Theme): void;

  /**
   * The applied density: `auto` resolves to compact below 820 px of window width.
   *
   * @returns compact or comfortable.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // flowView spaces its layout by the density the shell shows.
   * ctx.require(workspacePlugin).density(); // "compact" in a 720 px window with the default "auto"
   * ```
   */
  density(): Density;

  /**
   * Chooses the density, persists the choice and sets `data-density` on `<html>`. Emits
   * `workspace:density` when the applied value changes.
   *
   * @param value - auto, compact or comfortable.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.workspace.setDensity("compact"); // emits workspace:density { density: "compact" } in a wide window
   * app.workspace.density(); // "compact"
   * ```
   */
  setDensity(value: DensityChoice): void;

  /**
   * The preview state of a non-Game workspace.
   *
   * @param ws - The workspace.
   * @returns The prefs plus the float size in px.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.workspace.preview("flow");
   * // { visible: true, size: "S", corner: "bottom-right", width: 150, height: 280 }
   * ```
   */
  preview(ws: PreviewWorkspace): PreviewState;

  /**
   * Patches the preview prefs and persists them. A visibility change shows a toast.
   *
   * @param ws - The workspace.
   * @param patch - visible, size and/or corner.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.workspace.setPreview("render", { visible: false });
   * // toast: "Game preview hidden in Render · remembered for this workspace"
   * ```
   */
  setPreview(ws: PreviewWorkspace, patch: Partial<PreviewPrefs>): void;

  /**
   * The current device: the preset as it shows now (an unfolded foldable carries its inner
   * screen), the orientation and the folded flag.
   *
   * @returns The device choice.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A fresh viewer.
   * app.workspace.device(); // { preset: { id: "iphone-18-pro", w: 402, h: 874, … }, orientation: "portrait", folded: true }
   * ```
   */
  device(): DeviceChoice;

  /**
   * Changes the preset, the orientation and/or the fold; the frame resizes live (the game sees a
   * window resize, no reload); the choice persists and `onPrefs` listeners run. A new preset
   * starts folded unless the patch says otherwise.
   *
   * @param patch - The preset, the orientation and/or the fold.
   * @param patch.preset - A preset id.
   * @param patch.orientation - portrait or landscape.
   * @param patch.folded - true for the cover screen of a foldable, false for the inner one.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] Unknown device "<id>".` for an unknown preset.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // gameView's Fold button opens the Galaxy Z Fold 6.
   * app.workspace.setDevice({ preset: "galaxy-z-fold-6" });
   * app.workspace.setDevice({ folded: false });
   * app.workspace.device().preset.w; // 707: the inner screen
   * ```
   */
  setDevice(patch: { preset?: DevicePresetId; orientation?: Orientation; folded?: boolean }): void;

  /**
   * The twenty-one presets in display order: iPhone, Android, Foldable, Tablet, Desktop. Each
   * carries its `frame` (R9): only the iPhone SE 3 has the home-button frame.
   *
   * @returns The DeviceSpec list.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // gameView lists the presets of each group under its own <optgroup>.
   * app.workspace.devices().filter(device => device.group === "foldable").map(device => device.id);
   * // ["galaxy-z-fold-6", "galaxy-z-flip-6", "pixel-9-pro-fold", "iphone-duo"]
   * ```
   */
  devices(): readonly DeviceSpec[];

  /**
   * The single game frame.
   *
   * @returns The GameFrame api: one object for the app's life.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.workspace.gameFrame() === app.workspace.gameFrame(); // true
   * ```
   */
  gameFrame(): GameFrame;

  /**
   * The command palette.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A view adds its own command and opens the palette on it.
   * app.workspace.palette.add({ id: "cmd:capture", group: "Commands", label: "Capture", run: () => {} });
   * app.workspace.palette.open("capture");
   * ```
   */
  palette: {
    /**
     * Adds palette items; an existing id is replaced.
     *
     * @param item - One item or many.
     * @returns Removes them.
     * @example
     * ```ts
     * // flowView lists every node of the flow graph.
     * const remove = app.workspace.palette.add({ id: "node:a", group: "Nodes", label: "a", run: () => {} });
     * remove(); // the item leaves the palette
     * ```
     */
    add(item: PaletteItem | readonly PaletteItem[]): () => void;

    /**
     * Opens the palette.
     *
     * @param query - The initial query.
     * @example
     * ```ts
     * app.workspace.palette.open("merge"); // the palette shows the matches of "merge"
     * ```
     */
    open(query?: string): void;
  };

  /**
   * Shows a toast; `file` renders in mono after a middle dot.
   *
   * @param message - One line.
   * @param file - A file to name.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.workspace.toast("Saved", "src/styles.ts");
   * ```
   */
  toast(message: string, file?: string): void;

  /**
   * Mounts the shell. The first call also creates the frame layer and the iframe.
   *
   * @param element - The mount element.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The tools page entry mounts the shell after start.
   * await app.start();
   * app.workspace.mount(document.body);
   * ```
   */
  mount(element: HTMLElement): void;

  /**
   * The host element of a workspace: created on the first call, also before mount, and kept
   * after it.
   *
   * @param ws - The workspace.
   * @returns The host.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // panels mounts the Flow panels into the Flow host.
   * const unmount = app.panels.mountInto("flow", app.workspace.host("flow"));
   * ```
   */
  host(ws: WorkspaceId): HTMLElement;

  /**
   * Sets or clears the rail badge of a workspace.
   *
   * @param ws - The workspace.
   * @param badge - The badge, undefined to clear.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The console counts 2 warnings and 1 error.
   * app.workspace.badge("console", { count: 3, tone: "error", label: "2 warn · 1 error" });
   * app.workspace.badge("console", undefined); // clears it
   * ```
   */
  badge(ws: WorkspaceId, badge: Badge | undefined): void;

  /**
   * Where the preview floats in a workspace. The remover drops the zone unless a newer zone
   * replaced it.
   *
   * @param ws - The workspace.
   * @param element - The zone element.
   * @param insets - Insets in px, or a function that reads them.
   * @returns Removes the zone.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The flow panel keeps the preview inside its canvas, clear of the 56 px bars.
   * const remove = app.workspace.previewZone("flow", canvas, { top: 56, bottom: 56 });
   * ```
   */
  previewZone(
    ws: PreviewWorkspace,
    element: HTMLElement,
    insets?: Insets | (() => Insets)
  ): () => void;

  /**
   * The keyboard: bindings and Esc layers.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // flowView binds "c" in Flow and closes its context menu on Esc.
   * app.workspace.keys.bind({ keys: "c", label: "Show where the game is", workspace: "flow", run: () => {} });
   * app.workspace.keys.escape("contextMenu", () => true);
   * ```
   */
  keys: {
    /**
     * Adds a key binding. Two bindings of one scope may share a combo only when one of them has a
     * `when` condition.
     *
     * @param binding - The binding.
     * @returns Removes it.
     * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] Key "<combo>" is already bound in <scope>.` for a clash.
     * @example
     * ```ts
     * // flowView: "c" shows where the game is while Flow is shown.
     * const off = app.workspace.keys.bind({ keys: "c", label: "Show where the game is", workspace: "flow", run: () => {} });
     * off();
     * ```
     */
    bind(binding: KeyBinding): () => void;

    /**
     * Adds an Esc closer on a layer. Esc unwinds the open layers in rank order.
     *
     * @param layer - The layer.
     * @param close - Returns true when it closed something.
     * @returns Removes it.
     * @example
     * ```ts
     * // The context menu closes on Esc before the registry popover does.
     * const off = app.workspace.keys.escape("contextMenu", () => true);
     * off();
     * ```
     */
    escape(layer: EscLayer, close: () => boolean): () => void;
  };

  /**
   * The overlay-in-game flag. Always false at load; never persisted.
   *
   * @returns Whether it is on.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.workspace.overlayInGame(); // false
   * ```
   */
  overlayInGame(): boolean;

  /**
   * Sets the overlay-in-game flag: runs `editor.overlay` with origin `panel`.
   *
   * @param on - The new flag.
   * @returns Resolves when the run settled.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * await app.workspace.setOverlayInGame(true); // emits workspace:ran { id: "editor.overlay", … }
   * app.workspace.overlayInGame(); // true
   * ```
   */
  setOverlayInGame(on: boolean): Promise<void>;

  /**
   * The hot reload state of the game server, as link reports it: whether Bun reloads the game
   * page after a save, and who owns the server.
   *
   * @returns A copy of `{ hmr, owner }`; undefined until the hub sent one.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Under the moku-editor bin.
   * app.workspace.hotReload(); // { hmr: true, owner: "bin" }
   * ```
   */
  hotReload(): HotReload | undefined;

  /**
   * Asks the server for hot reload on or off (`link.setHotReload`). The bin switches by restarting
   * its server (D-32): workspace bookmarks the game first, toasts the new state, waits for this
   * tab's game on the restarted server and reloads the game frame with that bookmark, so the page
   * gains or drops Bun's HMR client. A refusal (a game's own server) or a failed switch toasts how
   * to change hot reload and keeps that hint in the switch's tooltip.
   *
   * @param on - The asked value.
   * @returns True when the bin owns the server and its HMR now equals `on`; false otherwise.
   * Never rejects.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The bin serves with HMR on.
   * await app.workspace.setHotReload(false); // true; toast "Hot reload off", then the game reloads with its state
   * ```
   */
  setHotReload(on: boolean): Promise<boolean>;

  /**
   * The sound flag of the game (R11): true while the viewer muted it. Kept in the preferences,
   * so it survives a reload of the tools page; false for a fresh viewer.
   *
   * @returns Whether the game's sound is off.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // gameView mutes the game again after it connects.
   * const workspace = ctx.require(workspacePlugin);
   * if (workspace.muted()) await ctx.require(panelsPlugin).run("game.mute", { muted: true });
   * ```
   */
  muted(): boolean;

  /**
   * Sets the sound flag and persists it; `onPrefs` listeners get the new `muted`. The same value
   * again changes nothing and calls no listener. The game is not touched here: gameView sends
   * `game.mute`.
   *
   * @param on - True to mute the game, false to give it its sound back.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // gameView's Sound switch.
   * app.workspace.setMuted(true);
   * app.workspace.muted(); // true; onPrefs listeners got { …, muted: true }
   * ```
   */
  setMuted(on: boolean): void;

  /**
   * The "Copy on select" preference (U5, D-70): what a click of the element picker does. On: the
   * pick writes the reference (the crop, the full frame and the card) and copies its line. Off:
   * the pick only selects the element for the Element tab and writes nothing. Kept in the
   * preferences, so it survives a reload of the tools page; true for a fresh viewer and for a
   * stored record from before the preference. Its control is the Copy Ref switch of gameView's
   * game toolbar; the palette command "Copy reference on select" flips it too.
   *
   * @returns Whether a pick writes the reference and copies its line.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // gameView handles a picker click: the element is selected either way, and the pick is
   * // completed (shots, card, clipboard) only while the preference is on.
   * const workspace = ctx.require(workspacePlugin);
   * if (!workspace.copyOnSelect()) return; // false after setCopyOnSelect(false): inspect only
   * ```
   */
  copyOnSelect(): boolean;

  /**
   * Turns "Copy on select" on or off: stores the flag in the preferences and calls the `onPrefs`
   * listeners (the Copy Ref switch of gameView's game toolbar follows them). The same value
   * again does nothing. No event is emitted: gameView reads the flag at the next pick.
   *
   * @param on - True for a pick that writes the reference and copies its line, false for a pick
   *   that only selects the element.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The person only wants to look at elements in the Element tab: no files, no clipboard.
   * app.workspace.setCopyOnSelect(false);
   * app.workspace.copyOnSelect(); // false; onPrefs listeners got { …, copyOnSelect: false }
   * ```
   */
  setCopyOnSelect(on: boolean): void;

  /**
   * Listens to preference changes (theme, preview, device, sound, Copy on select). A throwing
   * listener is logged and does not stop the others.
   *
   * @param fn - The listener.
   * @returns Removes it.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * const off = app.workspace.onPrefs(prefs => console.log(prefs.theme));
   * app.workspace.setTheme("dark"); // logs "dark"
   * off();
   * ```
   */
  onPrefs(fn: (prefs: Prefs) => void): () => void;

  /**
   * The scenarios of the game folder — every `.ts` file directly in `tests/scenarios/` but tests,
   * declarations and `index.ts`, by file stem, sorted (the engine's rule) — and the chosen one.
   * Empty until the first listing (it runs once the link's socket is open), and for a project
   * without the folder.
   *
   * @returns A copy.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // gameView shows the picker only when the game has scenarios.
   * ctx.require(workspacePlugin).scenarios(); // { scenarios: ["empty", "full"], chosen: undefined }
   * ```
   */
  scenarios(): ScenarioView;

  /**
   * Starts the game frame from a scenario (`?player=<name>` on the frame URL), or from the saved
   * player again with `undefined`: reloads the frame without restore (a scenario plays on a fresh
   * memory save; a bookmark restored on top would undo it) and toasts "Game started from scenario
   * <name>" or "Game started from the saved player" instead of the reload's own toast. The same
   * name again restarts it. Never persisted: a reload of the tools page starts from the saved
   * player. Before the first mount it only stores the choice and resolves `not_mounted`; the first
   * mount loads it. Emits no `workspace:ran` (it runs no command).
   *
   * @param name - A name from `scenarios()`, or undefined for the saved player.
   * @returns The reload result: `{ restored: false }`, or `reason: "timeout"` when no game came.
   * @throws {TypeError} Rejects `[moku-editor] Unknown scenario "<name>".\n  Pick one of
   *   workspace.scenarios().` for a name not listed (argument validation).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The person picks "full" in the game toolbar.
   * await app.workspace.setScenario("full"); // { restored: false }; toast "Game started from scenario full"
   * app.workspace.scenarios().chosen; // "full": the frame src carries player=full
   * ```
   */
  setScenario(name: string | undefined): Promise<ReloadResult>;

  /**
   * Lists `tests/scenarios/` again through the files channel (`link.files.list`). Concurrent calls
   * share one listing. A missing folder or a failed list gives no scenarios (no toast, a debug
   * log). A chosen scenario whose file is gone stays chosen until the next choice.
   *
   * @returns The new view; onScenario listeners run when the list changed.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // gameView refreshes the list when the picker gets focus.
   * await ctx.require(workspacePlugin).refreshScenarios(); // { scenarios: ["empty", "full", "rich"], chosen: undefined }
   * ```
   */
  refreshScenarios(): Promise<ScenarioView>;

  /**
   * Listens to the scenario list and the choice. A throwing listener is logged and does not stop
   * the others.
   *
   * @param fn - Called with the new view after a change.
   * @returns Removes it.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // gameView's picker re-renders on a change made elsewhere.
   * const off = ctx.require(workspacePlugin).onScenario(view => setOptions(view.scenarios));
   * off();
   * ```
   */
  onScenario(fn: (view: ScenarioView) => void): () => void;
};
~~~

### 7.14 panels — tools, Standard

- depends: `[linkPlugin, workspacePlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onStart` (mount the active workspace, one palette item per panel, `link.onManifest` → recheck), `onStop` (unmount, unwatch).
- Mount states (`data-panel-state`): `missing`, `no-game`, `waiting`, `ready`, `error`. Stale marking (`data-stale`): `silent`, `lost`, `resync`.
- `definePanel` (root export) validates id `/^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*(\.[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*)*$/`, workspace, source refs, command ids, `view`, `compact`.
- `shared/` modules (not exported from the root; views import them by relative path): `style-edit.ts`, `highlight.ts`, `tokens.ts`, `scene/`, `editor-url.ts`, `side-panel/`, `icons.tsx` (the `Icon` component of the top bar and views), `workspaces.ts` (`WORKSPACE_IDS` in rail order, `WORKSPACE_LABELS`), `manifest-paths.ts`, `styles-file.ts`.
- `side-panel/` is the one SidePanel of every view's side panel (flowView Inspector, gameView, filesView): `SidePanel` (Preact; props `id`, `side: "start" | "end"`, `title`, `defaultWidth`, `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, `overlayBelow?`, `open?`, `onOpenChange?`), `useSidePanel(id)` → `{ closed, expanded, show, toggle }`, `sidePanelState(id)` → `{ width, collapsed, closed, overlay, drawer }`, `showSidePanel(id)`, `toggleSidePanel(id)` (views bind `\`). Resize by a 6 px handle (←/→ step 16 px, double-click resets), collapse to a 32 px rail, close and reopen (toolbar `reopen-<id>` button, palette "Show <title>"), overlay drawer below `overlayBelow` px of container width. Persisted per id in localStorage `moku-editor:panel:<id>` (`{ width, collapsed, closed }`).
- Events: emits `workspace:ran`; hooks `link:status`, `workspace:changed`.

~~~ts
/**
 * A panel source: an id, or an id with its input.
 */
export type SourceRef = string | readonly [id: string, input: Json];

/**
 * The values a panel view gets, typed from its source ids.
 */
export type PanelValues<S> = { readonly [K in keyof S]: SourceValue<RefId<S[K]>> };

/**
 * What a panel view gets next to its values. Each `run` call emits `workspace:ran` (origin panel).
 */
export type PanelTools<C> = {
  run: { readonly [K in keyof C]: (...input: CommandArgs<C[K]>) => Promise<RunResult> };
  /** Snapshot at this render; the view re-renders on change. */
  status: LinkStatus;
  /** link's remote channel, for ad hoc reads; its `run` is reported as `workspace:ran` (origin panel). */
  channel: EditorChannel;
  /** link.files (R4). */
  files: FilesClient;
  workspace: WorkspaceApi;
};

/**
 * The input of definePanel.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const input: PanelInput<{ position: "game.position" }, {}> = { id: "state", title: "State", workspace: "state", sources: { position: "game.position" }, view };
 * ```
 */
export type PanelInput<
  S extends Readonly<Record<string, SourceRef>>,
  C extends Readonly<Record<string, string>>
> = {
  /** /^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*(\.[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*)*$/, e.g. "flow.inspector". */
  readonly id: string;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly workspace: WorkspaceId;
  readonly sources: S;
  readonly commands?: C;
  readonly view: (values: PanelValues<S>, tools: PanelTools<C>) => PanelElement;
  readonly compact?: (values: PanelValues<S>, tools: CompactTools<C>) => PanelElement;
};

/**
 * The registered, closure-erased panel.
 */
export type PanelSpec = {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly workspace: WorkspaceId;
  readonly sources: Readonly<Record<string, SourceRef>>;
  readonly commands: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  readonly view: (
    values: Readonly<Record<string, Json>>,
    tools: PanelTools<Readonly<Record<string, string>>>
  ) => PanelElement;
  readonly compact:
    | ((
        values: Readonly<Record<string, Json>>,
        tools: CompactTools<Readonly<Record<string, string>>>
      ) => PanelElement)
    | undefined;
};

/**
 * Panels configuration: empty (contracts §5).
 */
export type PanelsConfig = Record<string, never>;

/**
 * Where a run made outside the top bar started.
 */
export type PanelRunOrigin = "panel" | "key" | "palette";

/**
 * The panels api (`app.panels`, `ctx.require(panelsPlugin)`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * // A view registers its panel at init, then runs commands from its handlers.
 * ctx.require(panelsPlugin).register(createFlowPanel(ctx));
 * await ctx.require(panelsPlugin).run("game.step", { frames: 1 });
 * ```
 */
export type PanelsApi = {
  /**
   * Registers a panel built with definePanel. After start, a panel of an already mounted
   * workspace is mounted at once and gets a palette item (group Panels).
   *
   * @param panel - The PanelSpec.
   * @throws {Error} `[moku-editor] Panel "<id>" is already registered.` for a duplicate id.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // flowView registers its panel when it starts.
   * ctx.require(panelsPlugin).register(createFlowPanel(ctx));
   * ```
   */
  register(panel: PanelSpec): void;

  /**
   * Runs a registry command outside any render (R9): link.run, then the global `workspace:ran`
   * with the origin. A rejection emits `workspace:ran` with `ok: false` and still rejects.
   *
   * @param id - Command id.
   * @param input - Command input.
   * @param origin - Where the run started; default "panel".
   * @returns The RunResult; rejects like link.run.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * await app.panels.run("game.step", { frames: 1 });
   * // { value: null, state: { path: "board/awaitIntent", frame: 1841, tainted: false } }
   * ```
   */
  run(id: string, input?: Json, origin?: PanelRunOrigin): Promise<RunResult>;

  /**
   * Every registered panel, in registration order.
   *
   * @returns A copy of the list.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // After flowView and stateView registered their panels.
   * app.panels.list().map(panel => panel.id); // ["flow", "state"]
   * ```
   */
  list(): readonly PanelSpec[];

  /**
   * Mounts every panel of a workspace into an element, one `<section data-panel>` each, in
   * registration order. Idempotent for the same element; another element moves the mount.
   *
   * @param ws - The workspace.
   * @param element - The element, usually `workspace.host(ws)`.
   * @returns The unmount function: removes every section and unwatches.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * const unmount = app.panels.mountInto("flow", app.workspace.host("flow"));
   * unmount(); // the sections are gone
   * ```
   */
  mountInto(ws: WorkspaceId, element: HTMLElement): () => void;
};
~~~

### 7.15 flowView — tools, VeryComplex

- depends: `[linkPlugin, workspacePlugin, panelsPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` (registers the Flow panel with commands `step`, `pause`, `resume`; palette; keys; Esc layers; takes `workspace.density()`), `onStart` (watches `game.graph`, `game.position` and `game.history { last: historyLast }` for the whole session, so the Nodes palette, other views' intents and history frames work before Flow is shown; the canvas renders when Flow is first shown), `onStop` (waits for a pending layout save ≤ 1000 ms, disposes ELK).
- Runs commands only through `panels.run`; never `link.run`.
- The Info tab is the one place for a node's neighbours (D-25; the neighbours strip is gone). A click on a *Comes from* or *Outcomes* row follows its edge (`focus.followEdge`): the other end is selected, the camera frames both ends, a 600 ms pulse plays on the reached node, Back (Alt+←) returns. The current node is never dimmed.
- Find current (key `c`, the toolbar button): the camera moves onto the current node with a pulse; a chevron points to it while it is out of view.
- Items holding the current node (round 2 R5): a collapsed sub-flow, slot or hub with the current node inside, an expanded frame around it, or a node on the position stack is never dimmed; it gets `data-holds-current` (the accent ring) and a "here" tag; the trail edge into it is drawn 2 px accent (`data-here`). When `locateCurrent()` finds the current node inside a collapsed parent (`inside` set), the parent holds it and is not itself current (round 2b R16).
- Keys: Enter follows the highlighted row or focuses the focused card, but skips when focus is on a `<button>` (a frame's Collapse works by Enter, round 2b R16).
- Density: ELK spacing follows `workspace:density` (comfortable 120 / 20, compact 96 / 14), edge labels take their own layer so they never overlap.
- A `workspace:select-node` that shows Flow for the first time is framed by the first canvas measure, not the current node.
- Notes are gone: no `notes` namespace, no `notesDir`, no `workspace:new-note`.
- The Inspector has two tabs, Info and Code (D-66). The Styles tab, the palette group "Styles" and the config key `styleSaveDelayMs` are gone: text styles are edited in their file or through the agent.
- Events: emits `workspace:open-file`; hooks `link:status`, `link:project`, `workspace:changed`, `workspace:select-node`, `workspace:focus-frame`, `workspace:density`.

~~~ts
/**
 * Where the layout is saved and how ELK runs (`flowView.layout`). Replaced as a whole: an override
 * gives every field.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({
 *   pluginConfigs: {
 *     flowView: { layout: { file: ".moku/editor/layout.json", worker: false, saveDelayMs: 400 } }
 *   }
 * }); // ELK runs inline, positions save to .moku/editor/layout.json
 * ```
 */
export type FlowLayoutConfig = {
  /** Saved positions. Default ".moku/editor/layout.json". */
  readonly file: string;
  /** Run ELK in a Web Worker; false = inline (tests, strict CSP). Default true. */
  readonly worker: boolean;
  /** Debounce before the layout file is written after a drop. Default 400. */
  readonly saveDelayMs: number;
};

/**
 * The zoom range of the camera (`flowView.zoom`). Replaced as a whole: an override gives every
 * field.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { flowView: { zoom: { min: 0.08, max: 2, defaultMin: 0.8 } } } });
 * // zoomTo(3) stops at 200 %
 * ```
 */
export type FlowZoomConfig = {
  /** Lowest zoom (design §4: 8 %). Default 0.08. */
  readonly min: number;
  /** Highest zoom (design §4: 300 %). Default 3. */
  readonly max: number;
  /** Floor of the default camera (M11). Default 0.8. */
  readonly defaultMin: number;
};

/**
 * The hub rule (`flowView.hub`, design §7.1): the rest node drawn as a hub with one lane per
 * outcome. Replaced as a whole: an override gives every field.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { flowView: { hub: { minOutcomes: 8, minReturns: 4 } } } });
 * // a rest node with 6 outcomes is laid out by ELK, not as a hub
 * ```
 */
export type FlowHubConfig = {
  /** A hub has at least this many outcomes. Default 6. */
  readonly minOutcomes: number;
  /** A hub has at least this many distinct returning nodes. Default 4. */
  readonly minReturns: number;
};

/**
 * flowView configuration (spec/11 §2.6): flat fields plus the one-level objects `layout`, `zoom`
 * and `hub`. The kernel merges shallowly, so an object given in `pluginConfigs` replaces the
 * default object as a whole.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { flowView: { historyLast: 40 } } });
 * // flowView watches the last 40 entries of game.history
 * ```
 */
export type FlowViewConfig = {
  /** Entries of game.history flowView watches. Default 20. */
  historyLast: number;
  /** Edges drawn as the trail, newest strongest. Default 6. */
  trailLength: number;
  /** Outcome names drawn as rejections. Default ["rejected"]. */
  rejectedOutcomes: readonly string[];
  /** The layout file and the ELK engine. */
  layout: FlowLayoutConfig;
  /** The zoom range of the camera. */
  zoom: FlowZoomConfig;
  /** The hub rule. */
  hub: FlowHubConfig;
};

/**
 * The flowView api (`app.flowView`), namespaced (spec/15 §2.5).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.flowView.focus.select("board/merge"); // true, the Inspector shows board/merge
 * app.flowView.camera.fitAll(); // the whole main frame in view
 * ```
 */
export type FlowViewApi = {
  /**
   * The camera: fit all, fit the selection, zoom, Follow the game.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.camera.zoomTo(1); // 100 %
   * ```
   */
  camera: CameraApi;

  /**
   * Focus: select a node, walk the graph, follow an edge, focus the edge of a frame, Step, the
   * history strip.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.focus.select("board/merge"); // true, the Inspector shows board/merge
   * ```
   */
  focus: FocusApi;

  /**
   * Sub-flows: expand and collapse in place, enter as the canvas root, go back up.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.flows.enter("main/board"); // breadcrumb main › board
   * ```
   */
  flows: FlowsApi;

  /**
   * Pinned positions: how many are pinned in the visible flows, and Reset layout.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // merge and toast were dragged on the board.
   * app.flowView.layout.pinnedCount(); // 2
   * ```
   */
  layout: LayoutApi;
};

/**
 * The camera namespace of the api (`app.flowView.camera`).
 */
export type CameraApi = {
  /**
   * The current camera: screen = world · z + (x, y). A copy.
   *
   * @returns The camera.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The zoom readout of the zoom bar.
   * Math.round(app.flowView.camera.get().z * 100); // 100
   * ```
   */
  get(): Camera;

  /**
   * Fits every item of the root frame (F / ⇧1), leaving room for the preview and the minimap;
   * animated over 420 ms. Does nothing before the first layout.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // After a long walk through the board, show the whole main frame again.
   * app.flowView.camera.fitAll(); // whole main frame in view
   * ```
   */
  fitAll(): void;

  /**
   * Fits the selection and its neighbours (⇧2); the current node when nothing is selected.
   * Animated over 420 ms.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.focus.select("board/merge");
   * app.flowView.camera.fitSelection(); // merge, awaitIntent and the stubs of merge in view
   * ```
   */
  fitSelection(): void;

  /**
   * Zooms by a factor around the viewport centre (+ / −: 1.25 / 0.8), animated over 200 ms.
   *
   * @param factor - The zoom factor; the result is clamped to 8 %–300 %.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.camera.zoomBy(1.25); // 100 % → 125 %
   * ```
   */
  zoomBy(factor: number): void;

  /**
   * Sets an absolute zoom around the viewport centre (key 0 → 1), animated over 200 ms.
   *
   * @param z - The zoom; clamped to 8 %–300 %.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.camera.zoomTo(1); // 100 %
   * ```
   */
  zoomTo(z: number): void;

  /**
   * Toggles or sets Follow the game (B5). Only this call and the toolbar toggle change it (M9).
   * Turning it on moves the camera to the current node over 500 ms.
   *
   * @param on - The new value; omitted = toggle.
   * @returns The new value.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.camera.follow(true); // true: the camera tracks game.position
   * ```
   */
  follow(on?: boolean): boolean;
};

/**
 * The focus namespace of the api (`app.flowView.focus`).
 */
export type FocusApi = {
  /**
   * Select = focus (design §4): the camera moves, the rest dims, the Inspector shows the item.
   * A bare NodeId resolves to its first visible instance; inside a collapsed sub-flow the parents
   * expand first. `undefined` leaves focus.
   *
   * @param key - An ItemKey, a NodeId, or undefined.
   * @returns False for an unknown key, else true.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.focus.select("board/merge"); // true, the Inspector shows board/merge
   * app.flowView.focus.select("board/nope"); // false, nothing selected
   * ```
   */
  select(key: ItemKey | NodeId | undefined): boolean;

  /**
   * The selected item key.
   *
   * @returns The key, or undefined when nothing is selected.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.focus.select("main/home");
   * app.flowView.focus.selected(); // "main/home"
   * ```
   */
  selected(): ItemKey | undefined;

  /**
   * Node id of the current position, from game.position.
   *
   * @returns The id, or undefined before the first position.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The game waits on the board.
   * app.flowView.focus.current(); // "board/awaitIntent"
   * ```
   */
  current(): NodeId | undefined;

  /**
   * Walks the graph from the shown node: "next" (→) follows the highlighted *Outcomes* row of the
   * Info tab (default: the row on the trail), "prev" (←) the highlighted *Comes from* row
   * (default: the first). A row with its edge on screen is followed like `followEdge`.
   *
   * @param direction - "prev" = ←, "next" = →.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.focus.select("board/merge");
   * app.flowView.focus.walk("next"); // focus moves to "board/awaitIntent", the "Outcomes" row
   * ```
   */
  walk(direction: "prev" | "next"): void;

  /**
   * Follows an edge from the shown node to its other end: the target of an *Outcomes* edge, the
   * source of a *Comes from* edge (an exit resolves through its frame's edge). Selects that
   * instance, marks the edge, frames both ends, plays a 600 ms pulse on the reached node and
   * keeps the previous selection for Back (Alt+←).
   *
   * @param edgeKey - An instance edge key, "main/board>board/merge:done".
   * @returns False when the edge or its other end is not on the canvas, else true.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.focus.select("board/merge");
   * app.flowView.focus.followEdge("main/board>board/merge:done"); // true: awaitIntent selected, both ends framed
   * ```
   */
  followEdge(edgeKey: string): boolean;

  /**
   * Focuses the edge taken at a frame and marks its history row (the `workspace:focus-frame` hook
   * calls it), then toasts "Frame N · path · outcome", or "No edge at frame N · last edge before
   * it …".
   *
   * @param frame - A game frame.
   * @returns False when the history carries no frames (until F-H1), else true.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.focus.focusFrame(1778); // true: selects edge board/merge:rejected and its row
   * ```
   */
  focusFrame(frame: number): boolean;

  /**
   * Runs game.step { frames: 1 } through panels.run (R9). Does nothing unless the game is paused
   * (M5); a failed run is logged and toasted, and resolves undefined.
   *
   * @returns The run result, or undefined when not paused or failed.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * await app.flowView.focus.step(); // { value, state: { path, frame, tainted } } or undefined
   * ```
   */
  step(): Promise<RunResult | undefined>;

  /**
   * Toggles or sets the history strip (H).
   *
   * @param open - The new value; omitted = toggle.
   * @returns Whether the strip is open.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.focus.history(true); // true: 288 px strip with 20 rows
   * ```
   */
  history(open?: boolean): boolean;
};

/**
 * The flows namespace of the api (`app.flowView.flows`).
 */
export type FlowsApi = {
  /**
   * Expands a sub-flow or slot item in place (design §7.5).
   *
   * @param key - The item key of a sub-flow or slot node.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.flows.expand("main/settings"); // the settingsPopup frame opens inside main
   * ```
   */
  expand(key: ItemKey): void;

  /**
   * Collapses an expanded sub-flow or slot item back to a card.
   *
   * @param key - The item key of the expanded node.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.flows.collapse("main/board"); // the board hub folds into one card
   * ```
   */
  collapse(key: ItemKey): void;

  /**
   * Enters a sub-flow node as its own canvas (double-click, "Enter <flow>").
   *
   * @param key - The item key of a sub-flow node.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.flows.enter("main/board"); // breadcrumb main › board
   * ```
   */
  enter(key: ItemKey): void;

  /**
   * Leaves entered flows up to a depth (0 = main). Breadcrumb segments call it (M1).
   *
   * @param depth - How many entered flows stay.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * app.flowView.flows.up(0); // back to main
   * ```
   */
  up(depth: number): void;
};

/**
 * The layout namespace of the api (`app.flowView.layout`).
 */
export type LayoutApi = {
  /**
   * Pinned node positions in the visible flows: Reset layout is disabled at 0 (M8).
   *
   * @returns The count.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // merge and toast were dragged on the board.
   * app.flowView.layout.pinnedCount(); // 2
   * ```
   */
  pinnedCount(): number;

  /**
   * Clears the pins of the visible flows, writes layout.json and toasts the file (M12).
   *
   * @returns Resolves when the file is written.
   * @throws {Error} When nothing is pinned or layout.json is not valid.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * await app.flowView.layout.reset(); // toast "Layout reset · 3 pinned nodes · .moku/editor/layout.json"
   * ```
   */
  reset(): Promise<void>;
};
~~~

### 7.16 gameView — tools, Complex

- depends: `[linkPlugin, workspacePlugin, panelsPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` (Game panel, palette, keys, Esc layers), `onStart` (scene watches when Game is already active), `onStop`.
- Game is the default workspace (⌘1). Watches `game.ui`, `game.entities`, `game.projections` only while Game is shown. Runs `editor.*` commands through `panels.run`. Never captures on its own.
- Calibration: reads `{ key }` of one keyed ui node from `game.locate` when the manifest lists it (game 0.4), else `game.rect` (game 0.1). A manifest with neither: no read, no warn, and the picker hint says "This game reports no element rects".
- Picker and area pick: the element picker (the toolbar's Select button, ⇧⌘C, I, `pick()`) is the one way to pick, in the Game workspace; Reference mode and its `data-moku-*` proxy layer are gone (D-65). Select (`button[data-part="pick"]`, U4) is an icon button: the `select` tool icon and the screen-reader label "Select element", title "Select element ⇧⌘C"; `aria-pressed` follows the picker, so it is lit from the click until the pick completes, Esc or a second click. The cursor over the picker layer is a crosshair. A click (`pointerup`) picks the element at the point. A press that moves 4 client px or more drags an area (U9, A16): the layer takes the pointer, a dashed `<div data-box="area">` follows, the release picks the area and turns the picker off (Esc cancels): the elements fully inside (else the ones covered by half of their own area), group roots only, top to bottom then left to right, at most 40; the card `<capturesDir>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/area-f<frame>.md` lists them under the head `@moku area <w>×<h> · <flow node> · <N> elements · ref x,y w×h · <card path>`, which goes to the clipboard; the crop is `area-f<frame>-crop.jpg`. Each element line is `- <name> <type> · key <key> · text "…" · <file:line> · x,y w×h px · ref x,y w×h` (U5; `text` when the game reports `content`, 40 characters at most), followed by its child tree (visible descendants, two spaces per level, 3 levels, 60 lines in the whole tree, then `+N more`); then one `layout: <roots> < <parent> (…) < …` line per parent chain (up to 3 parents), `partly in the area: <name> <type> x,y w×h px · …` (overlapping nodes not inside, largest overlap first, at most 8), the tail lines; the card adds `## <key> · component <Name> · <file:line>` for each component instance (within the 10 new source searches of an area, A18).
- Selection over MCP (U4, D-33): every change of the selection (a pick, an area, select, Esc) is published through `link.notify("selection", …)` (first without the style source, then again with it; after a pick with `card`, `crop`, `line`). `edits` carries the pending style edits of the element (`{ path, from, to }` each, absent without any, U8); a change of them publishes the selection again, so `moku_selection` answers the edits the Element tab shows. `link.handle("select", …)` answers MCP `moku_select`: `rect` picks an area; `key` (first ui node with it, `"hud/infoBar"` allowed) or `ref` is inspected in the Game workspace and, unless `card: false`, picked without the clipboard; an unknown key is -32602 "No element with key <key>".
- A pick (round 2 R2; a picker click): `game.bookmark` (kept in `bookmarks()`, newest first, 20 at most, id `<key>-f<frame>`), `editor.capture`, the crop (the element rect + 8 px, scaled by the shot's pixel ratio) and the full frame saved through `files.writeBinary` as `<day>/<key>-f<frame>-crop.jpg` and `<day>/f<frame>-full.jpg` (JPEG 0.8, D-34, A19; the extension follows the picture type), then the card file `<day>/<key>-f<frame>.md` (round 2b R13; `-2`, `-3` … when taken that day); `<day>` is `<capturesDir>/<yyyy-mm-dd>` (local date; old flat files are not moved), ONE line on the clipboard and the toast "Reference, shot and bookmark copied" (a missing step leaves its word and its lines out; MCP `moku_select` passes `copy: false`: no clipboard, no toast), then the capture card of the shot with a Reference action that copies the line again. A picker click completes a pick only while the workspace preference "Copy on select" is on (U5, D-70; `pickAt` asks `workspace.copyOnSelect()`): with it off the click only selects the element, opens the Element tab and publishes the selection without `card`, `crop` and `line`, with no `game.bookmark`, no `editor.capture`, no file, no capture card, no toast and no clipboard, and the release of an area drag picks nothing (the marquee goes, the picker stays on). "Copy reference" in the Element tab writes the card and copies its line on demand. The MCP pick does not ask the preference. Shot and Series copy `shot: <path>` and `series: <dir>/ (<n> frames)`.
- The reference line (round 2b R13): `@moku <name> <type> · <flow/node> · <file:line> · ref <x>,<y> <w>×<h> · <card path>`, e.g. `@moku settingsBoard panel · settingsPopup/open · features/settings/settings.tsx:290 · ref 65,641 950×1060 · .moku/captures/2026-10-05/settingsBoard-f212.md`. `<file:line>` is the index's answer for the key (`jsx:<key>`; a key built in a loop answers the line of the element that builds it, `card0` → `features/orders/strip.tsx:216`, D-47), or for an entity the line that defines its projection; a field that is not known is left out, and a card that could not be written leaves its path out (`gameView: reference card failed`).
- The card file, Markdown: `# @moku <name> <type>`; the full reference block in a `text` fence (a fence one backtick longer than any run inside); `## JSX · <file:line>` and `## Style · <name> · <file:line>` with fenced snippets (language from the extension); an entity: `## Spawned by <projection> · <file:line>` and `- <component>: <short value>` rows; then `![element](<key>-f<frame>-crop.jpg)` `![frame](f<frame>-full.jpg)`. "Copy reference" writes the card of the same node and frame again (one file), or a new one.
- The reference block, one fact per line, fixed order, unknown lines and fields left out: `@moku <name> · <type> · <flow/node> · f<frame>`, `path: <ui path> | entity #<id> (<components>)`, `source: <file:line> · style: <identifier> <file:line> · texture: <key>`, `layout: <parent (direction, padding t/r/b/l, margin, gap)> < … (3 at most)`, `bounds: <x>,<y> <w>×<h> px · ref <x>,<y> <w>×<h>`, `state: <visible|hidden>, <flags> · value "<text>" · alpha <a>`, `flow: <stack joined by " > "> · last: <from> → <outcome> (f<frame>)`, `game: <name> <version> · <session> · f<frame> · <HH:MM:SS> · <live|paused> · <clean|tainted>`, `device: <preset> <w>×<h> <orientation> · dpr <n> · safe <t>/<r>/<b>/<l>`, `restore: bookmark <id>`, `shot: <crop> · frame: <full>`. It sits in the card file; the Element tab does not show it (U3). The footer of the filled tab holds two ghost buttons: "Copy reference" (`data-action="copy-reference"`, `copyReference()`), which writes the card and copies the one line, and "Show in render tree"; there is no "Pick another". A key built in a loop (`card${slot}` for `card0`) answers the line of the element that builds it (`features/orders/strip.tsx:216`, D-47); a key the index does not know leaves `source` out.
- Device toolbar: the select is grouped by `<optgroup>` (an estimated preset says so in its option title, "… · approx: estimated values"); a foldable shows Fold / Unfold (`data-action="fold"`, `fold(inner?)`); the overlay-in-game switch moved to the top bar (round 2 R1). The Copy Ref switch (`data-part="copy-on-select"`, `role="switch"`, D-72) stands after Safe area and Sound: `aria-checked` is `workspace.copyOnSelect()`, a click calls `workspace.setCopyOnSelect(!on)`, the title is "On: a pick writes the reference and copies its line. Off: a pick only selects the element", and it follows `workspace.onPrefs` (the palette command moves it too); no key, never dimmed. The Sound switch (`data-part="sound"`, key M in Game, round 2b R11) runs `game.mute { muted }` through `panels.run` when the manifest lists it and keeps the flag with `workspace.setMuted`; a game that connects while muted is muted again (a hot reload connects a new page); without `game.mute` it is `aria-disabled` with the title "Needs @moku-labs/game with game.mute"; a refusal toasts "Sound switch failed · <message>".
- Stage (round 2b R9): Fit is one scale per device kind, the scale that fits the tallest preset of the kind with its bezel (phones include foldables; tablets and the desktop have their own), and the screen shown always fits; 100 % is 1 CSS px per px. The bezel (`data-frame` on `[data-part="bezel"]`) follows `DeviceSpec.frame`: `modern` 10 px all round with the island and home bar guides; `home-button` 64 px above and below, 10 px at the sides, a square screen (`--screen-radius: 0px`) and a 44 px round `[data-part="home-button"]` in the bottom bezel (the right one in landscape), no island and no home bar.
- Code section (round 2b R12, `data-part="code"` in the Element tab): a ui element's JSX (the range the index answers for its key, from the line that opens its tag to the one that closes it) and the `defineStyle` block of `style={ident}`, each with `file:line`, Open in Files and the shared highlighter, 20 lines then "Show all N lines"; an entity: "Spawned by <projection> · <file:line>" (the `name: "<key>"` line inside a `projection({…})` call) and its components with short values (48 characters). A text style key (`style="ui.link"`) and a style call get no style snippet.
- Capture card (round 2b R14, `[data-game="card"]`): grid `56px minmax(0, 1fr) auto`; the thumbnail, one line each for the title ("✓ Screenshot saved", "✓ 20 shots saved"), the path cut in the middle (36 characters; the whole path in `title`) and `f<frame> · <device>`, then Copy link (`shot: <path>` / `series: <dir>/ (<n> frames)`), Open (Files, or the contact sheet of a series) and, after a pick, Reference; × closes. At most 360 px wide and 120 px tall; at 480 px of window it takes the width less 24. A screenshot, a pick and a series each show it; it hides after `captureCardMs` unless hovered or focused, and it is an Esc layer above the picker. A series ends like a screenshot (D-69): the recording popover closes, the card shows its first shot, `series: <folder> (<n> frames)` is on the clipboard and the toast says "✓ N shots saved"; the contact sheet opens only on request: `openSheet(indexPath)`, the `workspace:open-sheet` hook (Files) or Open on the series card.
- Styles fields and pending edits (U8, D-67; `section[data-part="style"]` in the Element tab): every entry of the element's scene style is a row of fields: a number is `<input type="number" step="1">`, a string `<input type="text">`, a boolean a checkbox, a record of those three (padding) one field per leaf with the path `<key>.<leaf>`; anything else is read-only text. A number or text field commits on Enter or on blur, a select and a checkbox on `change`, through `editStyle(path, to)`; Esc restores the shown value and commits nothing; an empty or non-numeric number field commits nothing. A row with a pending edit carries `data-edited` and shows the edited value, the scene value struck before it (`<s>556</s>`) and a reset button (`×`, `data-action="reset-edit"`). While any element has an edit, the edits bar `div[data-part="edits"]` shows "N edits · M elements" (the elements only above one), "Copy for agent" (`data-action="copy-edits"`, `copyEdits()`) and "Clear" (`clearEdits("all")`). The game does not change: no file is written and no command is sent; the edit is kept per element (the ui key, else the node id) and not persisted across a page load. An edit resolves by itself: on every new scene snapshot an edit whose scene value equals `to` is dropped (the agent wrote the code and hot reload brought it in). A new game session drops the entries kept by node id. The agent text (`editsText` in `element/edits.ts`): one block per element, the selected one first, then one block per text style key, blocks separated by one empty line; the head is `@moku <label>` plus ` · <path>:<line>` when the index answered the key (`@moku homePlay · features/stage/views/home-screen.tsx:199`), then one line per edit (`minWidth: 556 -> 600`, `padding.top: 25 -> 30`); strings in double quotes, numbers and booleans bare. The selected element's edits also go out as `SelectionInfo.edits`.
- Text style section (D-73; `section[data-part="text-style"]` inside the Styles section, above the edits bar): the engine sends the text style key a `text` was given (`UiNode.textStyle`, `@moku-labs/game` 0.14.11) and the scene keeps it as `SceneNode.textStyle` (a non-empty string; anything else is dropped; absent on an older engine, which shows no section). The block of the key is read through the project index (`find("textStyle:<key>")`, `findFresh`) and parsed with `parseStyleFile` / `findBlock` (kind `text`) of `panels/shared/style-edit`; `state.textStyle` holds it (`TextStyleCard`: `searching`, `missing`, or `found` with `path`, `line`, `version` and `rows`). The section is titled "Text style · <key>", shows `<path>:<line>` with "Open in Files" and one row per field of the block: a number literal and a quoted string are fields like the Styles rows (the same component: Enter or blur commits, Esc restores, `data-edited`, the file value struck, a reset); any other value (an identifier, a token such as `colors.cream`, a boolean, a call) is read-only text. A string is always a text field here: the enum table is the one of an element's style. A key the index does not know shows `Not in the project index: textStyle:<key>` (or why the index is off) and no fields. An edit is a pending edit of the style key, not of the node: the entry of `state.edits` has the map key `textStyle:<key>`, `label` `textStyle <key>`, `source` the path and line of the block, `byId: false`, and `from` is the value in the file; every text node with the key shows the same edits. It resolves when the block read again has the `to` value; a field that is no number or quoted string any more in a block that was read drops its edit, another value in the file becomes the `from` of the edit, a block that cannot be read keeps the edits, and the selection is published again when an edit changed or left. The block is read on selection and on a `link:project` delta that touches its file (also for a key with pending edits while another element is selected). The agent text gets one block per style key after the element blocks (`@moku textStyle ui.button · shared/styles/text.ts:88`, then `size: 105 -> 96`). `SelectionInfo.edits` of a selected text node also carries the edits of its key with the path `textStyle:<key>#<field>` (`textStyle:ui.button#size`, `textStyle:ui.button#shadow.dy`; the `#` ends the key, a key and a field both have dots); the edits bar counts them like any other edit; `clearEdits("selected")` on a text node drops its own edits and the ones of its key. The "Style · <key>" line of an empty scene style and the Code section's text style snippet use `SceneNode.textStyle` when the JSX lookup of the node gave no text style (a key built in code). Log (warn): `gameView: text style failed`.
- The Element panel is a `SidePanel` (panels/shared/side-panel). Notes and the attach api are gone (no `attach`, `notes`, `notesDir`, `workspace:new-note`).
- Events: emits `workspace:reveal`, `workspace:open-file`; hooks `link:status`, `link:project`, `workspace:changed`, `workspace:open-sheet`, `workspace:inspect`.

~~~ts
/**
 * gameView configuration. Where the game's code and asset manifest live is the project index's
 * answer (D-38), not configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { gameView: { captureCardMs: 5000 } } });
 * ```
 */
export type GameViewConfig = {
  /** Folder of screenshots and series, relative to the files root; each in a `<yyyy-mm-dd>/` day folder. */
  capturesDir: string;
  /** The capture card hides after this unless hovered or focused. */
  captureCardMs: number;
  /** Duration chips of the series popover (the longest equals capture's maxDurationMs). */
  seriesDurationsMs: readonly number[];
  /** Interval chips of the series popover (the shortest equals capture's minIntervalMs). */
  seriesIntervalsMs: readonly number[];
  /** Above this many planned shots the popover warns. */
  seriesWarnShots: number;
};

/**
 * A saved screenshot.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const shot: CaptureFile = { path: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/0846-board.jpg", frame: 1841, device: "iPhone 15 portrait", image: "data:image/jpeg;base64,…" };
 * ```
 */
export type CaptureFile = {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly frame: number;
  /** "iPhone 15 portrait". */
  readonly device: string;
  readonly image: string;
};

/**
 * A written series.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const result: SeriesResult = { folder: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/series-1015/", indexPath: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/series-1015/index.json", shots: 20 };
 * ```
 */
export type SeriesResult = {
  readonly folder: string;
  readonly indexPath: string;
  readonly shots: number;
};

/**
 * The gameView api (`app.gameView`, `ctx.require(gameViewPlugin)`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const shot = await app.gameView.capture(); // { path: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/0846-board.jpg", … }
 * ```
 */
export type GameViewApi = {
  /**
   * Turns the element picker on or off; without an argument it toggles. On shows the Game
   * workspace, the Element tab and the hint pill; off clears the hover box. What a click on an
   * element does next is the workspace preference "Copy on select" (the Copy Ref switch of the
   * game toolbar, on by default).
   *
   * On: the click bookmarks the game, saves the crop (`<key>-f<frame>-crop.jpg`) and the full
   * frame (`f<frame>-full.jpg`) in today's folder `<capturesDir>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/`, writes the
   * reference card next to them, puts its one reference line on the clipboard, shows the capture
   * card with a Reference action and publishes the selection with its `card`, `crop` and `line`
   * for MCP `moku_selection`. A drag of 4 px or more picks an area instead (`area-f<frame>.md`).
   *
   * Off: the click only selects the element for the Element tab and publishes the selection
   * without `card`, `crop` and `line`. Nothing is bookmarked, captured, written or copied, and a
   * drag picks nothing. `copyReference` writes the card and copies its line on demand.
   *
   * @param on - true for on, false for off, omitted to toggle.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The developer wants a reference of an element of the running game for the chat.
   * app.gameView.pick(true); // app.workspace.active() === "game", picker on
   * // After a click on the coin pill: the card is written and its line is on the clipboard.
   *
   * // The developer only wants to look at elements in the Element tab.
   * app.workspace.setCopyOnSelect(false);
   * app.gameView.pick(true);
   * // After a click on the coin pill: app.gameView.selected() names it, no file is written.
   * ```
   */
  pick(on?: boolean): void;

  /**
   * The picked element.
   *
   * @returns The element ref, undefined when nothing is selected.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // After a click on the coin pill in the game.
   * app.gameView.selected(); // { kind: "ui", path: "boardScreen/hudRow/coinPill" }
   * ```
   */
  selected(): ElementRef | undefined;

  /**
   * Selects an element without the picker, or clears the selection. Clears the style card and
   * publishes the selection to the hub (MCP `moku_selection`; null when cleared).
   *
   * @param ref - The element, undefined to clear.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // A test selects the first board item by its entity id.
   * app.gameView.select({ kind: "entity", id: 1_048_628 });
   * app.gameView.selected(); // { kind: "entity", id: 1048628 }
   * ```
   */
  select(ref: ElementRef | undefined): void;

  /**
   * Selects an element, opens the Element tab and shows the Game workspace. The
   * `workspace:inspect` hook calls it (renderView's "Inspect in Game", R9).
   *
   * @param ref - The element.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The palette jumps from a render-tree row to the Game workspace.
   * app.gameView.inspect({ kind: "ui", path: "boardScreen/boardSlot" }); // Game shown, Element tab filled
   * ```
   */
  inspect(ref: ElementRef): void;

  /**
   * The scene built with the shared `buildScene` from the watched `game.ui`, `game.entities`
   * and `game.projections` (watched while Game is shown, R6); a calibration in flight is waited
   * for, so the rects are the calibrated ones. While Game is hidden it reads the three once.
   * Rejects with the link's WireError when no game is connected.
   *
   * @returns The scene snapshot.
   * @throws {Error} The link's WireError, or `[moku-editor] game.ui has the wrong shape …`.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // merge-game on the inert renderer: one reference unit is one page px.
   * const scene = await app.gameView.scene();
   * scene.nodes.get("ui:boardScreen/boardSlot")?.rect; // { x: 55, y: 801, w: 970, h: 970 }
   * ```
   */
  scene(): Promise<SceneSnapshot>;

  /**
   * The page rect of one element, from `scene()`.
   *
   * @param ref - The element.
   * @returns Its rect in page CSS px, undefined when it is unknown or could not be placed.
   * @throws {Error} What `scene()` throws: the link's WireError, or a wrong game.ui shape.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The first board item of merge-game at board/awaitIntent.
   * await app.gameView.locate({ kind: "entity", id: 1_048_628 }); // { x: 428.5, y: 880.5, w: 223, h: 223 }
   * ```
   */
  locate(ref: ElementRef): Promise<PageRect | undefined>;

  /**
   * Draws the pink box (`--pick-tree`) around an element over the game frame, wherever the frame
   * is docked (stage or pinned preview); undefined clears it. A newer call drops an older one
   * still waiting for the scene.
   *
   * @param ref - The element, undefined to clear.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // renderView hovers a row of its tree.
   * app.gameView.highlight({ kind: "ui", path: "boardScreen/hudRow/coinPill" }); // pink ring over the game
   * app.gameView.highlight(undefined); // ring gone
   * ```
   */
  highlight(ref: ElementRef | undefined): void;

  /**
   * The game's texture catalogue: the manifest the project index names (`ProjectState.manifest`)
   * parsed with the shared `parseTextureManifest`. Cached until the session or the index names
   * another manifest, or the manifest changes on disk.
   *
   * @returns The catalogue, undefined when the index is off, names no manifest, or it does not parse.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The Element tab shows the GPU size of a picked sprite's texture.
   * (await app.gameView.manifest())?.textures.get("board.cell")?.gpuMb; // 4
   * ```
   */
  manifest(): Promise<TextureCatalogue | undefined>;

  /**
   * One screenshot: runs `editor.capture` through panels (R9), writes the picture into today's
   * folder `<capturesDir>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/` as `<hhmm>-<flow>` with the extension of its type
   * (`.jpg` for the JPEG editor.capture answers by default, D-34), puts `shot: <path>` on the
   * clipboard, toasts, shows the capture card and the shutter flash. Never captures on its own:
   * only a user action or this call does.
   *
   * @returns The saved capture, undefined when no game is connected, the game lacks
   * `editor.capture`, or the capture failed (a toast says which).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The developer saw a glitch on the board and keeps a picture of it.
   * await app.gameView.capture(); // { path: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/0846-board.jpg", frame: 1841, device: "iPhone 15 portrait", image: "data:image/jpeg;base64,…" }
   * ```
   */
  capture(): Promise<CaptureFile | undefined>;

  /**
   * Records a series with one `editor.series` call (R1, R9): numbered PNGs and `index.json` in a
   * new `<capturesDir>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/series-<hhmm>/` folder, puts `series: <folder> (<n> frames)`
   * on the clipboard, toasts and shows the capture card of its first shot, like a screenshot
   * (D-69). The contact sheet opens only on request (`openSheet`). Shows Game first. Refuses
   * while another series runs.
   *
   * @param options - Length and spacing in ms, and an optional label (default: the flow path).
   * @param options.durationMs - Length of the series.
   * @param options.intervalMs - Time between two shots.
   * @param options.label - Label of the sheet and the index.
   * @returns The folder, its index.json and the number of shots written; undefined when refused
   * or failed.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Watch the merge animation frame by frame.
   * await app.gameView.series({ durationMs: 2000, intervalMs: 100 }); // { folder: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/series-1015/", indexPath: ".moku/captures/2026-10-05/series-1015/index.json", shots: 20 }
   * ```
   */
  series(options: {
    durationMs: number;
    intervalMs: number;
    label?: string;
  }): Promise<SeriesResult | undefined>;

  /**
   * Stops the running series early: runs `editor.seriesStop` through panels (R2, R9). The
   * pending series then resolves with the shots taken so far; its index gets `stoppedEarly`.
   *
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The interesting moment is over long before the 20 s series ends.
   * const recording = app.gameView.series({ durationMs: 20_000, intervalMs: 100 });
   * app.gameView.stopSeries(); // the pending series resolves with the shots taken so far
   * ```
   */
  stopSeries(): void;

  /**
   * Opens a saved series' contact sheet: reads its index.json and every PNG. Shows Game. The
   * `workspace:open-sheet` hook calls it (filesView "Open contact sheet"), and so does "Open" on
   * the capture card of a series.
   *
   * @param indexPath - Path of the series' index.json.
   * @returns Resolves when the sheet is open (or a toast said why not).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // filesView's "Open contact sheet" on a series folder.
   * await app.gameView.openSheet(".moku/captures/2026-10-05/series-1015/index.json");
   * ```
   */
  openSheet(indexPath: string): Promise<void>;

  /**
   * Writes the reference card of the selected element and puts its one line on the clipboard
   * (round 2b R13): `@moku <name> <type> · <flow/node> · <file:line> · ref x,y w×h · <card path>`.
   * The card `<key>-f<frame>.md`, beside the pick's pictures in `<capturesDir>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/`,
   * holds the full reference block (`@moku` head, `path`, `source`, `layout`, `bounds`, `state`,
   * `flow`, `game`, `device`, and after a pick `restore` and `shot`), the JSX and style snippets with their `file:line`, and the links to
   * the pick's crop and full frame. The same node and frame write the same card again. A field
   * that is not known is left out; a card that cannot be written leaves its path out. A clipboard
   * that refuses is toasted; the line is returned all the same.
   *
   * @returns The line, undefined when nothing is selected or the selection is not in the scene.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The developer picked the settings board and asks Claude to move it.
   * app.gameView.select({ kind: "ui", path: "settingsScreen/settingsBoard" });
   * await app.gameView.copyReference();
   * // "@moku settingsBoard panel · settingsPopup/open · features/settings/settings.tsx:290 · ref 65,190 950×1060 · .moku/captures/2026-10-05/settingsBoard-f25.md"
   * ```
   */
  copyReference(): Promise<string | undefined>;

  /**
   * Folds or unfolds a foldable preset (its `fold` screens): the frame switches between the cover
   * and the inner screen live, the game sees a resize and the picker calibrates again. Without an
   * argument it toggles. Does nothing for a preset without `fold`.
   *
   * @param inner - true for the inner (unfolded) screen, false for the cover; omitted toggles.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // Check the board on the open Galaxy Z Fold 6.
   * app.workspace.setDevice({ preset: "galaxy-z-fold-6" });
   * app.gameView.fold(true); // app.workspace.device().preset.w === 707
   * ```
   */
  fold(inner?: boolean): void;

  /**
   * The bookmarks of the completed picks, newest first, at most 20. `game.restore` takes a
   * `value` back to the state of its pick.
   *
   * @returns A copy of the list.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The block said "restore: bookmark settingsBoard-f1841": go back there.
   * const bookmark = app.gameView.bookmarks().find(entry => entry.id === "settingsBoard-f1841");
   * if (bookmark) await app.panels.run("game.restore", { bookmark: bookmark.value });
   * ```
   */
  bookmarks(): readonly PickBookmark[];

  /**
   * Records a pending style edit of the selected element (U8, D-67). `from` is the value the
   * scene has for `path` now. A second edit of the same path replaces `to` and keeps the first
   * `from`. A `to` equal to the scene value removes the edit of that path. Nothing is written to
   * a file and no command is sent: the edit goes to the agent (`copyEdits`, and `edits` of the
   * published selection). Does nothing without a selected element in the scene, or for a path
   * the element's style does not have as a number, a string or a boolean.
   *
   * @param path - The style property, dotted for a nested one (`padding.top`).
   * @param to - The wanted value.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // homePlay is 556 wide in the game; the person wants 600 and more room on top.
   * app.gameView.select({ kind: "ui", path: "homeScreen/homePlay" });
   * app.gameView.editStyle("minWidth", 600);
   * app.gameView.editStyle("padding.top", 30);
   * app.gameView.edits()[0]?.edits;
   * // [{ path: "minWidth", from: 556, to: 600 }, { path: "padding.top", from: 25, to: 30 }]
   * app.gameView.editStyle("minWidth", 556); // back to the scene value: that edit is gone
   * ```
   */
  editStyle(path: string, to: StyleValue): void;

  /**
   * Drops pending style edits: the ones of the selected element, or all of them. The edits of a
   * selected text node are its own and the ones of its text style key (D-73). The selection is
   * published again without them.
   *
   * @param scope - `"selected"` for the selected element only; `"all"` (the default) for every element.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The person changed their mind about homePlay; the edits of the other elements stay.
   * app.gameView.clearEdits("selected");
   * app.gameView.edits().some(entry => entry.label === "homePlay"); // false
   * app.gameView.clearEdits(); // every pending edit is gone
   * ```
   */
  clearEdits(scope?: "selected" | "all"): void;

  /**
   * Every pending style edit, one entry per element, the selected element first, then one entry
   * per text style key (label `textStyle <key>`, D-73). An edit leaves by itself when a scene
   * snapshot shows its `to` value: the agent wrote the code and hot reload brought it in. The
   * edit of a text style key leaves when its block, read again, has the `to` value. A game
   * reload drops the entries of elements without a ui key.
   *
   * @returns A copy of the list.
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // The edits bar of the Element tab counts them: "2 edits".
   * const count = app.gameView.edits().reduce((sum, entry) => sum + entry.edits.length, 0);
   * app.gameView.edits()[0];
   * // { label: "homePlay", source: { path: "features/stage/views/home-screen.tsx", line: 199 }, byId: false, edits: [ … ] }
   * // After the size of the text style key ui.button was changed in the Element tab:
   * app.gameView.edits().at(-1);
   * // { label: "textStyle ui.button", source: { path: "shared/styles/text.ts", line: 88 }, byId: false, edits: [{ path: "size", from: 105, to: 96 }] }
   * ```
   */
  edits(): readonly ElementEdits[];

  /**
   * Puts the pending edits on the clipboard as text for the agent, toast "✓ 2 edits copied": one
   * block per element, the selected one first, then one block per text style key (D-73), blocks
   * separated by one empty line. The head is `@moku <label>` plus ` · <path>:<line>` when the
   * source is known; then one line per edit. Strings are written in double quotes, numbers and
   * booleans bare.
   *
   * @returns The text; undefined without edits, or when the clipboard refused (toasted).
   * @example
   * ```ts
   * // "Copy for agent" in the Element tab, after the two edits of homePlay.
   * await app.gameView.copyEdits();
   * // "@moku homePlay · features/stage/views/home-screen.tsx:199\nminWidth: 556 -> 600\npadding.top: 25 -> 30"
   * // With the size of the text style key ui.button changed too, its block comes last:
   * // "@moku homePlay · …:199\nminWidth: 556 -> 600\npadding.top: 25 -> 30\n\n@moku textStyle ui.button · shared/styles/text.ts:88\nsize: 105 -> 96"
   * ```
   */
  copyEdits(): Promise<string | undefined>;
};

/**
 * The bookmark a completed pick took (`game.bookmark`), kept in gameView state, newest first, at
 * most 20. `value` is what `game.restore { bookmark }` takes back.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const bookmark: PickBookmark = { id: "settingsBoard-f1841", frame: 1841, key: "settingsBoard", at: 1_790_000_000_000, value: { path: "settingsPopup/open" } };
 * ```
 */
export type PickBookmark = {
  /** `<key>-f<frame>`, with `-2`, `-3` … when taken; the `restore:` line prints it. */
  readonly id: string;
  /** The frame of the rest point the bookmark holds. */
  readonly frame: number;
  /** The ui key of the picked element, else its name. */
  readonly key: string;
  /** Date.now() when it was taken. */
  readonly at: number;
  readonly value: Json;
};

/**
 * The pending style edits of one element (U8, D-67): values the person changed in the Styles
 * fields of the Element tab and the source file does not have yet. They go to the agent as text
 * (`copyEdits`) and in the published selection (`SelectionInfo.edits`); the editor writes no code
 * for them. The pending edits of a text style key (D-73) are an entry of the same shape: the key
 * styles many text nodes, so the edit belongs to the key, not to a node.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const homePlay: ElementEdits = {
 *   label: "homePlay",
 *   source: { path: "features/stage/views/home-screen.tsx", line: 199 },
 *   byId: false,
 *   edits: [{ path: "minWidth", from: 556, to: 600 }, { path: "padding.top", from: 25, to: 30 }]
 * };
 * const button: ElementEdits = {
 *   label: "textStyle ui.button",
 *   source: { path: "shared/styles/text.ts", line: 88 },
 *   byId: false,
 *   edits: [{ path: "size", from: 105, to: 96 }]
 * };
 * ```
 */
export type ElementEdits = {
  /**
   * The head of the block in the agent text: the ui key, else the node name; `textStyle <key>`
   * for a text style key.
   */
  readonly label: string;
  /**
   * Where the index says the element is written, or where the block of the text style key is;
   * absent without an answer.
   */
  readonly source?: { readonly path: string; readonly line: number };
  /** True when the map key is a node id: such an entry does not survive a game reload. */
  readonly byId: boolean;
  /** The edits, in the order the person made them; one per path. */
  readonly edits: readonly StyleEdit[];
};
~~~

### 7.17 renderView — tools, Complex

- depends: `[linkPlugin, workspacePlugin, panelsPlugin]`. Lifecycle: `onInit` (Render panel), `onStart` (session watches `game.render`, `game.assets`, and `game.effects` while the manifest lists it as available), `onStop` (drops them, the device watches and the overlay root).
- Tiles: FPS (sparkline; "Resting at 30 fps …" while the game rests at its idle rate, D-28), frame time, draw calls ("Not counted in a production build" without the dev counter), texture memory, Scene (entities, display objects, pooled, and the effects line), and JS heap only where the page heartbeat reports `heap` (Chromium, `link.heap()`).
- Effects line: the `game.effects` counts (game 0.0.3); "Particles and filters are not reported (follow-up F-R1)" on an older game; "Effects not installed in this game" when the manifest lists `game.effects` with `available: false` (a game without `effectsPlugin`; `snapshot().tiles.effectsInstalled === false`, no watch is sent, nothing is logged).
- Calibration: `{ key }` of the first keyed ui element from `game.locate` when the manifest lists it (game 0.4), else `game.rect` (game 0.1); neither listed: no read, no warn, an uncalibrated scene.
- Device strip (spec 09 D1): a session whose manifest lists `editor.perf.second` (a phone's device session, or the game page whose agent has perf: a browser session) gets the strip above the tiles: the device row, the headline, More, the frame graph (its own window from `editor.perf.window`, painted by `perf/graph` at most every 250 ms), the spike counts, REC (`editor.recorder`), the spike record side panel (`editor.perf.spike { frame }` on demand; `stepSpike(dir)`, `openSpike(frame)`, `closeSpike()`), STALE when the phone's engine differs from `link.engine()`. Watches only while Render is shown. A device session reads no scene tree (`game.ui`, `game.entities`, `game.projections`): it costs the phone frames. Every value is checked down to each member read (`device/guards.ts`); a bad value is warned and dropped.
- Events: emits `workspace:inspect`; hooks `workspace:changed`, `link:status`, `link:project`, `workspace:reveal`. Logs: `renderView: unexpected source shape` (warn), `renderView: calibration failed` (warn).

~~~ts
export type { DeviceStripState, DeviceStripView, RecordState } from "./device/types";

/**
 * renderView configuration.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * createApp({ pluginConfigs: { renderView: { fpsSamples: 120 } } });
 * ```
 */
export type RenderViewConfig = {
  /** FPS samples kept for the sparkline (one per changed game.render value). */
  fpsSamples: number;
  /** Release log entries kept, newest first. */
  releaseLogMax: number;
};

/**
 * game.effects as renderView reads it (mirrors the game's EffectsStats, game 0.0.3).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const effects: EffectsStats = { particles: 18, emitters: 1, filters: 24, renderPasses: 49 };
 * ```
 */
export type EffectsStats = {
  /** Live particles over every instance and orphan. */
  particles: number;
  /** Running emitter instances plus the orphans still flying. */
  emitters: number;
  /** Filter instances over every view. */
  filters: number;
  /** Render passes of the frame. */
  renderPasses: number;
};

/**
 * Sort key of the textures table.
 */
export type TextureSortKey = "key" | "bundle" | "size" | "gpuMb" | "fileMb" | "use";

/**
 * The six metric tiles.
 */
export type MetricTiles = {
  fps: { now: number; samples: readonly number[]; low: number } | undefined;
  frameMs: number | undefined;
  /** The counter, or absent in a production build; renderPasses only when game.render reports it. */
  drawCalls:
    | (({ kind: "value"; value: number } | { kind: "absent" }) & { renderPasses?: number })
    | undefined;
  textures:
    | {
        gpuMb: number;
        count: number;
        bundles: number;
        budgetMb: number;
        unused: number;
        unusedMb: number;
      }
    | undefined;
  /** effects only when game.effects delivered (game 0.0.3). */
  scene: { entities: number; views: number; pooled: number; effects?: EffectsStats } | undefined;
  /**
   * Present, and false, only when the game has no effects plugin: the manifest lists game.effects
   * with `available: false` and the Scene tile reads "Effects not installed in this game".
   */
  effectsInstalled?: false;
  /** The page heap from its heartbeat (Chromium `performance.memory`); absent elsewhere. */
  heap: { kind: "value"; usedMb: number; limitMb: number } | { kind: "absent" };
};

/**
 * The derived view data (copies, never the live maps).
 */
export type RenderSnapshot = {
  frame: number | undefined;
  tiles: MetricTiles;
  tree: readonly TreeRow[];
  /** The rows of the table: loaded bundles, the bundle filter applied, sorted. */
  textures: readonly TextureRow[];
  bundles: readonly BundleRow[];
  pools: { views: number; pooled: number } | undefined;
  releases: readonly ReleaseEntry[];
};

/**
 * The renderView api (`app.renderView`, `ctx.require(renderViewPlugin)`).
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * app.workspace.show("render");
 * app.renderView.snapshot().tiles.heap; // { kind: "value", usedMb: 12.8, limitMb: 4095.8 } in Chromium
 * ```
 */
export type RenderViewApi = {
  /**
   * Re-reads the asset manifest and the calibration from game.locate or game.rect (the Textures
   * card's Refresh and a device change). Live values come from the watches: this is not a poll.
   * Does nothing while the link is not live or paused.
   *
   * @returns Resolves when both reads settled (never rejects).
   * @example
   * ```ts
